designs.angle: MEASUREMENT-FIRST / MINIMAL CUSTOM CODE: stock llama.cpp b11398 binaries (Windows prebuilt for speed numbers, Docker Linux build for the tracer) + thin Python harnesses; exactly one small C++ tool (pigemma-tracer, a cb_eval recorder) because the stock llama-eval-callback/llama-debug print only 3 elements per dimension and never run token generation. Optimised for producing honest measured numbers today and for byte-exact reproducibility (pinned commit a7b94df, JSON results with host/model fingerprints).
designs.overview:
Repository REPO_ROOT becomes a Python package `pigemma` (CLI: `python -m pigemma <cmd>`) plus one C++ tool, Pi shell scripts, docs and tests.

DESKTOP TODAY (E1-E7): (1) `pigemma bench threads` drives third_party/llama.cpp-win/llama-bench.exe (-o json) over thread counts for both GGUFs; (2) `pigemma bench gen` spawns llama-server.exe with/without `-md <mtp|dflash draft>` (and `--spec-type ngram-simple`), fires a fixed prompt set at temperature 0 and records the server's `timings` JSON (tok/s, draft_n, draft_n_accepted), peak WorkingSet/PrivateBytes via psutil and load time; (3) `pigemma quality` runs llama-perplexity.exe (PPL, optional KLD base gated on free disk) and a 24-item EN/HE/arith Q&A set through the server, stripping Gemma's `<|channel>thought...<channel|>` block before scoring; (4) `pigemma-tracer` (C++, built in Docker against third_party/llama.cpp via add_subdirectory) runs prompt+greedy generation with a cb_eval that records, per token and layer, the top-8 expert ids (+weights, optional full probs) of the 26B-A4B into a fixed-record binary trace, and, in a second mode, captures `ffn_norm`/`ffn_gate_par`/`ffn_out` activations of sampled layers of the 31B; (5) `pigemma sim` replays traces through LRU/LFU/static-hot/hybrid/Belady expert caches at the byte budgets of four Pi configurations, with an optional prev-token prefetch model, and projects tok/s = 1/(resident_bytes/ram_bw + miss_bytes/storage_bw + n_miss*latency), keeping measured/projected/assumed numbers in separate JSON fields; (6) `pc/proxy_cache_limit.sh` validates the cache model against reality by running llama-completion in Docker with `--memory=X` so the mmap'd model is evicted and re-read through the bind mount (a measured slow tier); (7) `pigemma h2` dequantises sampled 31B FFN matrices (gguf-py), builds W_base (Q2_K requant or low-rank r) + residual column groups, precomputes ||R_g||_2, and measures oracle residual-byte fraction at error thresholds, bound-certified skip fraction, and implied Pi bytes/token.

PI RUNTIME (E8, ready for the unknown Pi): parametric feasibility verdict (RAM/storage type/speed/free space/page size/busy-ness) in stdlib-only Python with a bash fact collector, OS tuning (dry-run by default), native llama.cpp build at the pinned commit, IO+memory bandwidth bench, quant/model selection table, run/bench wrappers, and a hot-set pinning daemon that mlocks non-expert tensor byte ranges + top-K hottest experts (ranges from the GGUF header, ranking from the desktop trace) so the page cache keeps them resident while cold experts stream.

HONESTY FRAME baked into docs/report: the MoE all-in-RAM on a Pi 5 is ~2.4 GB of weight reads per token (1.57 GB non-expert incl. the 0.6 GB tied LM head + 0.80 GB of experts) → roughly 3 tok/s at ~7.5 GB/s effective bandwidth; the dense 31B reads ~17.6 GB/token (attention+head alone 5.9 GB) → H2 is a measurement of a thesis, not a path to "good speed" on an 8 GB Pi.

components.language: Python (stdlib only, runs on the Pi's Python 3.13)
components.purpose: Minimal GGUF v3 header reader: metadata KV (all 13 value types incl. arrays), tensor infos (name, ndims, ne[], ggml type, offset), alignment (general.alignment, default 32), data_offset = align_up(end_of_header, alignment), per-tensor n_bytes computed from a built-in table {type: (block_size, type_size)} covering F32, F16, BF16, Q4_0(32,18), Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0(32,34), Q2_K(256,84), Q3_K(256,110), Q4_K(256,144), Q5_K(256,176), Q6_K(256,210), IQ2_XXS(256,66), IQ2_XS(256,74), IQ3_XXS(256,98), IQ4_XS(256,136), IQ4_NL(32,18), I32.
components.interface: `read_header(path) -> Header(kv: dict[str, Any], tensors: list[TensorInfo(name, ne: tuple[int,...], ggml_type: str, offset: int, n_bytes: int)], alignment: int, data_offset: int)`. `TensorInfo.abs_offset = header.data_offset + offset`. Row size helper `row_bytes(ggml_type, ne0)`.
components.test: tests/test_ggufhdr.py builds a tiny GGUF with gguf.GGUFWriter (one F32 [4] tensor, one Q4_0 [32,8,4] 3-D tensor named blk.0.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight, two KV strings, one u32 array) and asserts names/ne/offsets/n_bytes/data_offset equal gguf.GGUFReader's. Integration (@integration): on the real 26B file data_offset == 15823936 and blk.0.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight n_bytes == 285474816.

components.purpose: Byte-range model of a GGUF for caching/pinning: classifies tensors into RESIDENT (everything not matching `blk.N.ffn_(gate_up|gate|up|down)_exps.weight`) and EXPERT slabs; expert e of layer l is [abs_offset + e*nb2, abs_offset + (e+1)*nb2) with nb2 = n_bytes / ne[2] (asserts divisibility). Produces per-layer slab sizes and totals, and page-aligned range merging.
components.interface: `Layout.from_gguf(path) -> Layout(n_layer, n_expert, resident_ranges: list[Range(offset,length,name)], expert_ranges: dict[(layer, expert)] -> list[Range] (gate_up slab + down slab), expert_bytes(layer) -> int, resident_bytes -> int, per_token_resident_read_bytes -> int (= attention + dense FFN + router + output head; excludes token_embd lookups when output is a separate tensor, includes it when tied))`. `align_ranges(ranges, page=16384) -> merged list`. `Layout.to_json()/from_json()`.
components.test: tests/test_layout.py on the synthetic GGUF: 4 experts × slab 288 B each (32×8×18/4... computed), contiguity, resident classification, alignment merge; integration: 26B expert_bytes(l) == 3345408 for all 30 layers, sum of all expert bytes == 12846034944 ± 0, resident_bytes ≈ 1.58e9.

components.purpose: The only custom C++: a llama.cpp program that runs prompt processing + greedy generation and records MoE routing and/or FFN activations via llama_context_params.cb_eval into the PGTRACE1 / PGACTS01 binary formats.
components.interface:
Usage: `pigemma-tracer [standard llama.cpp args] [--trace-out F.trace.bin] [--trace-weights] [--trace-probs] [--acts-out F.acts.bin] [--acts-layers 0,12,24,36,48,59] [--acts-tensors ffn_norm,ffn_gate_par,ffn_out] [--acts-max-tokens 512] [--chat] [--summary-out F.json]`. Implementation contract: (1) pre-scan argv, pop every `--trace-*/--acts-*/--chat/--summary-out` (and value) into a local struct, then `common_params_parse(argc', argv', params, LLAMA_EXAMPLE_COMMON)`; (2) `params.cb_eval = pigemma_cb; params.cb_eval_user_data = &state; params.warmup = false;` then `common_init_from_params(params)` → `model()`, `context()`; (3) read n_layer = llama_model_n_layer(model); arch via llama_model_meta_val_str(model, "general.architecture"); n_expert/n_expert_used via meta keys `<arch>.expert_count` / `<arch>.expert_used_count` (0 → MoE trace disabled, error if --trace-out given); (4) prompt = params.prompt (from -p/-f), if --chat wrap as `<start_of_turn>user
{prompt}<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
`; tokens = common_tokenize(ctx, prompt, add_bos=true, parse_special=true); `common_batch batch = common_batch_get_one(ctx, tokens); llama_process(ctx, LLAMA_PROCESS_TYPE_DECODE, batch.get())`; after return flush records pos 0..n_prompt-1 (phase 0); (5) generation loop up to params.n_predict (-n): `float* lg = llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1)`; argmax over llama_vocab_n_tokens(vocab); stop on llama_vocab_is_eog; `common_batch b = common_batch_get_one(ctx, {tok}); llama_process(...)`; flush one record (phase 1, token = tok); collect common_token_to_piece text; (6) callback: `static bool pigemma_cb(ggml_tensor* t, bool ask, void* ud)`: classify t->name by prefix against the enabled set {"ffn_moe_topk-", "ffn_moe_weights-" (if --trace-weights), "ffn_moe_probs-" (if --trace-probs)} ∪ {"<kind>-" for kinds in --acts-tensors} and parse il = atoi(strrchr(name,'-')+1); for acts also require il ∈ acts-layers; `if (ask) return matched;` (returning true only for wanted nodes keeps scheduler batching); on ask=false: data = ggml_backend_buffer_is_host(t->buffer) ? t->data : ggml_backend_tensor_get into a scratch vector; copy USING nb STRIDES (ffn_moe_topk is a view of the argsort result: ne=[k, n_tokens], nb[1] = n_expert*4, type I32; ffn_moe_weights ne=[1,k,n_tokens] F32 → use ne[2] as n_tokens and nb[2]; ffn_moe_probs ne=[n_expert, n_tokens] F32; acts ne=[ne0, n_tokens] F32 → convert with ggml_fp32_to_fp16); append columns to per-layer accumulators; return true; (7) flush writes token-major fixed-size records, asserts every layer accumulated the same column count, then clears accumulators; header n_records patched at exit (also on SIGINT via atexit); (8) --summary-out JSON: {"n_prompt","n_gen","t_load_ms","t_p_eval_ms","t_eval_ms" (from llama_perf_context(ctx)), "gen_text" (JSON-escaped), "eog": bool, "n_layer","n_expert","n_expert_used","model": params.model.path}. Exit code 0 on success, 2 on usage error, 3 on compute failure.
components.test: Golden run in Docker: `-m <26B> -p 'The capital of France is' -n 4 -t 12 --trace-out tests/fixtures/golden_26b_4tok.trace.bin --trace-weights --summary-out tests/fixtures/golden_26b_4tok.json` → committed; tests/test_trace_io.py validates it (weights sum to 1, ids unique, record count == n_prompt+n_gen). components.purpose: Spawn/own a llama-server.exe child, wait for /health, send /completion requests, sample the child's memory, terminate it (our own child only).
components.interface: `class LlamaServer(bin, model_path, extra_args: list[str], port=18080, threads=6, ctx=4096)`: `start()` → Popen with stdout/stderr to a log file, poll `GET /health` until 200 (timeout 300 s), records `load_time_s` (wall from spawn to first 200) and parses `load time = ... ms` from the log when present; `complete(prompt, n_predict=128, temperature=0, cache_prompt=False, stop=["<end_of_turn>"]) -> {'content','timings','tokens_predicted','stop_type'}`; `mem_sampler` thread polls psutil.Process(pid).memory_info().rss and memory_full_info().private (0.5 s) → `peak_working_set_bytes`, `peak_private_bytes`; `stop()` → terminate() then kill() after 10 s; context-manager. Chat wrapping helper `gemma_chat(user_text)`.

Runs 6 prompts (3 EN, 2 HE, 1 code; chat-wrapped) sequentially, temperature 0. Writes results/bench/<model_id>__gen__<variant>.json = {"host","model_id","variant","server_args","load_time_s","peak_working_set_bytes","peak_private_bytes","requests":[{"prompt_id","timings","content","visible","thinking_chars"}],"agg":{"pp_tps_mean","tg_tps_mean","tg_tps_min","accept_rate","speedup_vs_plain" (filled by report)}}. 31B variants: plain, mtp (g4-31b-mtp-q4_0), ngram. --quick: 3 prompts, n_predict 48.

Writes results/quality/<id>__ppl[__kld-vs-<base>].json = {ppl, ppl_err, kld_*, corpus_sha256, argv}. `pigemma quality qa --model <id> --variant plain|mtp|dflash|ngram` → runs docs/eval/qa_set.jsonl through LlamaServer (temperature 0, n_predict 160), pass = any(expected substring in visible text, case/niqqud-insensitive) → results/quality/<id>__qa__<variant>.json = {items:[{id, visible, thinking_chars, pass}], score, exact_match_vs_plain (fraction of items whose visible text equals the plain variant's; None if plain not yet run)}.

components.purpose: E4 driver: runs pigemma-tracer in Docker over the corpus and writes sidecars.
components.interface:
`pigemma trace collect --model g4-26b-a4b-q4_0 [--corpus docs/corpus/trace_*.txt] [--n-gen 128] [--threads 12] [--probs] [--out traces/]` → per prompt file P: `pc/docker_run.sh -- build/tracer-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-tracer -m /work/ -f /work/

-n 128 -t 12 -c 4096 -b 512 -ub 512 --no-warmup --chat --trace-out /work/traces/__.trace.bin --trace-weights [--trace-probs] --summary-out /work/traces/<...>.summary.json`; then writes traces/<...>.trace.json sidecar (see data_formats) merging the summary, prompt sha256, argv, llama commit, wall time, and a `coherent` flag computed by a heuristic (≥ 60% of generated chars are letters/spaces/punct and no 6-gram repeats >3 times). `pigemma trace acts --model g4-31b-q4_0 --layers 0,12,24,36,48,59 --tensors ffn_norm,ffn_gate_par,ffn_out --n-gen 32 --max-tokens 288 --corpus docs/corpus/h2_*.txt` → same wrapper with `--acts-*` flags → traces/__

.acts.bin + sidecar. `pigemma trace stats traces/*.trace.bin` → prints per-layer expert-usage entropy, top-10 experts, token-to-token churn (fraction of experts at t also used at t-1 per layer), unique experts touched, and compulsory-miss bytes → results/trace/__stats.json.
components.test: unit: argv builder, sidecar merge, coherence heuristic on fixtures; integration: one short prompt end-to-end in Docker produces a readable trace with n_records == n_prompt + n_gen.

components.purpose: Expert-cache replacement policies over keys (layer, expert) with byte sizes.
components.interface: `class Policy: __init__(capacity_bytes, sizes: dict[key,int]); access(key, t) -> bool hit; evict_as_needed()`. Implementations: `LRU` (OrderedDict), `LFU` (frequency with optional exponential decay `--lfu-decay 0.999`/token, ties → LRU), `StaticHot(ranking)` (pre-filled with the top keys by ranking until capacity; misses are served but never inserted), `Hybrid(ranking, pinned_fraction)` (pinned static part + LRU for the rest), `Belady(next_use)` (offline optimal; next_use precomputed from the whole access sequence; evicts the key whose next use is farthest/never). All policies expose `resident_bytes()` and `stats()`.
components.test: tests/test_sim_policies.py: hand-computed hit sequences for LRU and Belady on a 5-access toy; Belady hits ≥ LRU hits on 50 random traces; capacity 0 → 0 hits; capacity ≥ total → only compulsory misses; StaticHot never inserts; Hybrid with pinned_fraction=0 equals LRU.

components.purpose: E5 driver: replay trace(s) through a policy at a Pi byte budget, with optional prefetch model, produce per-token byte accounting.
components.interface: `pigemma sim run --trace traces/*.trace.bin --layout traces/<model>__layout.json --config pi/configs/pi5-8gb-nvme-gen3.json --policy lru|lfu|static|hybrid:0.5|belady [--prefetch none|prev-token] [--warmup-tokens 256] [--fit-split 0.5] [--reset-per-trace]` → capacity_bytes = config.ram_bytes − config.reserve_os_bytes − layout.resident_bytes − kv_bytes(config.ctx, model) − config.compute_buffers_bytes (if ≤ 0 → verdict INFEASIBLE, still simulates with capacity 0 for the record). Access order: for each token t, for il in 0..L-1, for e in topk[t,il]: access((il,e)). StaticHot/Hybrid rankings are fit on the first fit_split of each trace and evaluated on the remainder (reported separately from the all-data ranking). Prefetch prev-token: predicted set for (t, il+1) = topk[t-1, il+1]; bytes of predicted misses that can be loaded during layer il's compute (min(bytes, storage_bw × layer_compute_s)) are counted as `overlapped_bytes` and removed from stall. Output results/sim/<model>__<config>__<policy>[__pf].json = {capacity_bytes, inputs:{traces, n_tokens, warmup}, per_token:{miss_bytes mean/p50/p95, n_miss mean, hit_rate steady-state and overall}, per_layer_hit_rate[L], overlapped_bytes_mean, projection (from projection.py), assumptions (copied from config with `source` tags)}. Also `pigemma sim sweep --config all --policy all` producing results/sim/summary.csv.
components.test: tests/test_expert_cache.py: synthetic trace with 2 hot experts per layer → hit rate → 1 after warm-up for capacity ≥ 2 slabs/layer; capacity accounting equals formula; prefetch prev-token on a constant-routing trace overlaps 100% of misses after token 1.

components.purpose: Turns byte accounting into projected tok/s, keeping measured, projected and assumed values apart.
components.interface: `project(resident_read_bytes, hit_expert_bytes, miss_bytes, n_miss, cfg) -> {'t_resident_s': (resident_read_bytes+hit_expert_bytes)/cfg.ram_bw_eff, 't_stall_s': miss_bytes/cfg.storage_bw + n_miss*cfg.io_latency_s − overlapped/cfg.storage_bw, 't_token_s', 'tok_s', 'floor_tok_s_all_in_ram': cfg.ram_bw_eff/(resident_read_bytes+all_expert_bytes_per_token)}`. `calibrate_ram_bw(measured_tg_tps, bytes_per_token) -> ram_bw_eff` used on the desktop (e.g., 9.86 tok/s × 2.37 GB = 23.4 GB/s) and later on the Pi from pi/06 bench; `project_dense(model_bytes_per_token, cfg)` for the 31B (17.65 GB/token → NVMe-streamed ≈ 0.045 tok/s; the table is printed, not hidden).
components.test: tests/test_projection.py: formula on known numbers; monotonicity in storage_bw; all-in-RAM floor independent of storage.

components.purpose: Ranks (layer, expert) by trace frequency and emits the pinning plan consumed on the Pi.
components.interface: `pigemma sim hotset --trace traces/*.trace.bin --layout <layout.json> --budget-bytes <N> [--out traces/<model>__hotset.json]` → ranking by access count (ties by recency), cumulative bytes; writes hotset.json (data_formats). Prints how many experts fit the budget and the trace hit-rate a static set of that size would get (from StaticHot).
components.test: unit on synthetic traces: ranking order and cumulative bytes; budget cut correct.

components.purpose: E6: desktop reality check of the cache model — run llama-completion under a cgroup memory cap so mmap'd expert pages are evicted and re-read through the bind mount (the measurable slow tier), at several caps.
components.interface: `pc/proxy_cache_limit.sh --model <gguf> --mem 5g,7g,10g,20g --n 64 --threads 6 --prompt docs/corpus/trace_en_01.txt` → for each cap: (a) tier bandwidth: `pc/docker_run.sh --memory $M -- bash -c 'vmtouch -e <gguf>; dd if=<gguf> of=/dev/null bs=2M count=512 skip=$((RANDOM%6000)) iflag=direct 2>&1 | tail -1'` (3 samples; iflag=direct may be ignored by the mount → recorded as `direct_honoured: bool` by comparing to a warm re-read); (b) `pc/docker_run.sh --memory $M --cpus 6 -- third_party/llama.cpp/build-linux-x86/bin/llama-completion -m <gguf> -f <prompt> -n 64 -t 6 -c 2048 --no-warmup -no-cnv --temp 0 2> results/proxy/<M>.stderr` and parse `eval time ... tokens per second` and `prompt eval`; (c) `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.stat` file/anon at the end (printed by a wrapper `cat` inside the same container run). Writes results/proxy/<model>__proxy.json = {points:[{mem_cap_bytes, tier_bw_bytes_s, tg_tps, pp_tps, cgroup_file_bytes}]}. `pigemma sim validate --proxy results/proxy/<..>.json --trace traces/<model>__trace_en_01.trace.bin --layout ...` computes, per point, capacity = cap − anon − resident, simulates LRU, projects with ram_bw_eff calibrated from the uncapped (20g) point and storage_bw = tier_bw, and reports predicted vs measured tg_tps and relative error.
components.test: script passes `bash -n`; integration: 4 points recorded; validate prints a table; pass threshold in experiments E6.

components.purpose: Load one Q4_0 tensor from the 31B GGUF as float32 [n_out, n_in] using gguf.GGUFReader + gguf.quants.dequantize, with row-major orientation checked against llama.cpp conventions (GGUF ne = [n_in, n_out]; dequantize(t.data, t.tensor_type) returns (n_out, n_in)).
components.interface: `load_matrix(gguf_path, tensor_name) -> np.float32[n_out, n_in]`; `ffn_tensors(layer) -> ('blk.{l}.ffn_gate.weight','blk.{l}.ffn_up.weight','blk.{l}.ffn_down.weight')`; `q4_0_bytes(shape) -> int` (ne0*ne1/32*18); `requant(W, 'Q2_K'|'Q3_K'|'Q4_0'|'Q8_0') -> (W_hat float32, n_bytes)` via gguf.quants.quantize→dequantize (row length must be a multiple of 256 for K-quants: 5376 and 21504 both are).
components.test: tests/test_h2_dequant.py: quantize→dequantize round-trip on random [64, 256] matrices has rel. RMS error < 0.08 for Q4_0 and < 0.25 for Q2_K; integration: `ffn_out` reconstruction check (see run_h2).

components.language: Python (numpy; torch optional for randomized SVD)
components.purpose: W = W_base + R with residual split into input-column groups; bounds per group.
components.interface: `make_base(W, kind: 'q2k'|'q3k'|'lowrank', rank=256) -> Base(W_base, bytes_base, meta)` — lowrank uses torch.svd_lowrank(W, q=rank+16, niter=3) and stores U,S,V in f16 (bytes = rank*(n_in+n_out)*2); q2k/q3k use dequant.requant. `group_residual(W, W_base, group_cols=64) -> Groups(R: float32[n_out,n_in] (view), col_slices, spectral_norm[n_groups] (via np.linalg.svd on each [n_out, group_cols] slice, compute_uv=False → max singular value), fro_norm[n_groups], bytes_per_group = q4_0_bytes((n_out, group_cols)))`. Residual byte accounting is Q4_0-equivalent (4.5 bpw) — stated in output.
components.test: tests/test_h2_decompose.py: for random W (256×512) and 1000 random x: ||R_g x_g||₂ ≤ spectral_norm[g]·||x_g||₂ always (and ≤ fro bound); lowrank rank=min(dims) reconstructs exactly; bytes formulas.

components.purpose: Per-token oracle selection and bound-certified skipping metrics.
components.interface: `oracle_fraction(W, base, groups, X: float32[n_tok, n_in], eps_list=(0.01,0.03,0.1)) -> dict[eps] -> {'frac_groups_mean','frac_groups_p50','frac_groups_p90','bytes_mean'}`: for each token x: y = W@x; yb = W_base@x; C[:,g] = R[:,cols_g] @ x[cols_g] for all g (vectorised as (R * x[None,:]) then np.add.reduceat over group boundaries); sort groups by ||C[:,g]|| desc; take the smallest prefix with ||y − yb − Σ C||₂ ≤ eps·||y||₂. `certified_skip(groups, X, tau_rule='per_group_budget') -> {'frac_certified_mean', 'tightness_p50': median of ||R_g x_g||/(||R_g||·||x_g||), 'certification_efficiency': frac_certified/frac_oracle_skipped at eps=0.03}` where τ = eps·||yb||₂/√n_groups (so Σ certified errors ≤ eps·||yb|| by the triangle inequality in the worst case). `pi_bytes_per_token(frac_by_layer_kind, n_layer=60, attention_bytes=4.77e9, head_bytes=1.156e9) -> dict`.
components.test: unit on small random matrices: frac(eps) is non-increasing in eps; eps=∞ → 0; W_base=W → 0 groups; certified groups never include a group whose true contribution exceeds τ.

components.purpose: E7 driver with configurable sampling so it finishes in < 1 h on the desktop.
components.interface: `pigemma h2 run --model g4-31b-q4_0 --acts traces/g4-31b-q4_0__*.acts.bin --layers 0,12,24,36,48,59 --matrices gate,up,down --bases q2k,lowrank:256 --group-cols 64 --max-tokens 320 [--quick]` → for each (layer, matrix): X = acts ffn_norm (for gate/up) or ffn_gate_par (for down); first a SANITY step on layer l: y_ref = acts ffn_out[t]; y_ours = W_down @ (gelu-already-applied ffn_gate_par[t]) → rel. error reported (expect < 2%, Q8 activation quantisation in llama.cpp); then decompose + oracle + certified; results/h2/<model>__h2.json = {sampling, per_layer_matrix:[{layer, matrix, base, bytes_base, bytes_residual_total, sanity_rel_err, oracle:{eps:{...}}, certified:{...}, seconds}], summary:{frac_0.03_median, cert_eff_median, pi_bytes_per_token:{attention, head, ffn_base, ffn_residual_at_0.03, total}, verdict}} and results/h2/<model>__h2.csv. --quick: layers 0,30,59; matrices gate,down; 64 tokens; base q2k only.
components.test: unit: the driver on a synthetic 'model' (tiny random GGUF written with GGUFWriter containing blk.0.ffn_{gate,up,down}.weight Q4_0 [256×512] and a synthetic acts file) completes and writes the JSON; integration: full --quick run on the 31B acts < 15 min.

components.purpose: Assemble every results/**/*.json into results/REPORT.md following docs/RESULTS_TEMPLATE.md, with three labelled sections per table: MEASURED (desktop), PROJECTED (Pi, from simulation), ASSUMED (bandwidth/latency inputs with sources).

components.purpose: Pi hardware budgets for the simulator and for feasibility; every number tagged with its source.
components.interface: Schema in data_formats 'pi_config'. Defaults: 4gb-microsd {ram 4.0e9, reserve_os 0.7e9, storage_bw 60e6 (assumed, microSD 2 MB reads), io_latency 2e-3, ram_bw_eff 7.5e9 (assumed; to be replaced by pi/06 measurement), ctx 2048, compute_buffers 0.3e9}; 8gb-usb3 {8.0e9, 0.8e9, 350e6, 0.5e-3, 7.5e9, 4096, 0.3e9}; 8gb-nvme-gen3 {8.0e9, 0.8e9, 800e6, 0.2e-3, 7.5e9, 4096, 0.3e9}; 16gb-ram {16.0e9, 0.9e9, 800e6, 0.2e-3, 7.5e9, 4096, 0.4e9}.

components.purpose: Collect raw machine facts into JSON and call the Python verdict; prints a human table and exits 0 (some tier feasible) / 2 (nothing feasible) / 3 (machine busy and no --force). Read-only; refuses to do anything heavy.
components.interface: `pi/00_feasibility.sh [--force] [--out pi/out/feasibility.json]` collects: free -b (MemTotal/MemAvailable/SwapTotal), `getconf PAGESIZE`, nproc, lscpu flags (asimddp, i8mm, sve present?), uname -r, /etc/os-release, `lsblk -b -d -o NAME,ROTA,TRAN,MODEL,SIZE,TYPE -J`, root device via findmnt -J /, `df -B1 --output=avail,target <models_dir>`, NVMe: ls /dev/nvme* and `cat /sys/class/nvme/nvme0/device/current_link_speed` + `current_link_width` if present, /boot/firmware/config.txt grep pciex1_gen, governor (`cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_governor`), `ulimit -l`, loadavg, top-5 RSS processes (name + RSS only), whether `cmake`/`gcc`/`git`/`python3` exist and versions. Then `python3 -m pigemma.pi.feasibility --facts pi/out/facts.json --configs pi/configs --out pi/out/feasibility.json`.
components.test: `bash -n`; runs inside the Docker image (Linux, non-Pi) and produces a verdict JSON (storage type 'unknown' tolerated).

components.purpose: Pure decision logic from facts → per-tier verdicts with reasons; unit-testable on Windows.
components.interface: `decide(facts: dict, tiers: list[Tier]) -> Verdict` where tiers (built-in table): 26B-A4B {Q4_0 14.44 GB, UD-IQ4_XS 13.6, UD-Q3_K_M 12.7, UD-IQ3_XXS 11.4, UD-Q2_K_XL 10.6, UD-IQ2_XXS 9.9} with resident_bytes ≈ 1.58e9 × (quant_bytes/14.44e9) scaled, and 31B {Q4_0 17.65, IQ4_XS 16.4, Q3_K_S 13.2, UD-IQ3_XXS 11.8, UD-Q2_K_XL 11.8, UD-IQ2_XXS 8.5}. Rules: available_for_model = MemAvailable − reserve − kv(ctx) − compute_buffers; FITS_RAM if file ≤ available_for_model; else STREAM_<NVME|USB3|SD> if storage_free ≥ file+2 GB and (for MoE) available_for_model ≥ resident + 1.0e9 (≥ ~300 experts); dense models streaming → INFEASIBLE_SPEED (projected < 0.1 tok/s) but allowed with --force for measurement; 4 GB + microSD MoE → INFEASIBLE (reason: residual budget < 1 GB and 60 MB/s tier ⇒ < 0.2 tok/s projected). Busy rule: loadavg1 > 1.0 or MemAvailable < 60% MemTotal → `busy: true`. Output Verdict(dict) incl. `recommended` (best tier by projected tok/s with quality tie-break preferring higher-bit quant) and `pi_config_match` (closest pi/configs/*.json).
components.test: tests/test_feasibility.py: facts for the 4 configurations (4GB/SD → MoE INFEASIBLE, recommends nothing heavy; 8GB/USB3 → STREAM_USB3 Q4_0 or IQ2 with projected <1 tok/s; 8GB/NVMe → STREAM_NVME; 16GB → FITS_RAM UD-Q3_K_M/IQ4_XS, Q4_0 FITS only if MemAvailable ≥ 15.5 GB); busy detection; the probed context-friend-1 facts (4 GB, SD, Hailo on PCIe, busy) → exit code 3.

components.purpose: Map a feasibility verdict to a concrete download (HF repo/file, size) and llama.cpp flags; used by 04_fetch_model.sh and 05_run.sh.
components.interface: `python3 -m pigemma.pi.select_quant --feasibility pi/out/feasibility.json [--prefer quality|speed] --emit env` → prints `MODEL_REPO=... MODEL_FILE=... MODEL_BYTES=... LLAMA_FLAGS='-t 4 -c 2048 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -b 256 -ub 64 --mmap on --no-mlock --prio 2' DRAFT_REPO=ggml-org/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF DRAFT_FILE=mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_0.gguf PIN_BUDGET_BYTES=...`. Table: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf gemma-4-26B_q4_0-it.gguf; unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF UD-* files; 31B equivalents.
components.test: unit: each verdict class maps to exactly one selection; env output is shell-safe.

components.purpose: Idempotent OS tuning; dry-run by default, prints exact commands; `--apply` executes; notes which changes need a reboot.

Prints before/after values.

components.purpose: Native llama.cpp build on the Pi at the pinned commit, plus the tracer optionally.

components.purpose: Measure the storage tier and RAM bandwidth the projections depend on; write them into pi/out/io_mem.json so `pigemma sim` can replace ASSUMED values with MEASURED ones.
components.interface: `pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh [--dir <models_dir>] [--size-mb 1024]` → fio if installed else dd: random 2 MiB reads (`fio --name=rr2m --rw=randread --bs=2M --direct=1 --size=1G --numjobs=1 --runtime=20 --time_based --output-format=json`), sequential read, and 4 KiB random read (IOPS); RAM: python3 `memoryview` copy of a 512 MiB bytearray ×5 (GB/s) and, if numpy present, `a.sum()` streaming read bandwidth; CPU: 1 s `openssl speed -evp aes-128-gcm`-free alternative → skip; prints a table. Refuses if free disk < size×1.2.

Both scripts re-run the busy check and refuse (exit 3) if MemAvailable < needed or loadavg high, printing why.

components.language: Python (stdlib: mmap, ctypes, os, signal, json)
components.purpose: Hot-set pinning daemon: MAP_SHARED-map the GGUF and mlock page-aligned byte ranges of all RESIDENT tensors plus the top-K experts from hotset.json until the budget is reached, so the shared page cache keeps them while llama.cpp's own mmap streams cold experts. Reports VmLck and exits cleanly on SIGTERM (munlock).
components.interface: `sudo python3 -m pigemma.pi.pin_hotset --gguf <file> --hotset traces/<model>__hotset.json --budget-bytes <N> [--page-size auto] [--dry-run] [--verify]` → computes ranges with pigemma.layout (via ggufhdr), merges/aligns to getconf PAGESIZE (16384 on this kernel), checks RLIMIT_MEMLOCK (resource.getrlimit) and MemAvailable − budget ≥ 1.0 GB else refuses with the exact ulimit/limits.conf fix; mlock via `ctypes.CDLL(None).mlock(addr, len)` with addr from `ctypes.addressof(ctypes.c_char.from_buffer(mm, offset))` per range (touching pages first with a strided read to fault them in); prints bytes pinned per category (resident, experts, count), `/proc/self/status VmLck`, and with --verify runs `vmtouch -v <file>` summary if available; then sleeps until SIGTERM/SIGINT. 07_pin_hotset.sh wraps it as a background process with a pidfile under pi/out/.
components.test: tests/test_pin_hotset.py: range planning on the synthetic GGUF with a fake hotset and page size 16384 (alignment, budget cut, resident-first ordering); mlock calls mocked on Windows; integration on Linux (Docker): pins a 64 MB synthetic file and VmLck ≥ 64 MB.

data_formats.name: PGTRACE1 routing trace (traces/<model>__<prompt>.trace.bin)
data_formats.spec: Little-endian binary. HEADER (64 bytes): [0..8) magic ASCII "PGTRACE1"; [8..12) u32 version=1; [12..16) u32 n_layer (all layers of the model, 30 for 26B-A4B); [16..20) u32 n_expert (128); [20..24) u32 n_expert_used (8); [24..28) u32 flags (bit0 HAS_WEIGHTS, bit1 HAS_PROBS); [28..32) u32 record_size; [32..40) u64 n_records (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF while writing, patched at close; readers infer from file size if unpatched); [40..64) zeros. RECORDS from offset 64, fixed size, token-major: u32 pos (sequence position, prompt then generated), i32 token (input token id at pos), u8 phase (0 prompt-batched, 1 single-token decode), u8 pad[3], u16 topk[n_layer][n_expert_used] (expert ids in llama.cpp's selection order = descending prob), then if HAS_WEIGHTS f32 weights[n_layer][n_expert_used] (post-normalisation gating weights, sum≈1), then if HAS_PROBS f16 probs[n_layer][n_expert] (full softmax router probs). record_size = 12 + 2*L*k + (4*L*k if weights) + (2*L*E if probs); 26B: 492 / 1452 / 9132 bytes. Sidecar JSON next to it (same stem, .trace.json): {"format":"PGTRACE1","model_id","gguf_path","gguf_size","gguf_header_sha256" (sha of the first data_offset bytes),"llama_commit":"a7b94df","llama_build":11398,"tracer_argv":[...],"prompt_file","prompt_sha256","chat_wrapped":true,"n_prompt","n_gen","eog":bool,"t_load_ms","t_p_eval_ms","t_eval_ms","gen_text","coherent":bool,"host":{...},"created_utc"}. Layout companion traces/<model>__layout.json = Layout.to_json(): {"n_layer","n_expert","data_offset","alignment","resident_ranges":[[abs_offset,length,name],...],"expert_slabs":{"<layer>":[[gate_up_abs_offset, 2230272],[down_abs_offset,1115136]] per expert as offset of expert 0 + stride},"expert_bytes_per_layer":[3345408,...],"resident_bytes","per_token_resident_read_bytes"}.

data_formats.name: PGACTS01 activation capture (traces/<model>__<prompt>.acts.bin)
data_formats.spec: Little-endian. HEADER: [0..8) "PGACTS01"; u32 version=1; u32 n_layer_total; u32 n_sampled; u32 n_kinds; u32 dtype (1 = f16); u32 record_size; u64 n_records (patched at close); u64 reserved; then u32 layer_ids[n_sampled]; then n_kinds × (u32 name_len, bytes name (e.g. "ffn_norm", "ffn_gate_par", "ffn_out"), u32 ne0); header_end padded to 64-byte multiple (u32 header_size stored right after the magic block? — no: header_size is derivable; readers parse sequentially then align up to 64). RECORDS: u32 pos, i32 token, u8 phase, u8 pad[3], then for s in layer_ids order, for kind in kinds order: f16[ne0]. For the 31B with the 3 default kinds: record_size = 12 + n_sampled × (5376+21504+5376) × 2 = 12 + 64512 × n_sampled (387 KB for 6 layers; 320 tokens ≈ 124 MB). Sidecar .acts.json mirrors the trace sidecar plus {"layer_ids","kinds","max_tokens"}.

experiments.hypothesis: Both models are memory-bandwidth-bound on the desktop CPU for generation, so tg tok/s saturates well before 12 threads, while pp tok/s keeps scaling; the 31B generates at ≈ (effective BW / 17.65 GB) ≈ 2–3.5 tok/s.
experiments.procedure: `pigemma bench threads --model g4-26b-a4b-q4_0 --threads 4,6,8,12 --pp 128 --tg 32 --reps 3`, then with `--kv q8_0`; repeat for g4-31b-q4_0 (tg 16, reps 2). Windows prebuilt llama-bench.exe, mmap, no mlock.
metrics: pp tok/s ± sd per thread count
tg tok/s ± sd per thread count
effective GB/s = tg tok/s × bytes/token (2.37 GB MoE, 17.65 GB dense)
model_size and load behaviour from the JSON
experiments.runtime_estimate: 26B ≈ 4 min; 31B ≈ 8 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS = JSON written for both models with ≥ 4 thread rows each; sanity: 26B tg at 6 threads within ±25% of the earlier 9.86 tok/s; FLAG if tg(12) < tg(6) by >15% (SMT contention) → recommend physical-core count on the Pi.

experiments.hypothesis: MTP/DFlash drafts give ≥ 1.4× generation speed-up on the 26B at greedy decoding with ≥ 60% draft acceptance; ngram-simple gives < 1.1× on free text; on the 31B MTP gives ≥ 1.5× because verification is bandwidth-bound and amortises weight reads.
experiments.procedure: `pigemma bench gen --model g4-26b-a4b-q4_0 --variant plain|mtp|dflash|ngram --n-predict 128` (6 prompts, temperature 0, llama-server.exe, -t 6, -c 4096, -fa on); `--model g4-31b-q4_0 --variant plain|mtp` (n-predict 64). Record spec_type_effective (inferred vs explicit fallback).
experiments.runtime_estimate: 26B 4 variants ≈ 12 min; 31B 2 variants ≈ 12 min
experiments.thresholds: Speculation counts as ACTIVE only if timings.draft_n > 0 on every request; PASS for the hypothesis if speed-up ≥ 1.4 (26B) / 1.5 (31B) with accept_rate ≥ 0.6; report otherwise as 'no benefit' — not a failure of the harness. E3-qa exact_match_vs_plain must be ≥ 0.95 for a speculative variant to be reported as lossless.

experiments.hypothesis: The official QAT Q4_0 GGUFs produce coherent EN/HE answers (QA ≥ 80%) and sane perplexity on the fixed corpus; speculative variants reproduce the plain greedy outputs.
experiments.procedure: `pigemma quality ppl --model <id> --ctx 512 --chunks 8` for both models (adds `--kld-base` only if ≥ 3.2 GB free on D:); `pigemma quality qa --model <id> --variant plain` then `--variant mtp` (and dflash for 26B). Optional later (disk-gated, not today): alt-quant KLD vs the Q4_0 base for Pi quant selection.
metrics: KLD mean/p99.9/same-top-p when a base exists
experiments.runtime_estimate: PPL 8 chunks: 26B ≈ 3 min, 31B ≈ 6 min; QA 24 items: 26B ≈ 6 min, 31B ≈ 15 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS: QA ≥ 0.80 plain for both models; spec exact_match ≥ 0.95; FLAG if Hebrew subset < 0.6 (document as a quality caveat for the Pi tier).

experiments.hypothesis: Expert usage in Gemma 4 26B-A4B is skewed and temporally sticky: a minority of (layer, expert) slabs carries most accesses and ≥ 40% of a token's experts were also used by the previous token in the same layer — the precondition for H1.
experiments.procedure: `pc/build_tracer.sh`; `pigemma trace collect --model g4-26b-a4b-q4_0 --n-gen 128 --threads 12` over the 6 trace prompts (chat-wrapped, -b 512 -ub 512); `pigemma trace stats traces/*.trace.bin`. Golden fixture produced first with -n 4.
metrics: fraction of accesses covered by the top 25% / 50% of slabs
unique experts touched per prompt and across prompts
tracer wall time (not a performance number)
experiments.runtime_estimate: build 5–8 min; 6 prompts × (≈60 s load through bind mount + ≈90 s compute) ≈ 15–20 min
experiments.thresholds: Trace VALID if n_records == n_prompt+n_gen for every file, weights sum to 1±1e-3, ids unique per token-layer, generated text coherent. H1 precondition MET if the top 50% of slabs cover ≥ 75% of accesses OR churn ≥ 0.4; otherwise H1 is already weak before simulation.

experiments.hypothesis: At the Pi 5 8 GB + NVMe budget (≈5 GB of expert cache ≈ 1500 of 3840 slabs) an LRU/hybrid policy reaches ≥ 70% steady-state hit rate so streamed bytes fall to ≤ 250 MB/token and projected speed is ≥ 1 tok/s; 4 GB + microSD is infeasible; 16 GB is bandwidth-bound at ≈ 3 tok/s regardless of policy.
experiments.procedure: `pigemma sim sweep --trace traces/g4-26b-a4b-q4_0__*.trace.bin --layout traces/g4-26b-a4b-q4_0__layout.json --config all --policy all --prefetch none,prev-token --warmup-tokens 256 --fit-split 0.5`; `pigemma sim hotset --budget-bytes <capacity of pi5-8gb-nvme-gen3>`.
metrics: steady-state hit rate per config × policy
projected tok/s (with ASSUMED ram_bw_eff 7.5 GB/s and storage bw per config) and all-in-RAM floor
Belady gap = Belady hit − best online hit
experiments.runtime_estimate: < 5 min for 4 configs × 5 policies × 2 prefetch modes on ~4k-token traces
experiments.thresholds: H1 SUPPORTED if best online policy at 8 GB+NVMe: hit ≥ 0.70 and projected ≥ 1.0 tok/s; WEAK if 0.5–1.0 tok/s; FALSIFIED-for-8GB if < 0.5 tok/s. Belady gap > 0.15 → prefetch/prediction research is worthwhile; ≤ 0.05 → policy is not the bottleneck.

experiments.hypothesis: The simulator's cache model predicts real behaviour: when the mmap'd model is capped by a cgroup memory limit, the measured tg slowdown matches miss_bytes/tier_bw + n_miss×latency within ±35%.
experiments.procedure: `pc/proxy_cache_limit.sh --model <26B gguf> --mem 5g,7g,10g,20g --n 64 --threads 6 --prompt docs/corpus/trace_en_01.txt` (Linux static llama-completion in Docker on the bind mount; tier bandwidth measured in the same session; cgroup memory.stat recorded), then `pigemma sim validate --proxy results/proxy/<..>.json --trace traces/g4-26b-a4b-q4_0__trace_en_01.trace.bin --layout ...` (ram_bw_eff calibrated from the 20g point).
metrics: tier bandwidth (bytes/s) and whether O_DIRECT was honoured
experiments.runtime_estimate: 4 caps × ≈ 5 min ≈ 20–25 min
experiments.thresholds: VALIDATED if |error| ≤ 35% on ≥ 3 of 4 caps and the ordering of caps is reproduced; otherwise report which term is off (stall vs resident) and keep Pi projections labelled 'unvalidated'. Note in the report that the slow tier here is the Docker bind mount (host-cached), i.e., this validates the cache model, not Pi NVMe speed.

experiments.hypothesis: For the dense 31B FFN, a cheap base (Q2_K requant or rank-256) plus an oracle-selected ≤ 25% of residual column groups keeps the FFN output within 3% relative error, and the per-group norm bound ||R_g||₂·||x_g|| certifies at least half of the oracle's skips.
experiments.procedure: `pigemma trace acts --model g4-31b-q4_0 --layers 0,12,24,36,48,59 --tensors ffn_norm,ffn_gate_par,ffn_out --n-gen 32 --max-tokens 288 --corpus docs/corpus/h2_*.txt` (Docker; 31B at ≈ 1.5–2.5 tok/s); `pigemma h2 run --layers 0,12,24,36,48,59 --matrices gate,up,down --bases q2k,lowrank:256 --group-cols 64 --max-tokens 320`.
metrics: sanity_rel_err of our dequant pipeline vs llama.cpp ffn_out (expect < 2%)
oracle frac_groups at eps 0.01/0.03/0.10 (mean, p50, p90) per layer×matrix×base
bytes_base + residual bytes at eps 0.03 vs Q4_0 bytes
certified skip fraction, tightness p50, certification_efficiency
implied Pi bytes/token (attention 4.77 GB + head 1.16 GB + FFN) and tok/s at 7.5 GB/s
experiments.runtime_estimate: acts capture ≈ 15 min (2 prompts incl. loads); h2 run: 6 layers × 3 matrices × 2 bases ≈ 36 decompositions × ~40–60 s ≈ 30–40 min (--quick ≈ 8 min)
experiments.thresholds: Pipeline VALID if sanity_rel_err < 0.02. H2 PROMISING if median frac(0.03) ≤ 0.25 for some base AND certification_efficiency ≥ 0.5; WEAK if frac ≤ 0.5 or efficiency 0.2–0.5; FALSIFIED (for this model/base family) if median frac(0.03) > 0.5. Regardless of outcome the report states the hard floor: attention+head alone are 5.9 GB/token → ≤ 1.3 tok/s from RAM on a Pi 5 and do not fit 8 GB.

experiments.hypothesis: The Pi scripts are correct and parametric before the real Pi is known: they produce the right verdict for the four reference configurations and for the probed (wrong) Pi, and run on a generic Linux without touching anything.
experiments.procedure: `pytest tests/test_feasibility.py tests/test_pin_hotset.py tests/test_select_quant.py`; `pc/docker_run.sh -- bash pi/00_feasibility.sh --out pi/out/feasibility.docker.json`; `pc/docker_run.sh -- bash pi/01_os_tune.sh` (dry-run); `pc/docker_run.sh -- bash pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh --size-mb 256`; `bash -n` on all pi/*.sh; pin_hotset integration on a 64 MB synthetic file in Docker (VmLck check).
metrics: verdicts for pi5-4gb-microsd / 8gb-usb3 / 8gb-nvme / 16gb and for context-friend-1 facts
pinned bytes vs requested in the Docker pin test
experiments.runtime_estimate: ≈ 10 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS: 4 GB+SD → INFEASIBLE with reasons; 8 GB+USB3 → STREAM_USB3 projected < 1 tok/s; 8 GB+NVMe → STREAM_NVME; 16 GB → FITS_RAM (UD-Q3_K_M/IQ4_XS; Q4_0 only if MemAvailable ≥ 15.5 GB); context-friend-1 facts → busy, exit 3; all shell scripts pass `bash -n`; VmLck ≥ requested in the pin test.

implementation_order: WAVE 0 (one agent, ~15 min, blocks everything): pyproject.toml, pigemma/__init__.py, pigemma/paths.py (model registry + fingerprint), .gitignore additions, pc/docker_run.sh, tests/conftest.py skeleton with tiny_moe_gguf/tiny_dense_gguf fixtures (gguf.GGUFWriter), docs/ skeletons, docs/corpus + docs/eval prompt files, pi/configs/*.json. Commit.

WAVE 1 — five agents in parallel: [A] tools/tracer/{CMakeLists.txt,tracer.cpp} + pc/build_tracer.sh → build in Docker → golden 4-token trace fixture + 31B acts smoke (-n 2, 2 layers) → commit fixtures. [B] pigemma/bench/{parsers,llama_bench,server_client,gen_bench,quality}.py + tests/fixtures + tests → immediately start E1 (26B) then E2/E3 (26B) on the Windows binaries while coding continues (they are long-running and independent of A). [C] pigemma/ggufhdr.py, layout.py, trace.py, sim/{policies,expert_cache,projection,hotset}.py + tests on synthetic traces; `pigemma sim` validated end-to-end on a synthetic trace before the real one arrives. [D] pigemma/h2/{dequant,decompose,oracle,run_h2}.py + tests on random matrices; dequant sanity on one real 31B tensor (header read is instant). [E] pi/00..07 scripts, pigemma/pi/{feasibility,select_quant,pin_hotset}.py + tests; docs/HARDWARE_BUDGET.md and docs/PI_RUNTIME.md.

WAVE 2 — dependent runs: when A is built: pigemma/trace_collect.py (A or C) → E4 trace collection on the 26B in Docker (≈20 min) → C runs E5 sweep + hotset → E4/E5 JSONs. In parallel A runs the 31B acts capture (≈15 min) → D runs E7 (--quick first, then full if time allows). B continues E1/E2/E3 for the 31B.

WAVE 3 — validation and write-up: E6 proxy sweep (pc/proxy_cache_limit.sh, ≈25 min, Docker + bind mount; runs while E7 computes); `pigemma sim validate`; E8 Pi-readiness checks in Docker; pigemma/report.py → results/REPORT.md; README/HYPOTHESES/EXPERIMENT_PLAN finalised with the measured numbers and the three-column MEASURED/PROJECTED/ASSUMED tables; pc/run_all_today.ps1 re-run with -Quick to prove idempotent resumability; commit results JSON + REPORT.md (traces .bin and .kld stay untracked).

Parallelism rules: A is the only C++ work and is on the critical path for E4/E5/E7 — start it first; B's long benchmarks should start within the first 30 minutes; never run two model-loading jobs simultaneously on the desktop (both GGUFs together exceed the Docker VM's 31 GB page cache and distort timings) — serialize via a lock file results/.bench.lock honoured by cli.py; Windows-native benchmarks and Docker trace runs may overlap only if total RAM in use < 48 GB (cli.py checks psutil.virtual_memory()).

risks.risk: Docker bind-mount I/O: loading a 14–18 GB GGUF through the Windows→WSL2 mount is slow and the Docker VM has 31 GB, so the 31B acts run (17.65 GB file + process memory) may thrash or take very long; tracer timings are meaningless as performance numbers.
risks.mitigation: Trace/acts runs are the only Docker model jobs; run them one at a time with -t 12, small token budgets (--acts-max-tokens 288, 2 prompts, 6 layers), `docker stats` check before start, and never report tracer wall times as tok/s. Fallback for the 31B: 3 layers (0,30,59) and 1 prompt; fallback for E6 if the bind mount is too slow: reduce -n to 32 and caps to 6g,10g,20g.

risks.risk: cb_eval tensor assumptions: `ffn_moe_topk-<il>` is a strided view of the argsort result (nb[1]=512 B), `ffn_moe_weights` is 3-D [1,8,n], names could change if the pinned commit differs, and returning true on `ask` for many nodes slows the graph.
risks.mitigation: Tracer asserts type/ne on first sight of each name and aborts with a clear message; copies with nb strides; returns true on ask only for matched names; the golden fixture test checks weights sum to 1 and unique ids; the llama.cpp commit (a7b94df) is pinned and recorded in every sidecar.

risks.risk: Speculative decoding plumbing: `-md` is not accepted by llama-completion/llama-bench; spec-type inference from the draft GGUF may fail; Windows prebuilt lacks llama-speculative-simple.
risks.mitigation: All speculative measurement goes through llama-server.exe; harness verifies `timings.draft_n` is present and otherwise retries with an explicit `--spec-type draft-mtp|draft-dflash`, recording `spec_type_effective`; if still absent the variant is reported as 'speculation inactive', not as a speed-up of 1.0.

risks.risk: Disk space: D: has ~32 GB free (not 63), C: 34 GB. KLD base files are ≈2.1 GB each, acts ≈125 MB, no room to download alternative quants for a quant-vs-quality comparison today.
risks.mitigation: quality.py gates --kld-base on free space with the exact computed size; alt-quant KLD is documented as a follow-up (needs ~12 GB per quant); all large outputs are gitignored; pc/run_all_today.ps1 prints free space before each heavy step.

risks.risk: Honesty of projections: ram_bw_eff (7.5 GB/s), storage bandwidths and latencies for the Pi are assumptions until a Pi is measured; the desktop proxy's slow tier is a host-cached FUSE mount, not an NVMe; Windows RSS includes mapped file pages.
risks.mitigation: Every pi_config number carries a `source` string; report.py prints MEASURED / PROJECTED / ASSUMED columns and refuses to render a projection without its assumption list; E6 is described as validating the cache model only; memory is reported as both WorkingSet and PrivateBytes with definitions; pi/03 and pi/06 overwrite the assumed values when the Pi runs.

risks.risk: Gemma 4 thinking channel (`<|channel>thought … <channel|>`) consumes generated tokens and would break QA scoring and skew tok/s comparisons across variants.
risks.mitigation: parsers.strip_thinking is applied before scoring and `thinking_chars`/`thinking_share` are reported; n_predict 160 for QA; identical prompts and temperature 0 across variants so thinking length is comparable; exact_match_vs_plain compares visible text.

risks.risk: Time: the 31B is slow (~2.5–3.5 tok/s desktop), and five agents may contend for the same CPU/RAM, distorting benchmarks.
risks.mitigation: results/.bench.lock serializes model-loading jobs; cli.py refuses to start a benchmark if psutil shows < 16 GB available or another pigemma job holds the lock; every command has --quick; the implementation order puts E1–E3 (26B) first so a complete MoE story exists even if the 31B runs are cut short.

risks.risk: Pi scripts are untested on real Pi hardware (the probed Pi is the wrong one, busy, 4 GB, SD, Hailo on the PCIe lane); 16 KB page size and RLIMIT_MEMLOCK can break pinning; OS tuning could disturb a production device.
risks.mitigation: Feasibility is read-only and exits 3 when busy; 01_os_tune is dry-run by default and refuses pciex1_gen=3 when an AI HAT occupies the bus; pin_hotset aligns to getconf PAGESIZE and checks RLIMIT_MEMLOCK and MemAvailable before any mlock; all logic that can be unit-tested lives in stdlib-only Python with fixture facts for the four configurations and for context-friend-1; shell scripts are syntax-checked and exercised inside the Docker image.

risks.risk: H2 compute/memory: dequantising 21504×5376 matrices to float32 (462 MB each) and randomized SVD/thin SVDs could exceed the < 1 h budget or RAM when run alongside benchmarks.
risks.mitigation: Process one matrix at a time, free arrays explicitly, torch.svd_lowrank with q=rank+16, niter=3; group spectral norms via np.linalg.svd(compute_uv=False) on [n_out,64] slices (fast); --quick mode (3 layers, 2 matrices, 64 tokens, q2k only); runs under the bench lock so it never overlaps a model benchmark.

risks.risk: The all-in-RAM MoE ceiling itself (~2.4 GB weight reads per token incl. the 0.6 GB tied LM head) may make even the best H1 outcome only ~3 tok/s on a Pi 5, which may disappoint relative to 'good speed'.
risks.mitigation: State it up front in README/HARDWARE_BUDGET with the arithmetic; the report lists what would change the number (speculative decoding ×1.4–1.8 measured in E2, vocabulary/head pruning, lower-bit expert quant with KLD evidence) so the conclusion is actionable rather than just negative.

designs.angle: SYSTEMS ENGINEER: bytes moved per token. The Pi runtime is a storage/page-cache problem: non-expert weights (1.6 GB) + the hottest experts must be resident and locked; cold experts stream from NVMe/USB/microSD through the kernel page cache via llama.cpp's own mmap. Everything is measured in bytes/token first, tok/s second.
designs.overview: Design for REPO_ROOT. Core finding from reading llama.cpp @ a7b94df that shapes the whole runtime: by default llama.cpp REPACKS Q4_0 weights into the "CPU_REPACK" extra buffer type (x86: Q4_0_8x8, ARM dotprod: Q4_0_4x4). Repacked tensors are COPIED out of the mmap into anonymous memory at load (llama-model.cpp:1849-1870 only uses buffer_from_host_ptr for the DEFAULT "CPU" buft -> "CPU_Mapped"). So with defaults the 14.4 GB MoE file becomes 14.4 GB of anonymous RSS, page-cache streaming is impossible, and the 12.7 s load you measured is the repack copy. Two switches exist: `-nr/--no-repack` (everything stays mmap'd, slower kernels) and the hybrid `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` which keeps attention/dense-FFN/embeddings repacked (fast, ~1.6 GB anon) and leaves ONLY the expert slabs in CPU_Mapped buffers that the page cache can evict and refill. The hybrid is the Pi runtime's default mode; everything else (hot-set pinning daemon, cache simulation, Docker --memory validation) is built around it. Second constraint from source: `cparams.warmup` makes build_moe_ffn use n_expert_used = n_expert (llama-graph.cpp:1473), so the trace tool must set params.warmup=false (eval-callback.cpp already does) or the trace is polluted. Tensor names to hook are exact: "ffn_moe_topk-<il>" (I32, ne=[8, n_tokens]), "ffn_moe_weights-<il>" (F32, ne=[1,8,n_tokens]), "ffn_moe_probs-<il>" (F32, ne=[128,n_tokens]), gemma4 FFN inputs "ffn_norm_1-<il>" (dense shared FFN), "ffn_norm_2-<il>" (MoE input) on the MoE model, and "ffn_norm-<il>" on the dense 31B (gemma4.cpp:350). The repo splits into: (1) pigemma/ Python package (GGUF byte-range planner, trace format, cache simulator, hot-set planner, device profiles, feasibility verdict, bench/quality wrappers, H2 math) fully unit-testable on Windows with synthetic GGUFs; (2) tools/ with three tiny native programs: `pigemma-probe` (one cb_eval C++ tool with modes moe-trace and act-dump), `pinner` (C, mmap+mlock byte ranges of the GGUF and hold), `membw` (C, memory bandwidth); (3) pc/ desktop drivers (PowerShell for native Windows binaries, bash for Docker runs); (4) pi/ parametric runtime scripts that collect facts -> JSON -> Python verdict and refuse heavy work when infeasible or when the host is the production ContextFriend Pi; (5) docs/. Runs today on the desktop: bench matrix (both models x threads x mmap/repack), speculative (MTP/DFlash), KLD quality, trace collection in Docker, cache sim, Docker --memory page-cache-limited validation with and without pinning, H2 oracle on 4 sampled 31B layers. Honest projections: 26B-A4B fully in RAM on a Pi 5 is bandwidth-bound at ~2.4 GB touched/token over ~10 GB/s LPDDR4X -> ~3-4 tok/s ceiling; streaming experts from NVMe Gen3 (~850 MB/s) at an LRU hit rate h costs (1-h)*803 MB/token -> every 100 MB/token missed costs ~0.12 s; dense 31B touches 17.65 GB/token -> <0.6 tok/s even at 16 GB RAM (does not fit) and ~0.05 tok/s streaming; H2 is measured as an oracle, not promised.

components.purpose: GGUF byte-range planner. Parses the header with gguf.GGUFReader and emits a map of every tensor and every expert slab as absolute file byte ranges, classified hot/cold, page-aligned for 4 KiB or 16 KiB pages (Pi kernel 6.18 uses 16 KiB).
components.interface: CLI: `python -m pigemma.gguf_map <model.gguf> --out <map.json> [--page-size 4096|16384]`. API: `build_map(path, page_size) -> GgufMap` (dataclass; `.tensors: list[TensorRange]`, `.experts: list[ExpertSlab]`, `.nonexpert_bytes`, `.expert_bytes`, `.file_size`, `.n_layer`, `.n_expert`, `.n_expert_used` read from KV keys `gemma4.block_count`, `gemma4.expert_count`, `gemma4.expert_used_count`). Expert slab rule: for tensor name matching `blk\.(\d+)\.ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps\.weight`, n_expert = shape[-1] (gguf-py keeps ggml ne order, ne[0] fastest), nb2 = n_bytes // n_expert, slab(e) = [data_offset + e*nb2, data_offset + (e+1)*nb2). Uses ReaderTensor.data_offset (absolute offset; asserted by unit test). `aligned(range, page)` floors start / ceils end. Classification: kind in {token_embd, output, attn, ffn_dense, norm_router, expert}. `expert_bytes_per_token = n_moe_layers * n_expert_used * (nb2_gate_up + nb2_down)` printed in the summary (expected 803 MB for 26B-A4B).
components.test: tests/test_gguf_map.py builds a synthetic GGUF with gguf.GGUFWriter (2 layers, 4 experts, n_embd 64, n_ff_exp 32, Q4_0 experts via gguf.quants.quantize on random data, F32 norms) and asserts: slab offsets are contiguous and cover the tensor exactly, 16 KiB alignment pads correctly, sum(kind=expert) == tensor bytes, nonexpert+expert == all tensor bytes, data_offset read back equals the writer's offset.

components.purpose: Reader/writer/validator for the binary expert-routing trace (.moetrace, format defined in data_formats) plus statistics: per-layer expert frequency, coverage curve (fraction of activations covered by the K hottest experts per layer), unique experts per token, layer-to-layer co-activation, prefill vs generation split.
components.interface: API: `TraceWriter(path, header: dict)` with `.write(token_id, pos, phase, ids: np.uint8[n_moe,8], weights: np.float16[n_moe,8], probs_top: optional)`; `TraceReader(path)` -> `.header`, `.n_tokens`, `.ids` (np.uint8 [T, n_moe, 8]), `.weights`, `.phase`, `.token_ids`; `stats(reader) -> dict` and CLI `python -m pigemma.trace stats <trace> [--json out.json] [--csv-coverage out.csv]`; `python -m pigemma.trace validate <trace>` (magic, record count vs header.token_count, ids < n_expert, 8 distinct ids per layer-token). `merge(paths) -> path` concatenates traces of the same model.
components.test: tests/test_trace_format.py: write 1000 synthetic records, read back bit-exact; validate() rejects a truncated file and a bad id; coverage curve monotone and reaches 1.0 at K=n_expert; stats on a trace with a single hot expert per layer gives coverage(K=1)=1.0.

components.purpose: Expert-cache simulator for H1. Replays a trace against a byte budget for the expert cache and computes bytes read per token and miss rate under policies LRU, LFU, STATIC_HOT (top experts by frequency from a training split of the trace, never evicted), BELADY (oracle: evict the expert whose next use is farthest), and an optional PREFETCH_PREV_LAYER variant (issue reads for layer l+1 experts chosen by the top-8 router probs of layer l if `probs_top` is present, else by the same expert ids as layer l; prefetches count as reads but are overlapped with compute in the projection). Granularity: one expert = one unit of nb2_gate_up+nb2_down bytes (3.345 MB); page-level readahead modeled by `--read-granularity` (default 128 KiB rounding up).
components.interface: CLI: `python -m pigemma.cache_sim <trace> --map <map.json> --profiles pigemma/profiles/pi5.json --policies lru,lfu,static,belady,prefetch --budgets-gb 0.5,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,12.85 --train-split 0.3 --out results/h1/sim.json`. API: `simulate(trace, map, policy, budget_bytes, read_gran) -> SimResult(bytes_per_token, miss_rate, cold_bytes, hits, misses, per_layer_miss)`; `project(sim: SimResult, profile) -> {tg_serial, tg_overlap}` where t_io = bytes_per_token / profile.storage.rand_read_mbps, t_compute = 1/profile.compute_tg_in_ram, tg_serial = 1/(t_compute+t_io), tg_overlap = 1/max(t_compute, t_io). Budget semantics: budget is the EXPERT cache only; `--total-ram-gb` mode derives it as total - profile.os_reserve - nonexpert_bytes*profile.nonexpert_overhead(1.0 for -nr, 2.0 for hybrid where repacked copy + mapped file both exist unless the mapped copy is dropped) - kv_cache_bytes(n_ctx).
components.test: tests/test_cache_sim.py: (1) infinite budget -> bytes/token = cold load only; (2) zero budget -> bytes/token = 8*n_moe*unit; (3) Belady misses <= LRU misses <= worst case on 50 random traces; (4) cyclic access pattern of size budget+1 makes LRU miss 100% and Belady not; (5) projection math known-answer.

components.purpose: Hot-set planner: turns map.json + trace stats into an ordered list of byte ranges to mlock under a RAM budget: all non-expert tensors first (mandatory), then experts by descending (frequency * bytes-saved) until budget exhausted. Output consumed by tools/pinner and by pi/06_pin_hotset.sh.
components.interface: CLI: `python -m pigemma.hotset --map map.json --trace-stats stats.json --budget-bytes N [--page-size 16384] [--no-nonexpert] --out hotset.json`. API: `plan(map, stats, budget, page) -> HotSet(ranges: list[{offset,length,kind,layer,expert,hits}], total_bytes, expert_coverage_fraction)`. Ranges are page-aligned and merged when adjacent.
components.test: tests/test_hotset.py: budget respected within one page per range; non-expert ranges always present unless --no-nonexpert; ordering by hits; adjacent experts merged into one range; coverage fraction equals sum(hits of selected)/sum(all hits).

components.language: Python 3.13+ (stdlib only; runs on the Pi)
components.purpose: Pure decision logic for the Pi feasibility verdict: given facts JSON (ram_total_mb, ram_free_mb, swap_mb, page_size, storage_type, storage_dev, free_disk_mb, pcie_gen, cpu_model, hostname, running services) and a model catalog, print a verdict table (per model/quant: FITS_IN_RAM / STREAM_EXPERTS_OK / STREAM_TOO_SLOW / NO_DISK) with the reason and the recommended quant, and exit non-zero when nothing heavy may run.
components.interface: CLI: `python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts facts.json --catalog pigemma/model_catalog.json [--want 26b|31b] [--json out.json]`. API: `verdict(facts, catalog) -> Verdict(ok: bool, rows: list[Row], recommended: Row|None, reasons: list[str])`. Rules (constants at top, documented): usable_cache = ram_total - 700 MB - nonexpert_bytes*overhead - 400 MB (KV 4k ctx q8) ; FITS_IN_RAM if file_size <= ram_total-700MB; STREAM_EXPERTS_OK if usable_cache >= 2 GB and storage in {nvme, usb-ssd}; microSD -> STREAM_TOO_SLOW always (projected <0.3 tok/s); 31B dense -> NEVER_GOOD_SPEED with the bandwidth arithmetic in the reason; refuse (`ok=False`) if hostname in protected list (context-friend-1) or free_disk < file_size*1.05 or ram_free < 1 GB.
components.test: tests/test_feasibility_verdict.py: table of fact fixtures (4GB+microSD, 8GB+USB3, 8GB+NVMe, 16GB+NVMe, protected host, no disk) -> expected verdict codes and exit status.

Variants map to flags: default = none; norepack = `--repack 0` (llama-bench) / `-nr` (completion); hybrid = `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"`; nommap = `-lm none`; mlock = `-lm mmap+mlock`. `python -m pigemma.bench completion --model ... --prompt-file prompts/he_en.txt -n 128 [--draft <gguf>] [--draft-max 3]` records tg, acceptance (parsed from 'draft acceptance rate' / 'n_accept' lines when speculative), and output text. components.purpose: Q4_0 block dequantization (block of 32: f16 scale d + 16 bytes of nibbles; value = d*(nibble-8), low nibbles are elements 0..15, high nibbles 16..31) directly from GGUF byte ranges without loading the whole file; W_base constructors for H2: `requant_q2(W)` (per-32 block symmetric 2-bit with f16 scale, 0.5625 B/elem... i.e. 2.5 bpw) and `lowrank(W, r)` via torch.svd_lowrank(q=r+32) returned as (U_r f16, V_r f16).
components.interface: API: `dequant_q4_0(buf: bytes, n_rows, n_cols) -> np.float32[n_rows, n_cols]` (ggml layout: rows = ne[1], each row = ne[0] elems contiguous); `load_tensor_f32(map, name) -> np.ndarray` (mmap read of the range); `requant_q2`, `lowrank`. Cross-checked against gguf.quants.dequantize.
components.test: tests/test_quant.py: random float matrices -> gguf.quants.quantize(Q4_0) -> our dequant equals gguf.quants.dequantize bit-exactly; requant_q2 error < Q4_0 error * 4 on Gaussian data; lowrank reconstructs a rank-r matrix exactly.

components.purpose: H2 step 1: for sampled layers of the dense 31B, load gate/up/down Q4_0 matrices, build W_base (variants q2, lowrank-256, lowrank-512), residual R = W - W_base, split R into column groups of g input columns (groups along the input/contraction dim so the bound uses x_g), precompute per-group spectral norms ||R_g||_2 (torch.linalg.matrix_norm(ord=2) via a few power iterations) and bytes per group under a chosen residual encoding (f16 and q4 of the residual).
components.interface: CLI: `python -m pigemma.h2.decompose --map map31.json --layers 5,20,35,50 --mats gate,up,down --base q2,lowrank256 --group 128 --out traces/h2/decomp/` writing per (layer,mat,base) an .npz with R (float16, memory-mapped), group_norms, base params, bytes accounting. Memory: one 5376x21504 f32 matrix at a time (462 MB).
components.test: tests/test_h2_decompose.py on a 64x256 synthetic matrix: W_base + sum(R_g) == W; group norms >= true ||R_g x_g||/||x_g|| for 100 random x (bound soundness).

components.purpose: H2 step 2: with real FFN-input activations X (from act-dump), for each token compute y = W x, y_base = W_base x, contributions c_g = R_g x_g. Oracle: add groups in descending ||c_g|| until ||y - y_hat||/||y|| <= eps for eps in {0.01,0.03,0.10}; record the fraction of residual bytes needed. Bound test: group certified-skippable when ||R_g||_2 * ||x_g||_2 <= tau_eps (tau chosen so that sum of skipped bounds <= eps*||y_base||); record certified-skip fraction, and verify soundness (actual error after skipping all certified groups <= eps). Also the baseline competitor: plain low-bit quant (q2 only, no residual) error, so H2 must beat 'just quantize lower' on the bytes-vs-error curve.
components.interface: CLI: `python -m pigemma.h2.oracle --decomp traces/h2/decomp/ --acts traces/h2/acts/31B/ --tokens 512 --eps 0.01,0.03,0.10 --out results/h2/oracle.json`. Output per (layer, mat, base, eps): {oracle_residual_fraction_mean/p90, certified_skip_fraction, oracle_skip_fraction, soundness_violations, bytes_per_token_layer, baseline_q2_rel_error}, and an extrapolation block: implied bytes/token for 60 layers = base_bytes + mean(needed residual bytes) vs the 17.65 GB Q4_0 baseline and the 8.5 GB IQ2_XXS alternative.
components.test: tests/test_h2_oracle.py: synthetic W with planted sparse large residual -> oracle finds exactly those groups; fraction monotone non-increasing in eps; soundness_violations == 0 on 200 random cases.

components.purpose: Renders results/h2/oracle.json into docs/results/H2_RESULTS.md with the bytes-vs-error table, the verdict rule applied, and projected Pi tok/s under the NVMe profile (storage-bound: bytes_per_token / 850 MB/s).
components.interface: CLI: `python -m pigemma.h2.report results/h2/oracle.json --profiles pigemma/profiles/pi5.json --out docs/results/H2_RESULTS.md`.
components.test: tests/test_h2_report.py renders a fixture JSON and checks the verdict string.

components.language: C++17 against llama.cpp common + llama (built in Docker image and on the Pi)
components.purpose: The one custom llama.cpp tool: `pigemma-probe`. Modeled on examples/eval-callback/eval-callback.cpp. Mode moe-trace: cb_eval collects 'ffn_moe_topk-<il>' (I32 [8,n_tokens]) and 'ffn_moe_weights-<il>' (F32 [1,8,n_tokens]) and optionally top-32 of 'ffn_moe_probs-<il>' for every ubatch, flushes one .moetrace record per token when the last MoE layer's topk arrives, then greedily generates N tokens (argmax over llama_get_logits_ith(ctx,-1)) and keeps tracing them with phase=1. Mode act-dump: for `--layers` writes the F32 activations of a named tensor family ('ffn_norm' for 31B, 'ffn_norm_1'/'ffn_norm_2' for 26B) as .npy per layer for the first `--tokens` tokens. Mode names: writes a list of all cb tensor names once (debug).
components.interface: Build: top-level tools/CMakeLists.txt does `add_subdirectory(${LLAMA_DIR} llama EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)` with `-DLLAMA_DIR=../third_party/llama.cpp` (Pi: ~/llama.cpp) and the probe target `target_link_libraries(pigemma-probe PRIVATE llama-common llama Threads::Threads)` exactly like examples/eval-callback/CMakeLists.txt. CLI = all common_params flags (-m, -f/-p, -t, -c, -b, -ub, -nr, -ot, -lm) parsed by common_params_parse(argc, argv, params, LLAMA_EXAMPLE_COMMON) plus probe flags consumed before parsing: `--mode moe-trace|act-dump|names --trace-out <file> --gen N --probs-top K --layers 5,20 --tokens 512 --act-out <dir> --corpus-id <str>`. Mandatory: params.cb_eval = probe_cb; params.cb_eval_user_data = &state; params.warmup = false. Decode via `common_batch batch = common_batch_get_one(ctx, tokens); llama_process(ctx, LLAMA_PROCESS_TYPE_DECODE, batch.get())`; for generation, `common_batch_get_one(ctx, &tok, 1)` per step (positions continue from memory). Callback: on ask=true return true only for names starting with the wanted prefixes (parse `-<il>` suffix with strtol after the last '-'); on ask=false, if !ggml_backend_buffer_is_host(t->buffer) use ggml_backend_tensor_get, else read t->data respecting nb[] strides. Header JSON fields filled from llama_model_meta_val_str / llama_model_n_layer and the GGUF path, file size, llama build number (LLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER). Exit code non-zero if any layer produced != n_expert_used ids.
depends_on: docker/ image for the x86 Linux build
components.test: Integration only (needs a model): `pc/trace_collect.sh --smoke` runs probe on 64 tokens of prompt + 8 generated against the 26B in Docker and `python -m pigemma.trace validate` must pass with token_count == 72 and every layer 0..29 present; `--mode names` output must contain ffn_moe_topk-0 and ffn_norm_2-0. Unit-level: a `tests/test_probe_cli.py` checks the shell wrapper builds the right argv.

components.purpose: Hot-set pinning daemon. Opens the GGUF read-only, mmap(PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED) the whole file, then for each range in hotset.json: madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) then mlock(addr+off, len) (page-aligned; aligns to sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE), 16 KiB on the Pi). Page-cache pages are shared with llama.cpp's own mmap of the same file, so pinned pages stay resident for the inference process without any llama.cpp change. Optionally madvise(MADV_RANDOM) the remaining (cold expert) ranges to stop readahead thrash. Prints locked bytes, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, and the exact fix (`ulimit -l unlimited` / limits.d / CAP_IPC_LOCK) on failure; holds until SIGTERM/SIGINT; `--once` touches+locks then exits (lock released, useful only for warmup); `--verify` re-reads mincore() per range and prints resident fraction.
components.interface: `pinner --gguf <file> --hotset hotset.json [--random-rest] [--verify] [--once] [--max-bytes N]`. Minimal JSON parsing: hotset.json is written by pigemma.hotset in a flat line-oriented form too (`hotset.ranges.txt`: one `offset length` pair per line) so pinner needs no JSON library; it reads the .txt. Exit codes: 0 locked all, 2 partial (prints how many), 3 permission.
components.test: Integration in Docker: generate a 64 MB random file, hotset of 3 ranges, run `pinner --verify` and check mincore resident == 100% for ranges and `grep Mlocked /proc/meminfo` grew by the expected amount; negative test with `ulimit -l 64` -> exit 3 with the hint.
