data_formats.name: .moetrace (expert routing trace, binary, little-endian)
data_formats.spec: File = magic 'MOETRC01' (8 bytes) | u32 header_len | UTF-8 JSON header (header_len bytes, padded with spaces to a multiple of 8) | records. Header keys (all required): format_version:1, model_name, gguf_path, gguf_size_bytes, gguf_sha256_first_16mb (hex; cheap identity), llama_build:11398, llama_commit:'a7b94df', n_layer:30, n_expert:128, n_expert_used:8, moe_layers:[0..29] (layer indices that have ffn_moe_topk; defines record order), probs_top:K (0 if not stored), corpus_id, prompt_file, created_at (ISO), token_count (patched at close; 0xFFFFFFFF while open), n_ctx, flags:[argv]. Record (fixed size = 12 + len(moe_layers)*(n_expert_used*(1+2)) + len(moe_layers)*probs_top*3 bytes): u32 token_id | u32 pos | u8 phase (0=prefill,1=generated) | u8 seq_id | u16 reserved(0) | for each il in moe_layers: n_expert_used x u8 expert_id (as output by ffn_moe_topk, order preserved = descending prob) then n_expert_used x f16 weight (from ffn_moe_weights) | if probs_top>0: for each il: probs_top x (u8 id, f16 prob) descending from ffn_moe_probs. For 26B-A4B with probs_top=0 the record is 12 + 30*24 = 732 bytes (100k tokens = 73 MB). Expert ids must be < n_expert and distinct within a layer-token; validator enforces. Sidecar `<name>.stats.json` from pigemma.trace: {token_count, prefill_tokens, gen_tokens, per_layer:{freq:[128 ints], entropy_bits, gini, coverage_at:{8:..,16:..,32:..,64:..}}, global:{unique_experts_per_token_mean, pairs_never_used, hot_set_coverage_curve:[(bytes, coverage)]}}.

data_formats.name: map.json (GGUF byte-range map)
data_formats.spec: {gguf, file_size, page_size, arch:'gemma4', n_layer, n_expert, n_expert_used, data_offset, tensors:[{name, type:'Q4_0'|'Q6_K'|'F32'..., shape:[ne0,ne1,ne2], n_bytes, offset (absolute), kind:'token_embd'|'output'|'attn'|'ffn_dense'|'norm_router'|'expert'|'other', layer:int|null}], experts:[{layer, expert, tensor:'gate_up'|'down', offset, n_bytes}], summary:{nonexpert_bytes, expert_bytes, expert_unit_bytes (gate_up+down for one expert), expert_bytes_per_token_worst}}. Offsets are byte offsets into the GGUF file; aligned ranges are computed by consumers with the given page_size.

data_formats.name: hotset.json + hotset.ranges.txt
data_formats.spec: hotset.json: {gguf, page_size, budget_bytes, total_bytes, nonexpert_included:bool, expert_coverage_fraction, ranges:[{offset, length, kind, layer, expert, hits}]} sorted by offset, page-aligned, merged. hotset.ranges.txt: same ranges, one line each `offset length` in decimal, '#' comments allowed; this is what tools/pinner reads.

data_formats.name: .npy activation dumps (H2 act-dump)
data_formats.spec: Directory traces/h2/acts/<model>/ with meta.json {model, tensor_family:'ffn_norm', layers:[...], n_tokens, n_embd, prompt_file, llama_build} and one `L<il>.npy` per layer: standard NumPy .npy v1.0 header, dtype '<f4', shape (n_tokens, n_embd), C order, written by the probe (header string: {'descr': '<f4', 'fortran_order': False, 'shape': (T, N), } padded to 64-byte alignment). For 31B: 512 tokens x 5376 x 4 B = 11 MB per layer.

data_formats.name: results JSON (one file per run)
data_formats.spec: See pigemma/results_schema.py: mandatory keys run_id, created_at, kind ('measured'|'projected'|'assumed'), host{name,os,cpu,ram_gb,page_size,storage}, llama_build, model{file,quant,bytes}, variant, flags[], threads, n_ctx; optional pp{tok_s,sd}, tg{tok_s,sd}, load_s, rss_peak_mb, mapped_mb, read_bytes_per_token, io_rbytes_per_token, accept_rate, identical_to_baseline, kld{mean,p99,top1_agree}, qa_score, output_sample, notes. Simulation outputs (results/h1/sim.json) add {trace, policy, budget_bytes, bytes_per_token, miss_rate, profile, tg_serial, tg_overlap, kind:'projected'}.

data_formats.name: facts.json (Pi feasibility input)
data_formats.spec: {hostname, kernel, page_size, cpu_model, cpu_flags:[...], ram_total_mb, ram_available_mb, swap_mb, model_dir, storage:{dev, type:'nvme'|'usb-ssd'|'microsd'|'unknown', rotational:bool, pcie_link_speed:'5.0 GT/s PCIe'|null, read_ahead_kb}, free_disk_mb, running_services:[names], memlock_limit:'unlimited'|int}. Produced by pi/lib/common.sh collect_facts; consumed by pigemma.feasibility.

data_formats.name: device profile JSON
data_formats.spec: {name, ram_gb, os_reserve_gb, mem_bw_gbps:{value,source}, storage:{type, seq_read_mbps, rand_read_3mb_mbps, rand_read_16k_iops, source}, compute_tg_in_ram:{value, source, note}, nonexpert_overhead:{norepack:1.0, hybrid:1.0}} where source in {'assumed','measured'}; measured values from results/pi/io_mem.json override on load.

experiments.hypothesis: Both Q4_0 models run end-to-end on the 8400F CPU; the MoE is compute-bound at 6 threads (~10 tok/s) while the dense 31B is memory-bandwidth-bound (~17.65 GB/token over ~50 GB/s -> ~2.5-3 tok/s). Repack vs --no-repack vs hybrid -ot differ in speed but not in output.
experiments.procedure: pc/bench_matrix.ps1 on both GGUFs: llama-bench.exe -t {4,6,12} -p 128 -n 32 -r 3 -o json for variants default / --repack 0 / -ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU" / -lm none; then llama-completion.exe -n 128 greedy per variant capturing load time, peak RSS (Get-Process PeakWorkingSet64), and the log lines 'CPU_REPACK model buffer size' / 'CPU_Mapped model buffer size' to prove which bytes are copied vs mapped.
metrics: tg32 tok/s per thread count and variant
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~40 min (31B runs dominate; each tg32 at ~2.5 tok/s is ~15 s x 3 reps x variants)
experiments.thresholds: PASS if 26B tg at 6 threads within 20% of the already-measured 9.86 tok/s and hybrid variant shows experts (~12.85 GB) as CPU_Mapped with anon RSS < 3 GB; 31B tg recorded (expected 2-3.5 tok/s, any coherent output passes). FAIL -> fix the variant flags before any streaming work, because the whole Pi runtime depends on experts staying mmap'd.

experiments.hypothesis: MTP/DFlash drafts raise generation tok/s on the CPU-bound MoE by >= 1.2x with greedy-lossless output; gains on the bandwidth-bound 31B are larger per accepted token but the draft itself is memory-bound too.
experiments.procedure: pc/spec_bench.ps1: llama-completion.exe --temp 0 -n 256 on 3 prompts (EN, HE, code) x {baseline, -md mtp, -md dflash (26B only)} x --draft-max {3,6}; verify token-identical output to baseline; record acceptance rate from the speculative summary lines.
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~25 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS (report 'useful') if speedup >= 1.2x on >= 2 of 3 prompts with identical output; else record 'no gain at this thread count' honestly. Any non-identical output with --temp 0 is a bug -> file in results notes, do not use that draft on the Pi.

experiments.hypothesis: Repack/hybrid/mmap variants are numerically identical (KLD ~ 0 vs the Q4_0 reference); lower quants degrade measurably (IQ2_XXS KLD >> Q3_K_M); both models answer the fixed Q&A set in Hebrew and English.
experiments.procedure: pc/quality.ps1: llama-perplexity.exe --save-all-logits on corpus/wiki_he_en.txt (-c 512 --chunks 20) per Q4_0 model; --kl-divergence runs for -nr, hybrid, and any downloaded lower quant (download UD-Q3_K_M and UD-IQ2_XXS of the 26B if time permits, ~22 GB); pigemma.quality qa on 12 questions with/without drafts.
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~45 min for the two Q4_0 references + variants; +30 min per extra quant
experiments.thresholds: PASS: variants KLD mean < 0.001 and top1 agreement > 99%; qa_score >= 10/12 for both models. Quant tiers for the Pi recommendation: KLD mean < 0.05 'acceptable', < 0.15 'degraded', else 'not recommended'.

experiments.hypothesis: Expert routing on real text is skewed: per layer, a hot set of ~32-48 of 128 experts covers >= 70% of activations, and the skew is stronger in early/late layers; Hebrew and code use partly different experts than English.
experiments.procedure: pc/trace_collect.sh: pigemma-probe --mode moe-trace in Docker (-nr -c 4096 -t 6) over EN (~30k tok), HE (~15k), code (~10k) corpora in 2048-token chunks with --gen 256 per chunk; merge; pigemma.trace stats.
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~60-90 min in Docker (first GGUF read through the bind mount is slow; prefill at ~40 tok/s via -nr)
experiments.thresholds: Trace PASS = validate() ok, >= 50k prefill + >= 2k generated tokens, all 30 layers present. Hypothesis signal: coverage@32 >= 0.70 averaged over layers = 'strong skew' (hot-set pinning worth it); 0.5-0.7 'moderate'; < 0.5 'near-uniform' (LRU alone is the plan).

experiments.hypothesis: At an expert-cache budget of ~5 GB (Pi 5 8 GB hybrid mode) LRU achieves >= 60% hit rate on real text (bytes/token <= ~320 MB), making NVMe Gen3 streaming ~1.5-2.5 tok/s; the 4 GB/microSD config is < 0.3 tok/s under every policy; 16 GB holds everything.
experiments.procedure: pigemma.cache_sim on traces/26b/all.moetrace with policies lru,lfu,static,belady,prefetch, budgets 0.5..12.85 GB, read granularity 128 KiB, train split 30% for static/LFU priors; project with the four Pi profiles (assumed values flagged) and the desktop profile.
metrics: projected tg_serial and tg_overlap per Pi profile (kind=projected)
experiments.runtime_estimate: < 10 min CPU
experiments.thresholds: Decision rule for the Pi recommendation: a config is 'viable for streaming' if projected tg_overlap >= 2.0 tok/s and tg_serial >= 1.0 tok/s with LRU (no oracle). Report Belady as the upper bound only. If LRU bytes/token > 1.5x Belady, prefetch/static policies are worth implementing on the Pi.

experiments.hypothesis: The simulator's LRU bytes/token predicts real page-cache behaviour within +-30% when the cache budget equals the cgroup limit minus anon RSS.
experiments.procedure: pc/pagecache_limit.sh: 26B GGUF copied into a Docker volume; llama-completion hybrid (-ot experts=CPU, -t 6, -n 64, --temp 0, same prompt as a trace chunk) under --memory {3,4,5,6,8} GB; measure cgroup io.stat rbytes and /proc/<pid>/io read_bytes deltas over the generation phase, tg tok/s, anon RSS; compare bytes/token with cache_sim lru at budget = limit - anon_rss - 300 MB.
metrics: measured read bytes per generated token
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~60 min (5 limits x ~3 min incl. cold start; 9p copy ~15 min once)
experiments.thresholds: PASS if |sim/measured - 1| <= 0.30 for limits 4-8 GB. If measured >> sim, suspect readahead (check read_ahead_kb in the VM, re-run with pinner --random-rest) or repack leakage (verify CPU_Mapped line). If measured << sim, the kernel is keeping more than the limit (check memory.stat file vs anon) - adjust the budget formula, document.

experiments.hypothesis: mlock-pinning non-expert weights plus the hottest experts (from E3) beats plain LRU at the same memory limit by >= 15% tok/s and fewer bytes/token, because LRU otherwise evicts always-needed attention/dense weights under pressure.
experiments.procedure: Same as E5 at --memory 5 and 6 GB with and without tools/pinner holding hotset(budget = limit - 2.3 GB) in the same container; pinner --verify before the run; pinner --random-rest on.
metrics: resident fraction of pinned ranges after the run (mincore)
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~25 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS if pinned tg >= 1.15x unpinned at 5 GB OR bytes/token reduced >= 20%. If no gain, document that Linux LRU already protects the hot pages and drop pinning from the Pi default (keep as optional).

experiments.hypothesis: For the dense 31B, W = W_base + sum R_g with a cheap base (2-bit or rank-256) needs only a minority of residual bytes per token to keep FFN output error <= 3%, and the norm bound ||R_g||*||x_g|| certifies a useful share of the skippable groups - AND this beats simply using a lower quant on the bytes-vs-error curve. Expected honest outcome: the bound is loose (certifies far less than the oracle) and the bytes saved do not approach what a Pi needs.
experiments.procedure: pc/h2_actdump.sh dumps 'ffn_norm-<il>' for layers {5,20,35,50}, 512 tokens of mixed corpus; pigemma.h2.decompose builds q2 and lowrank256 bases with group 128 and spectral norms; pigemma.h2.oracle computes oracle residual fraction at eps {1%,3%,10%}, certified-skip fraction, soundness, baseline q2-only error; report extrapolates bytes/token to 60 layers and Pi NVMe tok/s.
metrics: oracle residual byte fraction (mean, p90) per eps
implied bytes/token vs 17.65 GB (Q4_0) and 8.5 GB (IQ2_XXS)
experiments.runtime_estimate: act-dump ~20 min (31B prefill 512 tokens at ~10 tok/s + load); decompose+oracle ~25 min for 4 layers x 3 matrices (dequant 460 MB each, svd_lowrank, 512-token matmuls)
experiments.thresholds: 'Promising' only if at eps=3% the oracle residual fraction <= 25% AND certified-skip >= 50% of the oracle's skips AND implied bytes/token < 8.5 GB (i.e. beats IQ2_XXS at comparable error). Otherwise 'not supported by data at this scale' - still a valid result. Regardless, state the projected Pi speed: bytes_per_token / 850 MB/s (NVMe) -> any number > 2 GB/token is < 0.5 tok/s.

experiments.hypothesis: The Pi scripts are correct before a Pi exists: verdict logic, flag selection, safety refusals.
experiments.procedure: pytest on feasibility fixtures (4GB+microSD must print STREAM_TOO_SLOW and exit non-zero; protected hostname refuses); bash -n / shellcheck on pi/*.sh; the same tools/CMakeLists.txt builds in Docker; a 'fake facts' run of pi/00_feasibility.sh with PIGEMMA_FACTS_FILE override.
experiments.runtime_estimate: 5 min
experiments.thresholds: All green; later on the real Pi: 03_bench_io_mem numbers replace 'assumed' in the profile and E4 projections are recomputed with kind=measured inputs.

implementation_order: 0. (orchestrator, 10 min) Freeze docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md, map.json and results schema text from this design so lanes A-D code against the same formats.

1. LANE A (Python core, no models): pigemma/gguf_map.py -> trace.py -> cache_sim.py -> hotset.py -> profiles + model_catalog + feasibility.py -> results_schema.py, with tests. First deliverable (gguf_map on the real 26B file, prints 803 MB/token) within the first hour; unblocks hotset and sim.

2. LANE B (native tools, Docker): tools/CMakeLists.txt + probe.cpp (--mode names first to confirm tensor names, then moe-trace, then act-dump) -> pinner.c -> membw.c -> pc/build_tools_docker.sh. Smoke trace on 64 tokens as soon as it links.

3. LANE C (desktop measurements, starts immediately, independent): pigemma/bench.py + results writer -> pc/bench_matrix.ps1 (E0 on 26B now, 31B when download completes) -> pc/spec_bench.ps1 (E1) -> pigemma/quality.py + corpus + qa_set -> pc/quality.ps1 (E2).

4. LANE D (H2 math, synthetic first): pigemma/quant.py -> h2/decompose.py -> h2/oracle.py -> h2/report.py with synthetic tests; switches to real acts when LANE B's act-dump exists and the 31B is on disk (E7).
5. LANE E (Pi runtime + docs): pi/lib/common.sh -> 00..06 scripts -> docs/*.md + README skeleton; depends only on feasibility.py API and catalog from LANE A.
6. Integration (after A+B): pc/trace_collect.sh full run (E3) -> cache_sim + hotset (E4) -> pc/pagecache_limit.sh (E5, then E6 with pinner).
7. Results + docs: pigemma.results summarize -> docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>.md, H1_RESULTS.md, H2_RESULTS.md; README updated with Measured / Projected / Assumed tables and the Pi recommendation.

Parallelism: A, B, C, D, E run concurrently (5 agents). Critical path: B(probe) -> E3 -> E4/E5/E6 (~3 h). C and D are independent of the trace. The 31B-dependent items (E0-31B, E7 act-dump) are scheduled last in their lanes to absorb the download.

risks.risk: Repacking silently copies weights out of the mmap (CPU_REPACK buffers), so 'streaming experts from storage' never happens and RSS equals the whole file; results would look like the model 'fits'.
risks.mitigation: Hybrid `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` (experts -> default CPU buft -> CPU_Mapped via buffer_from_host_ptr; llama-model.cpp:1849-1870) or `-nr`. E0 asserts the 'CPU_Mapped model buffer size' log line covers ~12.85 GB and anon RSS < 3 GB before any streaming experiment. On the Pi, measure the compute penalty of non-repacked experts separately (05_bench variants) and report it.

risks.risk: Trace pollution: with warmup enabled llama.cpp routes to ALL experts (n_expert_used = n_expert when cparams.warmup, llama-graph.cpp:1473); ubatch splitting reorders when records are flushed.
risks.mitigation: probe sets params.warmup=false, flushes per ubatch on the last MoE layer's topk, keeps a token cursor, and the validator rejects any layer-token with != 8 distinct ids or ids >= 128. Smoke test compares token_count to tokens fed + generated.

risks.risk: Docker Desktop (WSL2) bind mounts over 9p/virtiofs are slow and the VM disk may lack 16 GB for a volume copy; page-cache accounting inside a cgroup may differ from a bare-metal Pi (file pages charged to the cgroup, readahead settings of the VM).
risks.mitigation: pagecache_limit.sh checks VM disk free first and falls back to the bind mount for bytes/token measurement only (time numbers flagged 'not representative'); read bytes measured two ways (cgroup io.stat and /proc/pid/io); results carry kind + notes; the real validation is repeated on the Pi via 05_bench/06_pin.

risks.risk: Pi kernel uses 16 KiB pages: hotset ranges and mlock must align to 16 KiB; expert slab boundaries (2,230,272 and 1,115,136 bytes) are not 16 KiB aligned, so adjacent experts share pages; RLIMIT_MEMLOCK defaults are tiny.
risks.mitigation: All alignment uses the runtime page size (getconf PAGESIZE / sysconf), map.json records page_size, pinner merges adjacent ranges and reports partial locks with exit code 2; 01_tune_os.sh installs limits.d memlock unlimited and 06_pin checks `ulimit -l` first.

risks.risk: Pi feasibility: the probed Pi (4 GB, microSD, production ContextFriend services, PCIe lane used by Hailo) is the wrong one and must not be touched; the right Pi's RAM/storage are unknown.
risks.mitigation: Every pi/*.sh sources assert_safe_host (refuses hostname context-friend-1 and any host running the ContextFriend service names unless PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1), collects facts and requires a passing verdict before downloading/building/running; verdict text names the recommended config (16 GB + NVMe Gen3) and gives the arithmetic for 8 GB + NVMe streaming.

risks.risk: Honesty risk: projected Pi tok/s rests on assumed storage/memory bandwidth and an assumed in-RAM compute ceiling; readers may read projections as measurements.
risks.mitigation: results schema forces kind in {measured, projected, assumed}; profiles carry per-field source; docs/RESULTS_TEMPLATE separates the three columns; projections are recomputed automatically once pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh writes measured values.

risks.risk: MTP/DFlash speculative paths may not work for gemma4 on the CPU build or may change outputs; acceptance-rate log lines may differ from the parser's expectation.
risks.mitigation: E1 verifies token identity under --temp 0 and records 'unavailable' with the exact error instead of failing the run; parser fixtures are captured from the real binary on the first run and checked in.

risks.risk: H2 compute/memory on the desktop: dequantizing 5376x21504 matrices (462 MB f32 each), SVD, and 512-token products for 4 layers x 3 matrices x 2 bases could exceed the 1-hour budget or RAM if done carelessly.
risks.mitigation: One matrix at a time, float32, torch.svd_lowrank (randomized), memory-mapped f16 residuals, --layers/--tokens/--group configurable with an ETA printed and a refusal above 8 layers without -Force; synthetic unit tests keep the pipeline correct before the big run.

risks.risk: 31B download still finishing; 63 GB free on D: must also hold the KLD reference logits (hundreds of MB), extra quants (~22 GB if downloaded) and traces.
risks.mitigation: Scripts check free space before writing; extra-quant downloads are optional in E2; the Docker volume copy is only made if the VM disk has room; results and traces are small (< 1 GB).

risks.risk: cb_eval slows inference (scheduler evaluates node-by-node) and reading large tensors (ffn_moe_probs 128 x n_tokens f32) per layer adds overhead; traces of 50k+ tokens could take hours.
risks.mitigation: probe returns true on ask only for the few wanted names; probs capture is opt-in (--probs-top); corpora are chunked at 2048 tokens with -ub 512; the smoke run reports tok/s so the full run can be sized to the time budget.

risks.risk: gguf-py API details (ReaderTensor.data_offset absolute vs relative, shape order) could be misread and shift every byte range by the header size.
risks.mitigation: tests/test_gguf_map.py round-trips a synthetic GGUF written with GGUFWriter and compares offsets against the writer; gguf_map also cross-checks the first Q4_0 block scale of one expert by dequantizing and comparing with gguf.quants.dequantize on the reader's tensor.data view.

designs.angle: RESEARCH-FIRST: H1 (MoE small active set) and H2 (dense staged residuals) are the heart. Everything else (bench, Pi runtime) exists to feed them with real numbers or to make them deployable. Every result file separates measured / projected / assumptions.
designs.overview:
pi-gemma4 is a Python-first experiment repo (package `pigemma/`) that leans on the already-built llama.cpp b11398 (commit a7b94df) and adds only three tiny C/C++ pieces. KEY DESIGN DECISION: the Windows prebuilt bundle (third_party/llama.cpp-win) has llama-bench/-completion/-perplexity/-quantize but NO llama-eval-callback and there is no Windows compiler, so the desktop tracer is `pigemma/llamadll.py` + `pigemma/tracer.py`: a ctypes binding to the prebuilt `llama.dll`/`ggml.dll` that installs `llama_context_params.cb_eval` and reads host tensors directly (zen4 kernels, reads D: natively, no Docker bind-mount). The same trace format (PGT1) is produced by a ~300-line C++ `tools/trace/pigemma-trace.cpp` that builds against llama.cpp via CMake in the Docker image and on the Pi; it is used for the page-cache-limited proxy run (where /proc/self/io byte counting per token is needed) and is the fallback if ctypes misbehaves.

Pipeline (desktop, today): (0) `pc/run_all.ps1` runs the bench matrix for both GGUFs (llama-bench thread sweep -t 4,6,8,12 with -o json; llama-completion greedy runs with and without `-md` MTP/DFlash drafts; peak working set via psapi; load time from llama perf log; PPL via llama-perplexity --chunks 8 -c 512; 20-item EN/HE Q&A set). (1) `pigemma.tracer` collects expert-routing traces of the 26B-A4B on a mixed EN/HE/code corpus in teacher-forced mode (~8k tokens) and free-running greedy mode (~1.5k tokens), optionally with router logits. (2) `pigemma.trace_stats` computes frequency skew, per-layer entropy, LRU stack-distance curves, token-adjacent reuse, working sets, cross-layer predictability; `pigemma.cache_sim` replays LRU/LFU/static-hot/Belady/prefetch at Pi RAM budgets using exact expert slab sizes from `pigemma.ggufmap`; `pigemma.pi_model` turns bytes/token into projected tok/s for 5 named Pi configs with explicit assumptions. (3) `pc/docker_proxy.sh` validates the simulator: the C++ tracer replays the SAME fixed token stream (teacher-forced, ubatch 1) inside `docker run --memory=<N>` against a model copied into a Docker volume and records bytes actually read from storage per token. (4) `pigemma.h2` captures FFN-input activations of the 31B at 6 sampled layers (teacher-forced + free-running), dequantizes the real Q4_0 matrices with gguf-py, builds W_base (2/3-bit group quant or low-rank) + group-major residual column groups with spectral-norm bounds, and measures oracle residual-byte fraction vs error, bound tightness and certified-skip rate, with an iso-byte uniform-quant control; an optional end-to-end bracket uses llama-quantize --tensor-type to make a "W_base only at sampled layers" GGUF and llama-perplexity --kl-divergence vs saved Q4_0 logits. (5) `pi/` ships parametric bash scripts: feasibility verdict (RAM/storage/free space/host deny-list), OS tuning (dry-run by default), native build, fio+membw bench, resumable fetch with quant selection, run/bench, and hot-set pinning (`tools/pin/pin_ranges.c` mlocks GGUF byte ranges = non-expert tensors + hottest experts from the trace). Honest framing throughout: the 26B-A4B is the realistic Pi tier (projected 3-5 tok/s all-in-RAM on 16 GB, bandwidth-bound; ~1-2 tok/s streaming on 8 GB+NVMe); the dense 31B cannot be fast on a Pi 5 8 GB and H2 is a measurement of how much residual must be read, not a speed promise.

components.purpose: GGUF header -> byte-range map. Uses gguf.GGUFReader (ReaderTensor.name, .shape, .tensor_type, .n_bytes, .data_offset). Classifies tensors: expert (`blk.N.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight`, `blk.N.ffn_down_exps.weight`, also ffn_gate_exps/ffn_up_exps if split), nonexpert (everything else). For expert tensors computes per-expert slab ranges: slab_bytes = n_bytes / ne[2]; expert e of layer N occupies [data_offset + e*slab_bytes, data_offset + (e+1)*slab_bytes). Derives n_layer, n_moe_layers (layers having ffn_gate_inp), n_expert, n_expert_used (from GGUF KV gemma4.expert_count / expert_used_count), expert_bytes_per_layer (gate_up slab + down slab, e.g. 2.23+1.115 MB), nonexpert_total_bytes, per-token resident traffic estimate (output head + attention + dense FFN + norms; token_embd counted as 1 row).
components.interface: CLI `pigemma-ggufmap summary <gguf> [--json out]` prints the table (tensor class, count, bytes, %). `pigemma-ggufmap hotset <gguf> --stats results/h1_stats_<trace>.json --budget-bytes B [--per-layer-min 8] -o results/hotset_<model>_<B>.ranges` -> writes ranges file (format in data_formats): all nonexpert tensor ranges first, then experts in descending global frequency (weight-mass optional `--by weight`) until budget, guaranteeing at least --per-layer-min experts per layer. Python API: `load_map(path) -> GgufMap` with fields above and `expert_range(layer, expert) -> list[(offset, length)]` (two ranges: gate_up and down), `tensor_range(name)`.
components.test: tests/test_ggufmap.py: build a tiny synthetic GGUF with gguf.GGUFWriter (arch 'gemma4', 2 layers, tensors blk.N.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight Q4_0 ne=[64,32,4], blk.N.ffn_down_exps.weight Q4_0 ne=[32,64,4], blk.N.ffn_gate_inp.weight F32 [64,4], token_embd.weight F16 [64,16]); assert slab offsets = data_offset + e*n_bytes/4, nonexpert bytes, hotset respects budget and per-layer-min, ranges non-overlapping and inside file.

components.interface: `class Llama(model_path, n_ctx=4096, n_batch=512, n_ubatch=512, n_threads=6, load_mode='mmap', cb=None)`; `.tokenize(text, add_bos=True, parse_special=True) -> np.int32`; `.detokenize(tokens) -> str`; `.decode(tokens: np.int32, n_past: int, logits_all=False) -> np.ndarray|None` (chunks by n_batch, sets positions n_past.., returns logits of last token or all as float32 [n, n_vocab] view copies); `.greedy_next(logits) -> int`; `.clear_memory()`; `.set_callback(cb: Callable[[ggml_tensor_ptr, bool], bool])` wraps into CFUNCTYPE and keeps a reference. Helper `tensor_view(t) -> (name:str, type:int, ne:tuple, nb:tuple, np.ndarray|None)` returning a numpy view for F32/I32/F16 host tensors using nb strides (np.ndarray(shape=reversed ne, dtype, buffer from address, strides=reversed nb)). Self-check at init: after creating the context assert llama_n_ctx(ctx)==n_ctx and llama_n_threads(ctx)==n_threads (detects struct misalignment early); after first decode assert callback fired >= 1 time when a cb is set.

components.purpose:
The desktop cb_eval tracer. Two capture sets: ROUTING (26B): on ask-phase returns True only for names in {ffn_moe_topk-<il>, ffn_moe_weights_norm-<il>} (+ ffn_moe_logits-<il> when --logits, + ffn_norm_2-<il> when --moe-input); on data-phase reads I32 [K, n_tok] and F32 [K, n_tok] (nb strides), keeps a per-layer running token counter (each layer sees the same tokens in order; counter += ne[1]) and emits PGT1 records sorted by weight desc. ACTIVATIONS (31B or 26B): names ffn_norm-<il> (F32 [n_embd, n_tok], input to gate/up) and ffn_gate_par-<il> (F32 [n_ff, n_tok], input to down) for layers in --layers, appended as f16 rows to traces/<name>.acts/<tensor>.f16 with an index JSON. Modes: `teacher` (feed corpus tokens as prompt in chunks of --ubatch; 512 default, or 1 to mimic decode kernels), `generate` (prompt via Gemma chat template `<start_of_turn>user
{p}<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
`, greedy or --temp with seed, n tokens, stops at EOG; records mode=1 for generated tokens, mode=0 for the prompt). Optional `--save-logprobs` writes f16 log_softmax rows per output token (512 KB/token) for offline KLD between two runs. Writes .meta.json (model, sha prefix, llama commit/build, host, mode, prompt/corpus sha, sampler, n_ubatch, wall ms per token array, tensor names captured).

components.purpose: H1 statistics from one or more PGT1 traces (optionally split train/test by token index or by trace file). Computes per layer and global: expert frequency f[l][e], Gini, entropy H_l (bits, vs log2(128)=7), effective experts exp(H), coverage curve cov[l][n] for n in {8,16,24,32,48,64,96,128} (fraction of selections and of routing weight mass covered by the top-n experts); LRU stack-distance histogram per layer and global (distance = number of distinct (layer,expert) items touched since the previous touch of this item) -> exact LRU hit-rate curve hit(C) for any cache size C in items; token-adjacent reuse P(e in S_{t+1} | e in S_t), Jaccard(S_t,S_{t+1}) mean; working set: distinct experts per layer per window W in {16,64,256,1024} (median, p95) and bytes; cross-layer predictability: conditional table P(e' in S_{l+1} | top1_l = e) from train split, precision@8/@16 on test split vs static-top-16 baseline and vs 'same ids as layer l' baseline; mutual information I(top1_l; top1_{l+1}); mode comparison teacher vs generate and per-corpus-language JS divergence of f[l]; if logits present: margin p8-p9 distribution and weight mass of the 8th expert (soft-skip opportunity).
components.interface: CLI `pigemma-stats traces/26b_teacher_mixed.pgt [more.pgt] --train-frac 0.7 -o results/h1_stats_<name>.json [--csv-dir results/h1_csv/] [--plots]`. Python: `compute(records_dense, meta, train_frac) -> dict` (schema pigemma.h1_stats.v1). Plots optional (matplotlib if importable, else skipped with a note).
components.test: tests/test_trace_stats.py: synthetic Zipf trace (make_synth_trace(T,L,K,alpha,seed) in tests/synth.py): uniform routing -> entropy≈7 bits, Gini≈0; alpha=1.5 -> top-32 coverage > uniform; stack-distance-derived LRU hit curve equals cache_sim LRU hit rate within 1e-9 for 3 budgets (the key cross-check); predictor precision@16 >= static baseline on a trace with injected layer-to-layer correlation.

components.purpose: Expert-cache simulators over a PGT1 trace with exact per-expert bytes from ggufmap (gate_up slab + down slab, 3.345 MB for 26B Q4_0; item = one expert of one layer; both slabs fetched on a miss). Policies: lru, lfu (aging factor param, ties by recency), static_hot (top-N by train-split frequency or weight mass; no replacement), belady (offline optimal using next-use index), lru_prefetch (after layer l of token t, prefetch predicted experts for l+1 from the conditional table; counts prefetch bytes and wasted prefetch separately), lru_per_layer (budget split equally per layer; control), and `pagecache_approx` (LRU with readahead granularity param to emulate kernel readahead inflation, default 128 KB). Budget in bytes; warm-start option (cache pre-filled with static hot set). Metrics per run: hit_rate, weighted_hit_rate (by routing weight), bytes_per_token mean/p50/p95/max, miss_count_per_token, unique_items_touched, cold-start bytes, and a per-token time series (npz).
components.interface: CLI `pigemma-sim traces/26b_gen.pgt --gguf 26b-q4 --policies lru,lfu,static_hot,belady,lru_prefetch --budgets-gb 1.2,2.5,4.9,6.0,13.0 [--train traces/26b_teacher_mixed.pgt] -o results/cache_sim_<name>.json [--series results/cache_sim_<name>.npz]`. Python: `simulate(trace_dense, bytes_per_item_fn, policy, budget_bytes, **opts) -> SimResult`.
components.test: tests/test_cache_sim.py: on synthetic traces: belady hit_rate >= lru >= lru_per_layer; hit rate monotone non-decreasing in budget; budget >= all items -> hit_rate==1 after cold start and bytes_per_token==0 steady state; budget < one item -> 0 hits; lru_prefetch with perfect oracle predictor -> bytes_per_token equals lru bytes (just shifted) and wasted==0; bytes accounting equals misses*3.345e6 for a constant-size fn.

components.language: Python (no numpy; runs on stock Pi python3)
components.purpose: Transparent performance model for Pi 5 configurations. Named configs: pi5-4gb-sd (4 GiB, microSD 60 MB/s seq, 2 ms access), pi5-8gb-usb3 (8 GiB, 350 MB/s, 0.5 ms), pi5-8gb-nvme-g2 (8 GiB, 450 MB/s, 0.2 ms), pi5-8gb-nvme-g3 (8 GiB, 800 MB/s, 0.15 ms), pi5-16gb-nvme-g3 (16 GiB, 800 MB/s). Shared assumptions (overridable, and replaced by measured values from results/pi_bench_<host>.json when present): ram_bw_eff 12 GB/s, compute_gflops_eff 80 (4xA76 dotprod), os_reserve 1.0 GiB (0.7 on 4 GiB), compute_buffers 0.3 GiB, kv_bytes(ctx) for Gemma4-26B (≈8 KB/token/sliding layer x25 capped at window 1024 + 2 KB/token x5 global layers), thinking disabled. Formula per token: t = max(resident_bytes/ram_bw, flops/compute) + miss_bytes/storage_bw + n_misses*access_latency; expert cache budget = RAM - os_reserve - nonexpert_resident - kv - compute_buffers. Prints MEASURED (from inputs), PROJECTED (outputs) and ASSUMPTIONS blocks separately; also prints the all-in-RAM ceiling (e.g. 26B: ~2.4 GB resident traffic/token -> 3-5 tok/s) and the dense-31B line (17.65 GB/token -> streaming at 800 MB/s = ~22 s/token; H2 with 2-bit base + 25% residual still ~11 s/token).

components.purpose: Load one tensor by name from a GGUF via gguf.GGUFReader (np.memmap, random access, no full read) and dequantize Q4_0 (and Q6_K/Q8_0 if needed) to float32 using gguf.quants.dequantize(tensor.data, tensor.tensor_type); returns W with shape (n_out, n_in) i.e. y = W @ x; verifies shape against ne. Also provides `quantize_q4_0_like(W) -> W_hat` and generic `group_quant(W, bits, block=32) -> (W_hat, bytes_per_elem)` symmetric absmax per block (bits 2,3,4) used for W_base and for residual-group quantization.
components.interface: `load_matrix(gguf_path, name) -> np.ndarray float32 (n_out,n_in)`; `ffn_names(layer) -> dict(gate='blk.L.ffn_gate.weight', up='blk.L.ffn_up.weight', down='blk.L.ffn_down.weight')`; `group_quant(W, bits, block=32)`; `bytes_per_elem(bits, block)` = bits/8 + 2/block.
components.test: tests/test_q4dequant.py: write random F32 matrix, quantize with gguf.quants.quantize(..., Q4_0), write tiny GGUF, load_matrix returns (n_out,n_in) and matches gguf.quants.dequantize reference bit-exactly; group_quant(bits=4) error <= Q4_0-equivalent; bytes_per_elem(4,32)==0.5625.

components.purpose: Builds W = W_base + R with residual split into input-column groups. W_base variants: `qk_g32` (k in {2,3}; symmetric block-32 group quant of W), `lowrank_r` (randomized SVD via torch.svd_lowrank(q=r+32, niter=2), stored f16, bytes=(n_in+n_out)*r*2), `qk_g32+lowrank_r` (low-rank on the quant residual). Residual R = W - W_base (f32) is grouped by column blocks of g input dims (g=64 default -> 84 groups for n_in=5376, 336 for n_in=21504); each R_g is quantized to the residual precision (`res_bits` 8 or 4, block 32) and stored group-major so one group = one contiguous read; bytes_g recorded. Bounds: spectral norm ||R_g||_2 via torch.linalg.matrix_norm(ord=2) (exact; also Frobenius for comparison).
components.interface: `decompose(W, base='q2_g32', g=64, res_bits=8) -> Decomp` with fields W_base_hat (f32), base_bytes, groups: list of (col_slice, R_g_hat f32 [n_out,g], bytes_g, norm2_g, normF_g), total_residual_bytes. `apply_base(dec, x)`, `group_contribs(dec, x) -> [G, n_out]` (all c_g = R_g x_g, computed as one matmul per group batch), `bounds(dec, x) -> b_g = norm2_g*||x_g||`.
components.test: tests/test_h2_decompose.py (random 256x512 matrices): sum of all group contribs + base == W x within 1e-3 rel when res_bits=16 (no residual quant); bounds b_g >= ||c_g|| for 1000 random x (never violated); lowrank_r=full rank reproduces W; bytes accounting = sum of group bytes + base bytes.

components.purpose: Per-token selection experiments. Reference y_ref = W_q4 x (what llama.cpp computes). For each token: err_base = ||y_ref - W_base x||/||y_ref||. ORACLE: sort groups by ||c_g|| desc, add until rel error <= tau for tau in {0.05,0.02,0.01}; record k_oracle(tau), residual-bytes fraction, and the full error-vs-bytes curve (fractions 0,0.05,...,1). BOUND-SELECT: sort by b_g desc; certified skip: largest skipped set S with sum_{g in S} b_g <= tau*(||W_base x|| - sum_S b_g) (lower bound on ||y_ref||); record certified fraction and the realized error; tightness ratios ||c_g||/b_g (median, p10, p90) and Spearman rank correlation between b_g and ||c_g||. ISO-BYTE CONTROL: for byte budgets equal to {uniform q2, q3, q4 full-read}, compare rel error of uniform group-quant (bits 2,3) vs base+oracle vs base+bound-select at the same bytes. Aggregates per layer/matrix (mean, p95 over tokens) separately for teacher-forced vs free-running activations.
components.interface: `run_token_batch(dec, X[n_tok,n_in], W_ref, taus) -> dict of arrays`; `aggregate(results) -> dict` (schema pigemma.h2.v1 with measured/assumptions blocks); implied Pi bytes/token = 60 layers x (base_bytes + selected residual bytes extrapolated from sampled layers) + attention/head bytes from ggufmap (labelled PROJECTED/EXTRAPOLATED).
components.test: tests/test_h2_oracle.py: with res_bits=16 the oracle at tau=0 selects all groups and error->0; a matrix whose residual is concentrated in 10% of columns -> oracle fraction <= 0.15 at tau=0.01 while bound-select finds the same groups (precision 1.0); tightness in [0,1].

components.purpose: Orchestrates E4: reads activation captures (traces/31b_acts_teacher/ and traces/31b_acts_gen/ index JSON), for each sampled layer loads gate/up/down via q4dequant one layer at a time (≈1.4 GB f32 per layer; frees before next), builds decompositions for the configured base variants, runs oracle on gate/up with X = ffn_norm-<il> rows and on down with X = ffn_gate_par-<il> rows, writes results/h2_<name>.json + CSV curves + optional PNGs. Config file h2_config.yaml-like JSON: layers [5,15,25,35,45,55], max_tokens_per_mode 256/128, g 64, bases ['q2_g32','q3_g32','lowrank_512'], res_bits 8, taus. Optional `--bf16-control`: downloads only the safetensors shard containing one sampled layer (via huggingface_hub hf_hub_download of model.safetensors.index.json then the single shard, ~3-5 GB) to report Q4_0-vs-bf16 error for that layer as the quantization-loss yardstick; skipped if the repo is gated or offline.

components.purpose: Hot-set pinning daemon for the Pi: opens the GGUF read-only, mmap(MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ) the whole file, reads the .ranges file, rounds each range out to the system page size (getpagesize(), 16 KB on the probed Pi), mlock()s each range, touches pages, reports resident bytes via mincore(), prints totals, then pauses (sigsuspend) until SIGTERM so the pages stay locked while llama.cpp (which mmaps the same file -> same page cache) runs. Refuses to pin if total > --max-bytes or > MemAvailable - reserve (reads /proc/meminfo). Never touches other processes.

components.purpose: E3 page-cache-limited proxy. Step 1 (one-time): copy the 26B GGUF into Docker volume `pigemma-models` (bind mount is too slow for mmap faults): `docker run -v pigemma-models:/models -v D:/...:/work ... cp /work/models/.../gemma-4-26B_q4_0-it.gguf /models/` (prints progress; ~14.4 GB). Step 2: for each memory limit in {6g, 8g, 12g, 20g(=all fits)}: `docker run --rm --memory=<M> --memory-swap=<M> --cpus=6 -v pigemma-models:/models:ro -v D:/...:/work pi-gemma4-build vmtouch -e /models/<gguf>` then run `pigemma-trace -m /models/<gguf> --tokens-file /work/traces/fixed.tokens.bin -ub 1 -t 6 --out /work/traces/proxy_<M>.pgt --io-csv /work/traces/proxy_<M>.io.csv`, capturing cgroup memory.stat (file, file_mapped) before/after. Step 3 (optional, probed): `--device-read-bps <dev>:<bps>` using the volume's block device major:minor to emulate microSD/USB3/NVMe bandwidth; if the cgroup io controller rejects it under WSL2, print a clear SKIP and proceed. Step 4: `pigemma-sim` on traces/26b_gen.pgt (the same token stream) at budget = M - resident nonexpert - buffers, and `pigemma.proxy_compare` writes results/proxy_<M>.json with measured bytes/token (from io.csv, excluding the first 200 warm-up tokens), simulated LRU and Belady bytes/token, ratio and readahead inflation estimate.

components.purpose: Shared helpers: detect_ram_gib (/proc/meminfo MemTotal), mem_available_gib, detect_storage <path> -> class (microsd|usb|nvme-g1|nvme-g2|nvme-g3|unknown) via findmnt -T + /sys/block/<dev>/ (mmcblk*, sd* with /sys/block/sd*/device/../../../ usb, nvme* with current_link_speed under /sys/bus/pci/devices), free_disk_gib <path>, cpu_flags (asimddp, i8mm, sve from /proc/cpuinfo), page_size, load_avg, is_production_host (hostname in DENY_HOSTS or any systemd unit matching PROTECTED_SERVICES active), require_not_production <stage>, json_kv emitter, verdict printer (colour + plain), die with exit codes (2 GO-STREAMING, 3 NO-GO, 4 REFUSED-PRODUCTION-HOST).

data_formats.name: PGT1 routing trace (traces/<name>.pgt)
data_formats.spec: Little-endian binary. HEADER 64 bytes: bytes 0-3 magic 'PGT1'; 4-7 u32 version=1; 8-11 u32 n_layer (total transformer layers, 30 for 26B); 12-15 u32 n_moe_layers; 16-19 u32 n_expert (128); 20-23 u32 n_expert_used K (8); 24-27 u32 n_embd (2816); 28-31 u32 flags (bit0 has_weights, bit1 has_generated_tokens, bit2 weights_are_normalized); 32-35 u32 record_size (= 8 + 2K + 2K = 40 for K=8); 36-43 u64 n_records (patched on close; 0 while streaming); 44-63 reserved zero. RECORDS, one per (token, MoE layer), in token-major then layer-ascending order: u32 token_index (0-based position in the trace's token stream = index into .tokens.bin); u16 layer (il); u8 mode (0 = teacher-forced/prompt token, 1 = generated token); u8 pad=0; K x u16 expert ids sorted by routing weight descending; K x f16 normalized routing weights (from ffn_moe_weights_norm-<il>, sum ≈ 1) — present only if has_weights, otherwise record_size = 8 + 2K. Invariants: every (token_index, moe layer) appears exactly once; expert < n_expert.

data_formats.name: Trace sidecars (traces/<name>.meta.json, traces/<name>.tokens.bin)
data_formats.spec: tokens.bin: raw int32 little-endian token ids in stream order (prompt tokens then generated), length == max(token_index)+1. meta.json keys: schema 'pigemma.trace_meta.v1', created (ISO-8601), tracer ('python-ctypes'|'cpp'), llama_commit 'a7b94df', llama_build 11398, model {id, path, size_bytes, sha256_prefix, arch 'gemma4', n_layer, n_expert, n_expert_used}, host (sysinfo.collect()), mode ('teacher'|'generate'), n_ubatch, n_threads, n_ctx, corpus [{path, sha256, n_tokens}] or prompts [{id, sha256, n_prompt_tokens, n_generated}], sampler {type:'greedy'|'temp', temp, seed}, captured_tensors [names], has_logits (bool, logits file traces/<name>.logits.f16 = per MoE layer, per token, n_expert f16 router softmax probs, layout [token][layer][expert]), wall_ms_per_token [floats], callback_overhead_ms_per_token (float), notes.

data_formats.name: Activation capture (traces/<name>.acts/)
data_formats.spec: Directory with index.json {schema 'pigemma.acts.v1', model, mode, layers [ints], tensors {'<name>-<il>': {file, dtype 'f16', n_cols, n_rows}}, token_index_per_row [ints], mode_per_row [0|1], meta: same as trace meta}. Each file '<name>-<il>.f16' is n_rows x n_cols float16 row-major (row = one token, appended in processing order). Dense 31B names: 'ffn_norm-<il>' (n_cols = n_embd 5376, input to gate/up) and 'ffn_gate_par-<il>' (n_cols = n_ff 21504, input to down). MoE optional: 'ffn_norm_2-<il>' (MoE input, 2816).

data_formats.name: Hot-set ranges (results/hotset_<model>_<budget>.ranges)
data_formats.spec: UTF-8 text. Line 1: '# pigemma-ranges v1 file=<basename> size=<bytes> budget=<bytes> source=<stats json or nonexpert-only>'. Then one range per line: '<offset_bytes> <length_bytes> <label>' where label is the tensor name for non-expert tensors or 'blk.<L>.exp<E>.gate_up' / 'blk.<L>.exp<E>.down' for expert slabs; ranges are absolute file offsets (data_offset-based), non-overlapping, sorted by offset; comment lines start with '#'. pin_ranges rounds each to page boundaries at runtime.

data_formats.name: Result JSON envelope (all results/*.json)
data_formats.spec: Every result file: {schema: 'pigemma.<kind>.v1', created, host: sysinfo, llama_commit, llama_build, model: {id, path, size_bytes, sha256_prefix, quant}, params: {...run parameters...}, measured: {...only numbers that were measured on this host...}, projected: {...derived numbers, each with 'from' listing which measured/assumption keys it used...}, assumptions: {...every constant used, with units...}, notes: [strings]}. Kinds: bench (measured: llama_bench [{n_threads, n_prompt, n_gen, avg_ts, stddev_ts}], completion [{draft:null|'mtp'|'dflash', prompt_tps, gen_tps, load_ms, n_draft, n_accept, accept_rate, peak_working_set_bytes, peak_private_bytes}], nommap_peak_bytes), qa ({n_pass, n_total, items:[{id, lang, pass, output}]}), ppl ({ppl, ppl_err, chunks, n_ctx}), kld ({mean_kld, p99_kld, top1_agree}), ggufmap (tensor classes/bytes, expert_bytes_per_layer, nonexpert_resident_bytes, per_token_resident_traffic_bytes), h1_stats (per-layer arrays described in trace_stats), cache_sim ({runs:[{policy, budget_bytes, hit_rate, weighted_hit_rate, bytes_per_token:{mean,p50,p95,max}, misses_per_token, prefetch_bytes_per_token, wasted_prefetch_bytes_per_token}]}), pi_projection ({configs:{name:{budget_bytes, tok_s_projected, s_per_token_breakdown:{ram, compute, storage_bytes, storage_access}}}}), proxy ({memory_limit_bytes, measured_bytes_per_token, sim_lru_bytes_per_token, sim_belady_bytes_per_token, ratio_measured_over_lru, readahead_inflation_est}), h2 (per layer/matrix/base/mode: err_base, oracle_fraction_at_tau{0.05,0.02,0.01}, oracle_curve[{bytes_frac, rel_err_mean, rel_err_p95}], bound_certified_fraction_at_tau, bound_tightness{p10,p50,p90}, spearman_bound_vs_actual, iso_byte_control[{bytes_per_elem, uniform_err, oracle_err, bound_err}], implied_pi_bytes_per_token PROJECTED), pi_bench, feasibility ({ram_gib, mem_available_gib, storage_class, link_speed, free_disk_gib, cpu_flags, page_size, production_host, verdicts:[{model, fits_in_ram, streaming_needed, class, reasons[]}], verdict, exit_code}).

data_formats.name: pigemma/fetch_table.json
data_formats.spec: {models: {'26b-q4': {repo:'google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf', file:'gemma-4-26B_q4_0-it.gguf', size_bytes, family:'26b', quant:'q4_0', draft:'26b-mtp'}, '26b-iq3xxs': {repo:'unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF', file:..., size_bytes ~11.4e9}, '26b-iq2xxs': {...9.9e9}, '31b-q4': {...17.65e9}, '31b-iq2xxs': {...8.5e9}, '26b-mtp': {...}, '31b-mtp': {...}}, selection: [{ram_gib_min:15, storage:['nvme-g3','nvme-g2','usb','microsd'], pick:'26b-q4', mode:'in-ram'}, {ram_gib_min:7.5, storage:['nvme-g3','nvme-g2'], pick:'26b-q4', mode:'streaming', alt:'26b-iq3xxs'}, {ram_gib_min:7.5, storage:['usb'], pick:'26b-iq3xxs', mode:'streaming'}, {ram_gib_min:0, storage:['*'], pick:null, mode:'no-go', force_pick:'26b-iq2xxs'}]}. Exact unsloth filenames must be filled from the HF listing at implementation time (not guessed).

data_formats.name: corpus/qa_set.jsonl item
data_formats.spec: {id:'qa07', lang:'he'|'en', prompt:'...', kind:'contains'|'regex'|'number', expect:['substring1','substring2'] | ['regex'] | ['42', tolerance], note:'...'}. Scoring: contains = any expected substring present (case/nikud-insensitive); regex = re.search; number = first number in the stripped output within tolerance.

data_formats.name: C++/Python tracer CLI contract for replay
data_formats.spec: Both tracers accept '--tokens-file <path>' (int32 stream) and process it teacher-forced with positions 0..N-1 in ubatch chunks; both write PGT1 + meta + copy the tokens.bin next to the output; the C++ one additionally writes '<out>.io.csv' with header 'tok,read_bytes_delta,rchar_delta,majflt_delta,wall_ms'.

experiments.hypothesis: Both GGUFs run end-to-end on the 6c/12t desktop CPU; thread count, speculative drafts and mmap vs no-mmap change tok/s and footprint measurably; outputs are coherent in EN and HE.
experiments.procedure: pc/run_all.ps1 S1-S4: ggufmap summaries; llama-bench -t 4,6,8,12 -p 128 -n 32 -r 3 -o json for 26b-q4 and 31b-q4 (31b: -t 6,12 only); llama-completion greedy -n 128 with fixed prompt, variants none/-md mtp/-md dflash (26b) and none/-md mtp (31b), peak working set via psapi, load time from perf log; --no-mmap variant once per model; Q&A 20 items per model; llama-perplexity -c 512 --chunks 8 on corpus/ppl_mixed.txt per model. All loads are warm-cache (documented).
metrics: pp tok/s and tg tok/s per thread count (mean, stddev)
gen tok/s with/without MTP and DFlash, draft accept rate, speedup ratio
peak working set bytes (mmap) and peak bytes (--no-mmap)
experiments.thresholds: Sanity: 26b tg at best threads >= 8.0 tok/s (reference 9.86±1.1 measured earlier) else investigate the environment before trusting anything else; 31b tg: report only (expected 2-4 tok/s). Speculative: 'useful on CPU' if gen speedup >= 1.15x with accept rate >= 0.5, otherwise record 'no gain'. Quality: Q&A >= 16/20 for each model (coherence gate); PPL recorded as the reference for later quant comparisons.
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~25 min total: 26B bench ~3 min, 31B bench ~6 min, completion variants ~6 min, Q&A 2 models x 20 x ~10 s ≈ 7 min, PPL 2 x ~3 min.

experiments.hypothesis: Routing traces of the 26B-A4B can be captured on the desktop with < 10% overhead via cb_eval, in both teacher-forced and free-running modes, and are internally consistent.
experiments.procedure: pigemma-trace --model 26b-q4 --mode teacher on corpus en/he/code, max 8192 tokens, --ubatch 512 (and a 512-token --ubatch 1 control to confirm routing is kernel-independent); pigemma-trace --mode generate on 6 prompts x 256 tokens greedy with --logits; validate() both; also save traces/fixed.tokens.bin from the generate run (prompt+generated, used by E3). Integration test compares --logits top-8 against recorded experts.
metrics: callback overhead ms/token and tok/s with tracer vs plain
experiments.thresholds: PASS if agreement >= 99% on both checks, overhead <= 15% of tok/s, >= 8000 teacher tokens and >= 1200 generated tokens collected.
experiments.runtime_estimate: teacher 8k tokens at ~50 tok/s ≈ 3 min; generate 1.5k tokens at ~8.5 tok/s ≈ 3 min; plus 2 loads ≈ 30 s.

experiments.hypothesis: H1: expert selection is skewed and temporally reusable enough that a Pi-sized cache of experts (≈4.9 GB on an 8 GB Pi) serves most expert reads from RAM, cutting bytes streamed per token from the 803 MB worst case to a level NVMe Gen3 can serve at > 1 tok/s; cross-layer routing is predictable enough to prefetch.
experiments.procedure: pigemma-stats on teacher + generate traces (train 70% / test 30% by token index); pigemma-sim with policies lru,lfu,static_hot,belady,lru_prefetch,lru_per_layer at budgets computed by pi_model for pi5-4gb-sd (≈1.2 GB), pi5-8gb-* (≈4.9 GB), pi5-16gb (≈13 GB = all 12.85 GB experts fit) plus 2.5 and 6.0 GB; pigemma-pimodel projections for all 5 configs; compare teacher vs generate stats (JS divergence) and EN vs HE segments.
metrics: per-layer entropy bits and effective experts
coverage of top-16/32/64 experts per layer (selection and weight mass)
LRU stack-distance hit curve; hit rate and weighted hit rate per policy/budget
cross-layer predictor precision@16 vs static baseline
projected tok/s per Pi config with assumption list
experiments.thresholds: H1 'viable on 8 GB+NVMe-G3' if LRU hit rate at 4.9 GB >= 0.60 AND bytes/token p50 <= 320 MB (model: ≥ ~1.5 tok/s); 'strong skew' if top-32/layer covers >= 60% of selections; prefetch worth building if predictor precision@16 >= 0.5 and lru_prefetch reduces stall bytes >= 20% at <= 1.3x total read bytes; 'static hot set sufficient' if static_hot is within 10% of LRU. If LRU hit at 4.9 GB < 0.40, report H1 as not viable for the 8 GB tier (only 16 GB all-in-RAM).
experiments.runtime_estimate: stats < 1 min; sim: 6 policies x 6 budgets over 9.5k tokens x 30 layers x 8 = 2.3 M accesses, pure Python with dicts ≈ 2-4 min (Belady precomputes next-use index); projections instant.

experiments.hypothesis: The cache simulator's LRU bytes/token predicts real storage reads of llama.cpp when the OS page cache is constrained to a Pi-like budget (Linux page cache ≈ LRU plus readahead).
experiments.procedure: pc/docker_proxy.sh: copy 26B GGUF into Docker volume; for memory limits 6g, 8g, 12g, 20g run vmtouch -e then pigemma-trace (C++) replaying traces/fixed.tokens.bin with -ub 1 -t 6, recording read_bytes per token (/proc/self/io) and major faults; discard first 200 tokens; compare with pigemma-sim lru/belady at budget = limit - 1.6 GB resident - 0.5 GB buffers on the same token stream; optional --device-read-bps throttle probe for sd/usb3/nvme bandwidth emulation (skip with message if unsupported under WSL2).
metrics: simulated LRU and Belady bytes/token at the matching budget
C++ vs Python trace expert-set agreement on the same tokens
tok/s under throttle (if supported) vs pi_model prediction using the throttle bandwidth
experiments.thresholds: PASS if 20g run shows ~0 bytes/token when warm (sanity) and for 6g/8g the measured bytes/token lies within [0.8 x Belady, 1.3 x LRU]; if measured > 1.3 x LRU, report the readahead inflation factor and feed it to pagecache_approx. Throttled tok/s within ±35% of pi_model prediction (if throttle works) validates the time model.
experiments.runtime_estimate: copy 14.4 GB into volume ~5-10 min once; each limit run: 1.5k tokens at -ub 1 ≈ 3-4 min + cold load ≈ 25 min for 4 limits.

experiments.hypothesis: H2: for the dense 31B, a cheap W_base (2-3 bit group quant or low-rank) plus a small oracle-selected subset of residual column groups reproduces the Q4_0 FFN outputs within 1-5% relative error using far fewer residual bytes than the full residual; the norm bound ||R_g||·||x_g|| can certify a useful fraction of the skips. Controls: iso-byte uniform quant; teacher-forced vs free-running activations; (optional) bf16 shard for quantization-loss yardstick.
experiments.procedure: pigemma-trace --model 31b-q4 --acts --layers 5,15,25,35,45,55 teacher (256 tokens mixed corpus) and generate (128 tokens, 2 prompts); pigemma-h2 with bases q2_g32, q3_g32, lowrank_512; g=64; res_bits 8; taus 0.05/0.02/0.01; per layer x {gate, up, down} x base x mode compute err_base, oracle curves, bound certification/tightness/Spearman, iso-byte control at the byte levels of uniform q2/q3; extrapolate implied Pi bytes/token (labelled PROJECTED) for 60 layers; optional --bf16-control on layer 15.
metrics: oracle residual-byte fraction at tau 5/2/1% (mean, p95 over tokens)
certified-skip fraction at each tau and realized error
iso-byte: uniform-quant error vs oracle vs bound-select at equal bytes
implied bytes/token on Pi (projected) and the honest s/token at 800 MB/s
experiments.thresholds: H2 'promising' if at tau=2% oracle needs <= 35% of residual bytes AND bound-select achieves >= 50% of the oracle's byte saving at the same error; 'bound useless' if tightness p50 < 0.1 and certified fraction < 10% at tau=2%; 'no advantage' if at equal bytes uniform q3 error <= 1.2x the oracle error (then the whole scheme loses to plain lower-bit quantization). Regardless of outcome, the report states the implied s/token on a Pi 5 8 GB (expected >> 1 s/token).
experiments.runtime_estimate: acts capture ≈ 2 min (31B prompt ~7 tok/s) + 2 loads ≈ 1 min; dequant 18 matrices ≈ 1 min; randomized SVD 18 x ≈ 15 s ≈ 5 min; oracle 384 tokens x 18 matrices ≈ 3 min; total ≈ 15 min, under the 1 h budget with margin (configurable layers/tokens).

experiments.hypothesis: Replacing the FFN of the 6 sampled layers with W_base only (no residual) measurably degrades the model (upper bound of H2 loss); the full Q4_0 is the lower bound; the oracle sits between but cannot be run end-to-end without custom kernels.
experiments.procedure: llama-quantize models/.../gemma-4-31B_q4_0-it.gguf models/h2base_31b.gguf q4_0 --allow-requantize --tensor-type 'blk\.(5|15|25|35|45|55)\.ffn_(gate|up|down)=q2_k' (verify the exact pattern syntax from tools/quantize/quantize.cpp usage); pigemma-quality kld-base --model 31b-q4 (llama-perplexity --save-all-logits, -c 512 --chunks 8, 2.1 GB file); pigemma-quality kld on h2base.gguf (--kl-divergence-base + --kl-divergence); also PPL of both.
metrics: mean KLD, p99 KLD, top-1 agreement of h2base vs Q4_0
experiments.thresholds: Report only; context line: mean KLD < 0.05 is typical of a good quant, > 0.3 is severe. If mean KLD of W_base-only is already < 0.05, the residual is unnecessary for those layers (strong negative result for H2's premise).
experiments.runtime_estimate: requant 17.6 GB ≈ 10 min; two perplexity passes of 4096 tokens at ~7 tok/s ≈ 10 min each; ≈ 35 min.

experiments.hypothesis: The Pi runtime makes a correct feasibility decision and refuses heavy work on an unsuitable or production host, without touching running services.

implementation_order: WAVE 0 (one agent, ~30 min, blocks nothing else because the formats are fully specified here): pyproject.toml, pigemma/paths.py, pigemma/sysinfo.py, pigemma/trace_format.py + tests, tests/synth.py, pigemma/ggufmap.py + tests (synthetic GGUF), docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md, corpus/ files.

WAVE 1 (5 agents in parallel, 1.5-2.5 h): A) pigemma/llamadll.py + pigemma/tracer.py + layout tests, then run E1 on 26B as soon as it works (produces traces/ and fixed.tokens.bin that E3 and E4 need). B) pigemma/bench.py + pigemma/quality.py + pc/run_all.ps1 + fixtures/tests, then run E0 (independent of everything else; can start immediately). C) pigemma/trace_stats.py + pigemma/cache_sim.py + pigemma/pi_model.py + pigemma/fetch_table.json + tests on synthetic traces (does not need real traces until wave 2). D) pigemma/h2/* (q4dequant, decompose, oracle, run_h2) + tests on random matrices; smoke-run q4dequant on one real 31B tensor as soon as the download finishes. E) tools/trace/pigemma-trace.cpp + CMakeLists, tools/pin/pin_ranges.c, tools/membw/membw.c, pc/build_linux.sh (build in Docker), pi/pi_config.env, pi/lib.sh, pi/00..06 scripts + fixture tests, docs/PI_RUNBOOK.md.

WAVE 2 (after A and C finish, ~1 h, 3 agents): run E2 (stats, sim, projections) on the real traces; run E4 acts capture with A's tracer on the 31B then D's pigemma-h2; run E3 (pc/docker_proxy.sh: volume copy first, then limits) using E's C++ tracer and A's fixed.tokens.bin; execute E6 dry-run on context-friend-1 (feasibility only).

WAVE 3 (one agent, ~45 min): pigemma/report.py + docs/RESULTS.md from real results; README.md, docs/HYPOTHESES.md, docs/HARDWARE_BUDGET.md, docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md with measured numbers cited; optional E5 bracket if time remains (requant + KLD ≈ 35 min, run in background).

Integration gates: (1) tests pass on Windows without models (`pytest`); (2) `pytest -m model` smoke tests pass for tracer (26B 32 tokens) and h2 (layer 15, 16 tokens); (3) Python vs C++ trace agreement on 64 tokens reported; (4) every results/*.json validates against the envelope (measured/projected/assumptions present).

risks.risk: ctypes struct mirror of llama_context_params / ggml_tensor is misaligned against the prebuilt llama.dll (b11398) -> silent garbage, callback never fires, or crash.
risks.mitigation: Field lists are copied from include/llama.h lines 365-425 and ggml.h 685-716 at the exact commit (sizes asserted: 336 / 160 / 88 bytes); runtime self-checks (llama_n_ctx and llama_n_threads round-trip, callback-fired assertion on first decode, defaults n_batch==2048/n_ubatch==512); fallback path is the C++ tracer in Docker with the model copied into a volume (same PGT1 output).

risks.risk: Windows prebuilt bundle lacks llama-eval-callback and there is no Windows compiler; Docker bind-mount reads of 14-18 GB GGUFs are slow.
risks.mitigation: Desktop tracing is done via ctypes on native Windows (reads D: directly). Docker is used only for E3 with the model copied once into a named volume (ext4 inside the VM); Docker VM has 31 GB RAM so the 14.4 GB 26B fits in page cache for the 20g sanity run.

risks.risk: Greedy generation diverges between the Windows zen4 build and the Docker/Pi builds (different kernels, rare near-ties), invalidating cross-platform comparisons.
risks.mitigation: All cross-platform replays are teacher-forced from traces/fixed.tokens.bin (int32 stream); routing agreement is measured and reported rather than assumed; E3 compares bytes/token of the same token stream.

risks.risk: cgroup io throttling (--device-read-bps) may be unsupported under Docker Desktop/WSL2, and kernel readahead + llama.cpp's mmap prefetch (MADV_WILLNEED) inflate measured reads relative to the simulator.
risks.mitigation: Throttle is an optional probed step; the primary E3 metric is bytes/token under a memory limit, compared against a band [0.8 x Belady, 1.3 x LRU]; readahead inflation is estimated and fed into the pagecache_approx policy; results state the inflation factor explicitly.

risks.risk: 31B runs are slow on the desktop (≈2-4 tok/s gen, ≈7 tok/s prompt) so E4/E5 could blow the 1-hour budget; the KLD base logits file is 2.1 GB per 8 chunks because vocab is 262144.
risks.mitigation: E4 sampling is configurable (default 6 layers, 256+128 tokens ≈ 15 min); E5 is optional and runs in the background; chunks limited to 8 at -c 512; disk check before writing logits.

risks.risk: H2 may simply lose to plain lower-bit quantization at equal bytes, or the norm bound may be too loose to certify anything (expected ~1/sqrt(64) ≈ 0.125 tightness for random directions).
risks.mitigation: This is a legitimate outcome: the iso-byte control and the tightness distribution are first-class metrics with explicit 'no advantage' / 'bound useless' thresholds, and the report states them as findings. The design also records Spearman rank correlation so a loose-but-well-ordered bound can still be useful as a ranking heuristic.

risks.risk: Even a perfect H1 cache cannot make the Pi 5 fast: all-in-RAM 26B is bandwidth-bound at ~2.4 GB resident traffic/token (3-5 tok/s projected), and the dense 31B streams 17.65 GB/token (≈22 s/token at 800 MB/s). Expectations ("Gemma 4 32B at good speed") may be disappointed.
risks.mitigation: pi_model prints the ceiling arithmetic in every projection with the assumptions block; HYPOTHESES.md and README state the non-promise up front; the recommendation (Pi 5 16 GB + NVMe Gen3, MoE 26B-A4B, optionally UD-IQ3_XXS for headroom) is surfaced by feasibility and docs.

risks.risk: Running anything heavy on the wrong Pi (context-friend-1: 4 GB, microSD, production ContextFriend services) could disturb production.
risks.mitigation: DENY_HOSTS + PROTECTED_SERVICES in pi_config.env; lib.sh require_not_production gates every heavy stage (exit 4); feasibility is read-only; scripts never kill/restart anything; E6 verifies no change in active units before/after.

risks.risk: 16 KB kernel pages on the Pi and unaligned expert slabs (2.23 MB / 1.115 MB) make pinning over-include bytes; mlock may fail on memlock limits.
risks.mitigation: pin_ranges rounds to getpagesize() and reports the overhead; 01_tune_os sets memlock limits (dry-run by default); pin refuses when total exceeds MemAvailable - reserve.

risks.risk: Warm page cache on the 64 GB desktop (both GGUFs fit) makes 'load time' and 'footprint' measurements optimistic and non-reproducible.
risks.mitigation: Reported as warm-load explicitly; the --no-mmap run gives the bytes-if-fully-read figure; cold behaviour is measured only in Docker (vmtouch -e) and on the Pi.

risks.risk: Gemma 4 emits a thinking channel (<|channel>thought ... <channel|>) that can consume the generation budget and confuse Q&A scoring.
risks.mitigation: quality.py strips the channel before scoring and uses -n 256 for Q&A; outputs are kept raw in the JSON for audit.

risks.risk: Unsloth alternative quant filenames / HF ETag-sha256 behaviour may differ from assumptions; the Pi has ~10 MB/s internet (≈24 min per 14 GB).
risks.mitigation: fetch_table.json filenames are filled from the live HF listing at implementation time; curl -C - resumable with retries and size check; sha256 verified only when the header provides it; dry-run shows the selection without downloading.

risks.risk: Several agents implementing the PGT1 writer twice (Python, C++) drift.
risks.mitigation: Normative spec in docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md + this design; the Python reader validates a C++-produced fixture in CI; constants (magic, header 64 B, record 8+4K) are asserted in tests on both sides.

judgments.rationale: Judged as the person who must produce evidence today and then hand a working runtime to a Pi. Design 1 (index 1) wins because it is the only design whose central mechanism is actually true at the pinned commit: llama.cpp repacks Q4_0 into CPU_REPACK anonymous buffers by default (llama-model.cpp:1849-1856 mmaps only the default buft; repack.cpp covers AVX2/AVX512 and NEON+dotprod including MUL_MAT_ID), so without `-nr` or the hybrid `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` there is no page-cache streaming, hot-set pinning pins pages nobody reads, and every memory-capped proxy run OOMs. Designs 0 and 2 both build their Pi runtime, their pinning daemon and their Docker validation on that false premise; they would discover it mid-afternoon as an OOM and lose the validation experiment, and their 8 GB Pi path would simply crash. Design 1 also gets warmup pollution (llama-graph.cpp:1473), the `-lm` load-mode flags, real bytes/token measurement (cgroup io.stat + /proc/pid/io), the pinned-vs-unpinned A/B, the mandatory measured/projected/assumed `kind`, and the H2 iso-byte competitor right. Its one verified defect — speculative decoding through `llama-completion -md`, which this build rejects — is fixed by grafting Design 0's llama-server harness (timings.draft_n/draft_n_accepted, spec_type_effective fallback), and its H2 down-matrix input gap is closed by also capturing `ffn_gate_par` and adding Design 0's `ffn_out` sanity check. From Design 2 graft the fixed.tokens.bin replay, the stack-distance LRU curve cross-check, the cross-layer predictability stats, `ffn_moe_weights_norm`, and the teacher-vs-free-running / Spearman / bf16-yardstick controls; keep the ctypes tracer off the critical path. Design 0 scores highest on getting the desktop bench/quality numbers today with the least yak-shaving (correct speculative route, disk gating, lock file, fixtures incl. the probed Pi), but its evidence would stop at the first `--memory` cap and its Pi tier would not stream. Design 2 has the best science and the richest H1/H2 analytics but the highest implementation risk (hand-mirrored ctypes structs with a 14 GB model loaded) and the same repack blind spot. Winner: index 1, implemented with Design 0's server-based speculative harness and Design 2's replay and statistics grafted in.

H2 activation capture hooks `ffn_gate_par-<il>` for the down-matrix input; gemma4's dense FFN (GELU+PAR) emits `ffn_geglu-<il>` instead and never reaches the ffn_gate_par branch, so the down oracle and the ffn_out sanity check get no data until renamed

Claims `ffn_moe_weights-<il>` are post-normalisation weights summing to 1; it is the pre-norm ggml_get_rows output (sum < 1). The post-norm tensor is `ffn_moe_weights_norm` (norm_w=true for gemma4). The golden-fixture 'sum to 1±1e-3' test would fail as written

Trace corpus is tiny (6 prompts × ~500 tokens + 128 generated ≈ 4k tokens) for 3840 slabs; StaticHot fit/test split and steady-state hit rates at a 1500-slab budget will be noisy.
