H2 act-dump captures only `ffn_norm-<il>`; the oracle on the down matrix needs the geglu output (`ffn_geglu-<il>`, not ffn_gate_par) or must recompute gelu(Wg x)·(Wu x) from dequantized gate/up — unspecified, and the recomputed input would not match llama.cpp's Q8 activation path exactly

`compute_tg_in_ram: 3.5 (assumed)` is a bare guess feeding the projection's compute term; it is not derived from the measured desktop numbers or the membw result, and the 'LRU hit h → (1-h)×803 MB' arithmetic ignores the resident-weight RAM traffic in tg_overlap

pinner `--random-rest` (MADV_RANDOM on cold ranges) is ineffective: madvise applies to the calling process's VMAs, not to llama.cpp's own mapping; llama-mmap.cpp uses MAP_POPULATE + MADV_WILLNEED on the full file, so load under a RAM cap churns the whole file (numa=on disables prefetch — not mentioned)
E3 trace collection (55k prefill + 2k gen tokens, -nr, through the 9p bind mount, 60-90 min) sits on the critical path for E4/E5/E6; no --quick corpus tier is defined for a 'result today' fallback

`--mmap` variant naming (`-lm none`) and `nommap` RSS measurement are fine, but bench.py's 'load time from llama_perf_context_print lines' + PeakWorkingSet on Windows mixes mapped and private bytes without the WorkingSet/PrivateBytes split Design 0 reports

The .moetrace header is free-form JSON padded to 8 bytes with token_count patched at close — fine, but no reader-side inference from file size if the writer dies; expert ids as u8 and weights as f16 are adequate but the trace drops ffn_moe_weights_norm (stores pre-norm weights) without saying so

best_ideas: ctypes binding to the prebuilt llama.dll for a native Windows cb_eval tracer (no Docker, reads D: directly, zen4 kernels). Struct mirrors verified correct against include/llama.h and ggml.h at a7b94df: ggml_tensor sizeof 336 / data@248 / name@256, llama_context_params sizeof 160 / cb_eval@88; batch_ext_init/add_token/set_pos/set_output_logits + llama_process all exist. Runtime self-checks (n_ctx/n_threads round-trip, callback-fired assert) are the right guards
Teacher-forced vs free-running capture modes with a `--ubatch 1` vs 512 control (routing must be kernel-independent) and `--logits` top-8(softmax) == recorded-experts consistency check (>= 99%)
Stack-distance histogram → exact LRU hit curve, cross-validated against the simulator to 1e-9 — an independent check that the simulator is correct

Cross-layer predictability (P(e' in S_{l+1} | top1_l), precision@8/16 vs static-top-16 and vs same-ids baselines, mutual information) — the only design that measures whether router-of-previous-layer prefetch has signal before modeling it
Weighted hit rate (by routing weight) and the 8th-expert weight-mass / p8–p9 margin as a soft-skip opportunity metric

H2 controls: iso-byte uniform quant, bound tightness p10/p50/p90 + Spearman(b_g, ||c_g||), explicit expected looseness ~1/sqrt(g), optional bf16 single-shard yardstick, and the E5 end-to-end bracket via llama-quantize --tensor-type (flag verified) + KLD
fixed.tokens.bin replay so Windows and Linux/Pi tracers process the identical token stream; cross-platform expert-set agreement is reported as a number, not assumed
C++ tracer writes per-token io.csv (read_bytes, rchar, majflt, wall_ms) — the right primary signal for a page-cache proxy; `--device-read-bps` throttle as an optional probed step with explicit SKIP
pi/lib.sh testable under Git Bash via PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC fixture dirs; pi_config.env as the single parameter surface; DENY_HOSTS + PROTECTED_SERVICES with exit 4
flaws: Repack blind spot (fatal for E3 as written): docker_proxy.sh runs the C++ tracer with default settings, so the 14.4 GB model is repacked into anonymous memory and the 6g/8g/12g runs OOM; the 20g 'sanity' run shows ~0 reads for the wrong reason. pin_ranges pins file pages the inference process never touches. No -nr/-ot anywhere
Hooks `ffn_gate_par-<il>` for the 31B down-matrix input; gemma4 emits `ffn_geglu-<il>` and never reaches the gate_par branch — down oracle has no data until renamed
bench.py uses `llama-completion -md` (invalid for COMPLETION) and a `--no-mmap` variant (flag removed; `-lm none`), and pi/05_run.sh uses `--mlock if fits` (removed; `-lm mmap+mlock`)

ctypes is inherently high-variance: a misdeclared argtype or a Python exception inside the CFUNCTYPE callback is a silent crash of the host process; llama_model_params sizeof claimed 88 is actually 80 (self-catching, but shows the mirror was not fully checked); Python callback overhead on ask=true for every graph node adds ~thousands of round-trips per token
Two writers of PGT1 (Python + C++) with acknowledged drift risk, and the C++ tracer is still required for E3, so the ctypes shortcut saves Docker only for E1/E4
Pi tier scripts are parametric and safe but inherit the invalid flags and lack the hybrid -ot streaming mode, so the GO-STREAMING verdict for 8 GB + NVMe cannot be delivered as specified

E3 pass band [0.8×Belady, 1.3×LRU] is well-chosen but would be evaluated on the broken mechanism; pi_model's ram_bw_eff 12 GB/s and compute_gflops_eff 80 are assumed with no on-device calibration path until membw runs

judgments.rationale:
Judged as a skeptical ML-systems reviewer after verifying the load-bearing claims against third_party/llama.cpp @ a7b94df and the real GGUF headers.

DECISIVE FINDING. Design 1's core claim is true and the other two designs are blind to it: llama-model.cpp:1849-1856 mmaps (buffer_from_host_ptr) only tensors on the DEFAULT CPU buft; repack.cpp picks q4_0_8x8 on AVX2 / q4_0_4x4 on NEON+dotprod and supports MUL_MAT_ID, so every Q4_0 expert slab (12.85 GB) is copied into CPU_REPACK anonymous memory at load. Consequences: Design 0's E6 (`docker --memory 5g` on a 14.4 GB model) and Design 2's E3 would OOM instead of streaming; both pin daemons would mlock file pages the inference process never reads; both Pi 'STREAM_NVME / GO-STREAMING' verdicts are undeliverable as specified. Design 1 gates everything on the 'CPU_Mapped model buffer size' log line and uses `-nr` in Docker and hybrid `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` on the Pi — the only mechanically workable streaming mode among the three. `-nr`, `-ot`, `-lm` verified; `--mlock`/`--no-mmap` verified gone.

OTHER VERIFIED FACTS THAT MOVED SCORES. (1) gemma4's dense FFN (GELU+PAR) takes the ggml_geglu_split branch and emits `ffn_geglu-<il>`, never `ffn_gate_par`; Designs 0 and 2 hook the wrong name for the 31B down-matrix activations. (2) `-md` is wired only for SPECULATIVE/SERVER/CLI/IMATRIX; Designs 1 and 2 pass it to llama-completion (invalid); Design 0 correctly routes speculative work through llama-server and checks timings.draft_n (verified present). (3) `ffn_moe_weights` is pre-normalisation; Design 0's 'sum to 1' claim/test is wrong (norm_w=true for gemma4 → `ffn_moe_weights_norm` exists, as Design 2 uses). (4) Design 2's ctypes struct mirrors are exactly right for ggml_tensor (336/248/256) and llama_context_params (160, cb_eval@88); llama_model_params is 80 not 88. (5) Design 0's GGUF constants are right except the expert-total (12846366720, not 12846034944). (6) `--save-all-logits` aliases `--kl-divergence-base`; quantize `--tensor-type` exists; eval-callback indeed prints 3 elements/dim and sets warmup=false. (7) Caveat for all three: llama-mmap.cpp uses MAP_POPULATE + MADV_WILLNEED on the whole file; under a RAM cap this churns the file at load, and madvise from a separate pinner process does not alter llama.cpp's mapping (Design 1's --random-rest is ineffective). `numa` disables prefetch — worth testing as a knob.

HYPOTHESIS-TEST SOUNDNESS. H1: all three have LRU/LFU/static/Belady at Pi budgets; Design 2 adds the strongest controls (teacher-forced vs free-running, ubatch-1 kernel-independence, logits-vs-topk consistency, stack-distance cross-check, cross-layer predictor precision vs baselines); Design 1 is the only one whose reality check (bytes/token via cgroup io.stat + /proc/pid/io, pinning A/B in the same cgroup) can actually run and whose Pi projections are fed by expert-granularity fio and membw measurements with mandatory `kind` tagging. Design 0's corpus (~4k tokens) is too small for 3840 slabs. H2: Designs 1 and 2 include the indispensable iso-byte 'just quantize lower' control and soundness checks; Design 0 omits it, so its PROMISING threshold is not falsifiable against the obvious alternative. All three state the 17.65 GB/token dense floor honestly.

SCORES: D0 = 7+5+8+6+6 = 32; D1 = 8+8+9+7+8 = 40; D2 = 6+5+9+5+8 = 33. Winner: Design 1.

GRAFTS TO APPLY TO THE WINNER (in priority order): from D0 — the llama-server speculative harness with draft_n presence check and spec_type_effective, strip_thinking + exact_match_vs_plain, bench lock + RAM check, stdlib-only Pi feasibility fixtures incl. the context-friend-1 facts, the WorkingSet/PrivateBytes split, the three-column report; from D2 — teacher-forced/free-running modes and fixed.tokens.bin replay, --logits top-8 consistency check, stack-distance ↔ simulator cross-check, cross-layer predictor precision@k, weighted hit rate, bound tightness + Spearman, the E5 llama-quantize --tensor-type bracket, PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC fixtures, pi_config.env; optionally the ctypes tracer as a fast Windows path for trace volume (its layouts are verified) while keeping the C++ probe for io.csv. Fixes the winner needs regardless: use `ffn_geglu-<il>` (or recompute from ffn_norm) for the down-matrix input; replace llama-completion -md with llama-server or llama-cli -st; derive compute_tg_in_ram from measured desktop tok/s × bytes/token and membw rather than a constant; define a --quick trace corpus tier; drop the cross-process --random-rest claim and test `numa` / `-lm` variants against the MAP_POPULATE load storm; keep a ≥10k-token mixed EN/HE/code trace so steady-state hit rates at a ~1500-slab budget are statistically meaningful.

best_ideas: Speculative decoding routed ONLY through llama-server with timings.draft_n / draft_n_accepted (verified: -md is registered for SPECULATIVE/SERVER/CLI/IMATRIX, NOT llama-completion; server-common.cpp:100 emits draft_n) plus the explicit-spec-type retry and 'speculation inactive' reporting - the only design whose speculative path works as written
Hardcoded GGUF constants are real (verified data_offset 15823936, blk.0.ffn_gate_up_exps.weight 285474816 B, both file sizes byte-exact) -> integration tests that catch byte-range bugs immediately
Disk-gated KLD base (--kl-divergence-base size computed as chunks*ctx*262144*2 B) and the correct observation that D: has ~32 GB free, not 63 (verified: 32G)
Gemma thinking-channel strip before QA scoring + thinking_share metric + exact_match_vs_plain for 'lossless' claims
01_os_tune refuses dtparam=pciex1_gen=3 when an AI HAT occupies the PCIe bus (exactly the Hailo situation on the probed Pi)
results/.bench.lock + psutil RAM check so parallel agents never load two GGUFs at once; --quick and skip-if-result-exists everywhere
stdlib-only feasibility.py with fixture facts for all four Pi configs AND the probed context-friend-1, tested on Windows
pin_hotset checks RLIMIT_MEMLOCK and MemAvailable-budget >= 1 GB before any mlock and prints the exact limits.conf fix
flaws: Repack blindness: at a7b94df llama.cpp repacks Q4_0 (incl. MUL_MAT_ID experts, also on ARM NEON+dotprod -> q4_0_4x4) into CPU_REPACK buffers that are COPIED out of the mmap (llama-model.cpp:1856 buffer_from_host_ptr only for the default buft). With the design's flags (--mmap on, no -nr) an 8 GB Pi 'STREAM_NVME' tier allocates ~12.85 GB anonymous memory at load and OOMs; the pinning daemon pins page-cache pages llama.cpp never reads after load; E6 (docker --memory 5g, default flags) is OOM-killed rather than slowed. None of this is anticipated anywhere in the design

Tracer records 'ffn_moe_weights-<il>' and asserts weights sum to 1; Gemma4 calls build_moe_ffn with norm_w=true so the normalized weights are 'ffn_moe_weights_norm-<il>' (llama-graph.cpp:2142 vs 2163) - the golden-fixture test fails as specified
No hostname/service deny-list for the production Pi: only a 'busy' heuristic (loadavg>1 or MemAvailable<60%) - an idle context-friend-1 would pass and receive heavy work
Expert-byte sum test constant 12846034944 is wrong (30 x 428,212,224 = 12,846,366,720)
31B activation capture and all traces go through the Docker bind mount (14-18 GB reads, 31 GB VM) - acknowledged, but the slowest possible path when native Windows DLLs exist
H2 has no iso-byte control against simply using a lower quant (IQ2_XXS/Q3) - 'PROMISING' could be awarded to a scheme that loses to plain quantization
02_build uses a fixed -j4; on a 4 GB Pi the ggml-cpu translation units can OOM (Designs 1/2 scale jobs by RAM)

best_ideas: THE finding that makes or breaks the Pi runtime: default repack copies weights out of the mmap into anonymous memory (verified llama-model.cpp:1848-1870, is_default_buft gate; repack.cpp supports MUL_MAT_ID; ARM dotprod -> q4_0_4x4), so 'streaming experts via page cache' requires -nr (llama-bench --repack 0) - plus E0's hard gate 'experts must show as CPU_Mapped (ggml-backend.cpp:2646) with anon RSS < 3 GB or fix flags before any streaming work'
Warmup pollution identified from source (llama-graph.cpp:1473 n_expert_used = n_expert when cparams.warmup) and validator rejects any layer-token with != 8 distinct ids
Bytes-moved-per-token as the primary metric; `kind: measured|projected|assumed` MANDATORY in the results schema so reports cannot mix them silently
Bench matrix variants default / --repack 0 / -lm none with the 'CPU_REPACK vs CPU_Mapped model buffer size' log split - the one measurement that tells the Pi engineer what the RSS really is

Pinner runs INSIDE the same cgroup as the proxy run (locked pages count against the limit exactly as on a Pi); pinner --verify via mincore; exit 2 partial / 3 permission with the ulimit/limits.d hint; MADV_RANDOM on cold expert ranges to kill readahead thrash
fio at expert-slab granularity (bs=3345k randread) + 16k IOPS - the storage number the simulator actually needs
assert_safe_host refuses hostname context-friend-1 or any host running ContextFriend units unless PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, sourced by every pi/*.sh; -j2 on 4 GB boards
H2 includes the plain-q2 competitor and requires 'beats IQ2_XXS (8.5 GB) at comparable error' before calling anything promising; states the expected honest outcome (bound loose) up front
E6 decision rule: if pinning does not beat LRU by 15%, DROP it from the Pi default and say Linux LRU already protects hot pages
flaws: The 'hybrid' -ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU" mode does not do what is claimed at a7b94df: an override to the CPU buft re-runs select_weight_buft over buft_list_cpu, which still contains CPU_REPACK (llama-model-loader.cpp:1241-1242), so experts get repacked anyway. Only -nr keeps them mapped; the design's own E0 gate would catch this, but the Pi default mode and the 'nonexpert_overhead hybrid' budget math need to become -nr-only with the non-repacked kernel penalty measured

spec_bench uses llama-completion -md: llama-completion parses with LLAMA_EXAMPLE_COMPLETION (completion.cpp:94) and -md is not in its example set -> immediate usage error; must move to llama-cli or llama-server (the mitigation only records 'unavailable')
Stores 'ffn_moe_weights-<il>' (pre-normalization) as the gating weight; Gemma4 uses norm_w=true, so weighted stats should read ffn_moe_weights_norm
KLD with --save-all-logits at --chunks 20 -c 512 is 20*512*262144*2 = 5.4 GB per model (10.7 GB for both) on a drive with 32 GB free; not sized or gated

E3 trace target (>= 50k prefill + 2k gen tokens in Docker, -nr, bind-mount loads) is the longest critical-path step (60-90 min est.) for a few-hours budget; the Docker-volume copy for E5 needs ~16 GB on the VM disk (C:, ~34 GB free) - checked, but tight
Trace flush 'when the last MoE layer's topk arrives' is fragile under ubatch splitting; Design 0's per-layer accumulators with equal-column assertion is sturdier
No --quick / resumable orchestrator equivalent to Design 0's run_all_today.ps1; Makefile.ps1 tasks only

best_ideas: Correctly identifies that the Windows bundle has NO llama-eval-callback (verified) and no compiler, and proposes a ctypes tracer against the prebuilt llama.dll reading D: natively; the struct mirrors are accurate (verified field-for-field: llama_context_params cb_eval@88, sizeof 160; ggml_tensor data@248, name@256, sizeof 336) with sizeof/round-trip self-checks and a C++ fallback
Uses 'ffn_moe_weights_norm-<il>' - the correct normalized gating tensor for Gemma4 (norm_w=true)
LRU stack-distance histogram -> exact hit-rate curve, cross-checked against the simulator within 1e-9 (the best unit-level validation of the cache model in any design)
fixed.tokens.bin teacher-forced replay so Windows-zen4 vs Docker vs Pi comparisons never depend on greedy divergence; Python-vs-C++ routing agreement is reported, not assumed
C++ tracer records /proc/self/io read_bytes + ru_majflt per token - direct bytes/token measurement; pi/05 stream-bench samples /proc/<pid>/io on the Pi itself

H2 controls: iso-byte uniform-quant baseline, teacher-forced vs free-running activations, bound tightness p10/p50/p90 + Spearman, soundness violations must be 0, optional bf16-shard yardstick; thresholds include 'no advantage' and 'bound useless' outcomes
E5 end-to-end bracket via llama-quantize --tensor-type (flag verified) + llama-perplexity --kl-divergence-base: a cheap upper bound on H2 loss without custom kernels

pi_config.env single parameter file, DENY_HOSTS + PROTECTED_SERVICES, exit codes 2/3/4, JOBS = min(nproc, floor(MemAvailable/1.2)), sha256 via HF ETag, udev-persisted read_ahead_kb, PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC fixture harness for lib.sh on Git Bash
Belady band [0.8xBelady, 1.3xLRU] and explicit readahead-inflation estimate fed back into a pagecache_approx policy
flaws: Repack blindness (same as Design 0): no -nr anywhere; 05_run.sh defaults OOM on the 8 GB streaming tier, pin_ranges pins pages the repacked model never touches, and E3 (--memory 6g) is OOM-killed by the ~14 GB anonymous repack copy unless the C++ tracer adds -nr
Speculative benchmark via llama-completion -md fails (not in LLAMA_EXAMPLE_COMPLETION's flag set) - the headline with/without-MTP number is missing until rerouted to llama-cli/llama-server

ctypes-into-llama.dll is high-variance for coding agents with no debugger: any struct/enum mistake is a silent corruption or crash; llama_model_params sizeof asserted as 88 but the header packs to 80 (test catches, but shows the fragility)
Proposes scp + running feasibility on the production context-friend-1 (read-only, but the user said it is the wrong Pi and must not be disturbed; fixtures suffice)
Two tracer implementations (ctypes + C++) must stay byte-compatible - acknowledged drift risk
Docker-volume copy of 14.4 GB needed before E3 (VM disk on C:), plus --device-read-bps probe likely unsupported under WSL2 (acknowledged)
pi_model's all-in-RAM projection of 3-5 tok/s assumes 12 GB/s effective and ignores the non-repacked-kernel penalty that -nr (once added) imposes on the Pi

judgments.rationale: Judged as the engineer who has to make this run on a Pi, with claims checked against the actual a7b94df checkout and the Windows bundle. The decisive fact: llama.cpp repacks Q4_0 by default (CPU_REPACK, incl. MUL_MAT_ID expert tensors, and on ARM NEON+dotprod -> q4_0_4x4), and repacked tensors are COPIED out of the mmap into anonymous memory (llama-model.cpp:1856 uses buffer_from_host_ptr only for the default buft). So on an 8 GB Pi every 'stream the cold experts through the page cache' story in Designs 0 and 2 OOMs at load with their stated flags, their mlock pinning helpers pin pages the inference process never reads after load, and their Docker --memory validation runs are OOM-killed instead of slowed. Only Design 1 found this (with correct line refs), built the E0 hard gate ('experts must appear as CPU_Mapped, anon RSS < 3 GB, else fix flags before any streaming work'), benchmarks --repack 0 / -lm none variants, and runs the pinner inside the same cgroup. Design 1's own proposed fix is partly wrong - -ot '...=CPU' re-selects the extra bufts at this commit (llama-model-loader.cpp:1241), so the 'hybrid' collapses to default and the real Pi mode is -nr with a measured kernel penalty - but its gate catches that in E0 rather than on the Pi. Design 1 also found the warmup all-experts pollution (llama-graph.cpp:1473), enforces kind=measured|projected|assumed structurally, adds the plain-lower-quant competitor to H2, uses fio at expert-slab size, and has the strongest production-host refusal. Its real flaws: llama-completion does not accept -md (verified: only SPECULATIVE/SERVER/CLI/IMATRIX), it reads the pre-norm ffn_moe_weights, and KLD at 20 chunks is 5.4 GB/model on a 32 GB-free drive. Design 0 is the best 'numbers today' harness (server-based speculative path is the only one that works as written; its GGUF constants are byte-exact; disk gating and AI-HAT detection are good), but it is blind to repack, has no host deny-list, and its weights-sum test is against the wrong tensor. Design 2 has the most rigorous science (stack-distance cross-check, iso-byte control, teacher vs free-running, fixed-token replay, /proc/io per token) and an impressively accurate ctypes layout, but carries the same repack blindness, the same -md flaw, and the highest implementation variance. Graft into the winner: Design 0's llama-server speculative path with draft_n timings, disk-gated KLD sizing, thinking-channel strip, AI-HAT check, bench lock file and four-config feasibility fixtures; Design 2's ffn_moe_weights_norm, stack-distance/LRU cross-check, iso-byte and teacher-vs-free-running controls, fixed.tokens.bin replay, /proc/self/io per-token and Pi stream-bench, --tensor-type KLD bracket, RAM-scaled build jobs and ETag sha256. Also note for all: `-lm dio` (direct I/O) exists at this commit and nobody uses it.

manifest.summary: Final build manifest for REPO_ROOT (repo-relative paths below). Base = winner (bytes-moved-per-token systems design); grafts and fixes applied after re-verifying every load-bearing claim against third_party/llama.cpp @ a7b94df and the real GGUF headers today. Verified facts that shape the build: (1) default repack copies every Q4_0 tensor out of the mmap into CPU_REPACK anonymous memory (llama-model.cpp:1849-1870 mmaps only the default buft). (2) The winner's 'hybrid' `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` does NOT keep experts mapped: an override to the CPU buft re-runs select_weight_buft over buft_list_cpu, which still contains CPU_REPACK (llama-model-loader.cpp:1240-1242), and `-ot` can only name default device bufts (arg.cpp:255-260). So the ONLY page-cache streaming mode at this commit is `-nr`/`--no-repack` (`--repack 0` in llama-bench): the whole file stays CPU_Mapped. Its kernel penalty is measured (E0), not assumed; the hybrid is kept only as a negative control. (3) gemma4 dense FFN emits `ffn_norm-<il>` (gate/up input), `ffn_geglu-<il>` (down input, [21504,T]) and `ffn_out-<il>` (down output, pre post-norm); MoE routing tensors are `ffn_moe_topk-<il>` (I32 view [8,T], nb[1]=512) and `ffn_moe_weights_norm-<il>` (F32 [1,8,T], sums to 1; gemma4 uses norm_w=true); warmup routes to ALL experts (llama-graph.cpp:1473) so the probe sets params.warmup=false (`--no-warmup` is not a COMMON flag). (4) `-md` is wired only for SPECULATIVE/SERVER/CLI/IMATRIX, so speculative decoding is measured through llama-server `timings.draft_n/draft_n_accepted` (the orchestrator's ad-hoc run already showed: MoE MTP never drafts, DFlash engages at 28% acceptance and is slower). (5) Load modes are `-lm auto|none|mmap|mlock|mmap+mlock|dio`; `--mlock/--no-mmap` are gone. (6) gguf-py ReaderTensor.data_offset is absolute. 26B: data_offset 15,823,936; 658 tensors; experts 12,846,366,720 B (gate_up 2,230,272 + down 1,115,136 = 3,345,408 B per expert-layer; 802,897,920 B/token worst case); non-expert 1,577,172,088 B (attn 624,885,760; tied Q6_K head 605,563,904 read every token; dense FFN 301,086,720; norms/router/scales 45,635,704). 31B: data_offset 15,833,440; 833 tensors; FFN 11,705,057,280 (65,028,096 per gate/up/down matrix, no scale tensors); attention 4,770,160,640; tied head 1,156,076,544. (7) Idle-machine desktop baseline already measured (results/desktop-baseline-2026-10-04.md): MoE tg32 15.18@4t, 13.52@6t, 12.79@12t; 31B tg32 2.44@6t; server MoE gen 16.03 tok/s; loads 12.7/13.3 s. (8) Disk: D: 32 GB free, C: 26 GB free (Docker VM vhdx lives on C:); Docker image pi-gemma4-build:latest exists; gguf-py header read takes ~11 s per model on Windows (cache map.json). Repo shape: `pigemma/` Python package (stdlib-only parts run on the Pi's Python 3.13), three tiny native tools (probe C++ cb_eval recorder, pinner C mlock daemon, membw C bandwidth bench) built in Docker and on the Pi from one CMake tree, `pc/` drivers (PowerShell for native Windows binaries, bash for Docker), `pi/` parametric runtime with host deny-list, `docs/`. 36 files in 6 dependency groups; all unit tests run on Windows without models via synthetic GGUFs/traces.

files.purpose: Installable `pigemma` package, pytest config, dependency pins, ignore rules for large artefacts.
files.spec: [project] name=pigemma, requires-python>=3.12, dependencies: numpy>=2.0, psutil>=5.9. Optional extras: h2=[torch>=2.4], hf=[huggingface_hub>=0.30]. gguf is NOT a pip dep: pigemma/__init__.py inserts <repo>/third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py at the front of sys.path if `import gguf` fails (same trick works on the Pi after pi/02 clones llama.cpp at a7b94df). [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths=['tests'], addopts='-q -m "not integration"', markers: integration (needs real GGUFs/Docker; run with `pytest -m integration`), linux (skipped on Windows). requirements.txt mirrors deps plus pytest>=8. .gitignore additions: models/ (exists), traces/**/*.moetrace, traces/**/*.bin, traces/**/*.npy, results/**/*.logits, results/**/*.log, tools/build-*/, **/__pycache__/, pi/out/; keep results/**/*.json and results/**/*.md tracked. No console_scripts: every CLI is `python -m pigemma.<module>`.
files.test: `pip install -e .` then `python -c "import pigemma, gguf"` works on Windows; `pytest` collects and runs unit tests in < 60 s.

files.purpose: Single source of truth for repo root, model registry, binary resolution per platform, host fingerprint, cheap model identity, free-disk check and the benchmark lock that serialises model-loading jobs across agents.
files.spec: REPO_ROOT = parent of the package dir. MODELS dict (id -> dict(path, bytes, kind, quant, draft_of)): '26b-q4' models/google__gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf/gemma-4-26B_q4_0-it.gguf 14439363584 moe; '31b-q4' models/google__gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf/gemma-4-31B_q4_0-it.gguf 17651001568 dense; '26b-mtp' models/ggml-org__gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF/mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_0.gguf 251939520; '26b-dflash' models/ggml-org__gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF/dflash-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q8_0.gguf 472433824; '31b-mtp' models/unsloth__gemma-4-31B-it-qat-GGUF/MTP/mtp-gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_0.gguf 279955968. `model_path(id_or_path)` accepts an id or a path; `require_model(id)` raises FileNotFoundError with the HF repo hint if missing or size differs. `bin(tool)` -> Path: Windows -> third_party/llama.cpp-win/<tool>.exe; Linux with /.dockerenv -> /work/third_party/llama.cpp/build-linux-x86/bin/<tool>; Linux aarch64 -> $LLAMA_DIR/build/bin/<tool> (default ~/llama.cpp); custom tools (pigemma-probe, pinner, membw) -> $PIGEMMA_TOOLS_BIN or tools/build-linux-x86/bin (Docker) or tools/build/bin (Pi). LLAMA_COMMIT='a7b94df', LLAMA_BUILD=11398 (assert against third_party/llama.cpp-win/VERSION when present; warn if different). `host_fingerprint()` -> dict(hostname, os, kernel, cpu (platform.processor() or /proc/cpuinfo 'model name'), n_logical, n_physical (psutil or os.cpu_count), ram_total_bytes, ram_avail_bytes, page_size (os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') or 4096), in_container (/.dockerenv), cgroup_mem_max (read /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max, None if absent/'max'), python). `sha256_prefix(path, n_bytes=16 MiB)` -> hex of first n bytes (cheap identity of 17 GB files) plus size. `free_disk_bytes(path)` via shutil.disk_usage. `bench_lock(min_free_gb=20)` context manager: creates results/.bench.lock with {pid, host, started, cmd}; if an existing lock's pid is alive (psutil.pid_exists) raise RuntimeError('another model-loading job is running'); if psutil.virtual_memory().available < min_free_gb GB raise; stale lock (dead pid) is replaced; env PIGEMMA_MIN_FREE_GB overrides. All commands that load a GGUF (bench, quality, trace_collect, pagecache_limit, h2 act-dump) must enter this lock; Docker runs enter it on the Windows side via `python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold -- <cmd>` (runs cmd under the lock, forwards exit code). Logging: one line per decision at INFO.
files.test: tests/test_paths.py: registry sizes present; bin() per platform via monkeypatched sys.platform/env; sha256_prefix on a temp file equals hashlib of its first bytes; bench_lock refuses while a lock with the current pid exists and replaces a dead-pid lock; `--hold` runs a trivial command and forwards its exit code.

files.purpose: One results-JSON envelope for desktop, Docker and Pi numbers (measured / projected / assumed never mixed silently) plus the summariser that renders docs/results/*.md.
files.spec: `write_result(path, **fields)`: validates required keys run_id (uuid4), experiment ('E0'...'E8' or 'adhoc'), created_at (ISO UTC), kind in {'measured','projected','assumed'}, host (paths.host_fingerprint()), llama_build, llama_commit, model {id,file,quant,bytes,sha_prefix}, variant (str), flags (list[str]), threads, n_ctx, and when kind != 'measured' a non-empty `assumptions` dict ({name: {value, unit, source}}) and `inputs` (list of result/trace paths used). Optional keys: pp {tok_s, sd, n}, tg {tok_s, sd, n}, load_s, rss_peak_mb, private_peak_mb, mapped_mb, buffer_split {CPU_REPACK_mib, CPU_Mapped_mib, CPU_mib}, read_bytes_per_token, majflt_per_token, io_rbytes_per_token, accept_rate, draft_n, draft_n_accepted, spec_type_effective, identical_to_plain, kld {mean, max, p999, same_top_p}, ppl, qa_score, qa_total, coherent, output_sample (<=2000 chars), notes (list[str]). Unknown keys allowed under `extra`. Raises ValueError listing missing keys. `load_results(dir_or_glob)` -> list[dict] (skips unparsable files with a warning). CLI `python -m pigemma.results summarize <dir...> --md <out.md> [--experiment E0]`: groups by experiment then model, renders markdown tables with three clearly labelled sections per experiment: MEASURED (kind=measured), PROJECTED (kind=projected, with an 'Assumptions used' sub-table listing name/value/unit/source), ASSUMED; missing metrics render as 'not run'. Also `python -m pigemma.results validate <file...>` -> exit 1 on schema errors.
files.test: tests/test_results.py: missing `kind` rejected; projected without assumptions rejected; summarize renders a fixture dir with one measured + one projected file into markdown containing both section headers and 'not run'.

files.purpose: Reference reader/writer/validator for the .moetrace routing-trace format, the tokens/acts sidecars, merge, and the H1 statistics (frequency skew, coverage, LRU stack-distance hit curve, token-adjacent reuse, cross-layer predictability).
files.spec: Binary layout exactly as data_formats '.moetrace'. `TraceWriter(path, header: dict)`: writes magic, header, placeholder n_records=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF; `.write(token_index, pos, token_id, phase, chunk_id, ids: np.uint8[L,K], weights: np.float16[L,K], probs: optional np.ndarray[L,P] of (id,prob))`; `.close()` patches n_records; also appends token_id to `<stem>.tokens.bin` (i32 LE). `TraceReader(path)`: parses header; if n_records is the sentinel, infers count from file size and sets `.truncated=True` (warn); exposes `.header`, `.n`, `.ids` (uint8 [T,L,K]), `.weights` (float32 [T,L,K]), `.phase` (uint8 [T]), `.chunk` (uint8 [T]), `.token_index`, `.token_ids` (from tokens.bin if present), `.probs` (or None); loads lazily via np.memmap + structured dtype. `validate(path) -> list[str]`: magic, header keys present (format_version, model_name, gguf_path, gguf_size_bytes, llama_build, llama_commit, arch, n_layer, n_expert, n_expert_used, moe_layers, probs_top, weights_tensor, created_at, n_ctx, n_batch, n_ubatch, flags), record_size matches formula, ids < n_expert, K distinct ids per (token,layer), weights finite and sum within 0.02 of 1.0 (weights_tensor=='ffn_moe_weights_norm'), token_index contiguous from 0, tokens.bin length == n_records when present. `merge(paths, out)`: same model/n_layer/n_expert, renumbers token_index, chunk_id offsets, concatenates tokens.bin, header.sources=[...]. `stats(reader, train_frac=0.7, item='layer-expert') -> dict` (schema in data_formats 'stats.json'): per layer freq[128], entropy_bits, effective_experts, gini, coverage_at {8,16,32,48,64,96} by selection count and by weight mass; global: unique experts per token mean, token-adjacent reuse P(e in S_t+1 | e in S_t) per layer and mean, mean Jaccard(S_t,S_t+1), LRU stack-distance histogram over items (layer,expert) -> exact LRU hit-rate curve hit[C] for C in 1..3840 (one pass with an order-statistics structure or a simple list; T*L*K ~ 4M accesses fine), working set (distinct experts per layer per window 16/64/256/1024: median/p95), prefill vs generated frequency JS-divergence per layer, per-chunk-source (corpus id from header.chunks) top-32 Jaccard overlap matrix, cross-layer predictor: table P(e' in S_{l+1} | e in S_l) from train split, precision@8/@16 on test split vs static-top-16 baseline vs 'same ids as layer l' baseline, mutual information I(top1_l; top1_{l+1}); if probs present: p8-p9 margin distribution and 8th-expert weight mass. CLI: `python -m pigemma.trace validate <trace>`; `stats <trace> [--train-frac 0.7] --out <stats.json> [--csv-dir dir]`; `merge <out> <in...>`; `info <trace>` (prints header + counts). Sidecar helpers: `write_meta(stem, dict)`, `read_meta`, `read_acts_dir(dir) -> Acts(meta, get(layer, kind) -> np.float16 memmap [T, ne0], phase, token_ids)`.
files.test: tests/test_trace.py: write 1000 synthetic records (L=4,K=8,E=16) read back bit-exact; sentinel n_records inferred with truncated=True; validate rejects bad id, duplicate ids, weight sum 1.5, truncated record; coverage curve monotone and 1.0 at K=E; single-hot-expert trace gives coverage@1 == 1.0 and entropy 0; stack-distance LRU curve equals cache_sim LRU hit rate within 1e-9 at 3 capacities (shared fixture via tests/synth.py); predictor precision@16 >= static baseline on a trace with injected layer correlation; merge renumbers token_index.

files.purpose: GGUF byte-range planner (every tensor and every expert slab as absolute file ranges, classified), per-token traffic accounting, hot-set planner that emits mlock ranges, and the catalog refresh.
files.spec: `build_map(path, page_size=16384) -> GgufMap` using gguf.GGUFReader: reads KV gemma4.block_count, gemma4.expert_count (0 if absent), gemma4.expert_used_count, gemma4.embedding_length, gemma4.feed_forward_length, gemma4.expert_feed_forward_length, attention.head_count_kv (list), attention.key_length/key_length_swa, sliding_window, sliding_window_pattern; tensors: for each ReaderTensor record name, type name, shape (gguf-py order, ne[0] fastest), n_bytes, offset=data_offset (absolute, asserted by the unit test), kind in {token_embd, output, attn, ffn_dense, norm, router, expert_scale, expert, other} by regex (expert: `^blk\.(\d+)\.ffn_(gate_up|gate|up|down)_exps\.weight$`; router: ffn_gate_inp.*; expert_scale: ffn_.*_exps\.scale), layer (int or null). Expert slabs: n_expert = shape[-1]; nb_expert = n_bytes // n_expert (assert divisible); expert e of that tensor = [offset + e*nb_expert, offset + (e+1)*nb_expert). map.json stores per layer {layer, gate_up:{offset, nb_expert}, down:{offset, nb_expert}} not 7680 rows. Summary: file_size, data_offset, nonexpert_bytes, expert_bytes, expert_unit_bytes (gate_up+down per expert), n_moe_layers, expert_bytes_per_token_worst = n_moe_layers*n_expert_used*unit, nonexpert_bytes_per_token = attn + ffn_dense + norm + router + expert_scale + (output bytes if a separate output tensor exists else token_embd bytes, because the tied head is read every token) + one embedding row, kv_bytes_per_token_f16 = sum over layers of n_head_kv[il]*(key_length_swa if sliding else key_length)*2*2 (K and V both counted: upper bound) and kv_bytes(n_ctx) = sum(min(n_ctx, 1024 if sliding else n_ctx) * per-layer bytes), and the expected numbers for 26B asserted in the integration test (expert_bytes 12846366720, unit 3345408, nonexpert 1577172088, worst/token 802897920). `aligned(offset, length, page)` floors start / ceils end; `merge_ranges`. CLI `python -m pigemma.gguf_map build <gguf> --out <map.json> [--page-size 16384]` (prints the summary table incl. GB per token). `python -m pigemma.gguf_map hotset --map map.json --stats stats.json --budget-bytes N [--page-size 16384] [--no-nonexpert] [--per-layer-min 0] [--rank count|weight] --out hotset.json`: ranges = all non-expert tensors first (mandatory unless --no-nonexpert; includes the tied head), then experts by descending stats.per_layer.freq (or weight mass) with at least per-layer-min per layer, until budget; page-align, merge adjacent, sort by offset; writes hotset.json (data_formats) AND hotset.ranges.txt (one 'offset length' per line, '#' comments) for the pinner; prints total bytes, expert count, expert_coverage_fraction = sum(freq of selected)/sum(all freq). Budget exceeded by at most one page per range. `python -m pigemma.gguf_map catalog-refresh` (PC only, huggingface_hub HfApi.model_info(files_metadata=True)) fills exact byte sizes and sha256 (LFS) for catalog entries with bytes_exact=false. Edge cases: non-MoE GGUF -> experts empty, n_expert 0; missing KV keys -> error naming the key.
files.test: tests/test_gguf_map.py on the conftest synthetic GGUF (arch gemma4, 2 layers, 4 experts, n_embd 64, expert ff 32, Q4_0 expert tensors ne=[64,32,4]/[32,64,4] via gguf.quants.quantize, F32 norms, Q6_K-shaped token_embd replaced by F16 [64,16]): slab ranges contiguous and cover the tensor exactly; offsets equal GGUFWriter's data offsets; kinds; nonexpert+expert == sum of tensor bytes; 16 KiB alignment pads correctly; hotset respects budget (+<=1 page/range), always includes non-expert ranges unless --no-nonexpert, orders by freq, merges adjacent experts, coverage fraction correct, ranges.txt round-trips. @integration: real 26B constants above and 31B ffn matrix bytes 65028096.

files.purpose: One out-of-tree CMake project building pigemma-probe (C++), pinner (C, Linux) and membw (C) against the pinned llama.cpp without modifying it; used in Docker (x86) and on the Pi (aarch64).

GGML_NATIVE and arch flags are passed on the command line (Docker: -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_AVX2=ON -DGGML_AVX512=ON; Pi: -DGGML_NATIVE=ON, fallback -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16). Header comment documents both invocations.
