files.purpose: Memory-bandwidth micro-bench so the Pi's in-RAM tok/s ceiling and the desktop calibration use measured GB/s instead of a guess.
files.spec: `membw [--size-mb 512] [--threads 1,2,4] [--reps 5] [--json]`. Allocates size_mb buffer per thread-set (page-touched), measures per thread count: read (sum of 64-bit words, result consumed to defeat DCE), copy (memcpy to a second buffer), triad (a[i]=b[i]+s*c[i], 3 arrays of size/3 each); best-of-reps GB/s (1e9 B/s). Threads split the buffer into equal contiguous chunks; barrier before timing. Output text table or JSON {"size_mb":512, "results":[{"threads":4,"read_gbps":x,"copy_gbps":y,"triad_gbps":z}], "host":"<uname -m>"}. Exit 1 on allocation failure. No external deps; builds with -Wall -Wextra -Werror.
files.test: Builds warning-free in Docker; `membw --size-mb 64 --threads 1,2 --json` finishes < 5 s and all numbers > 0; JSON parses (tests/test_bench_parse.py parses membw_sample.json).

files.purpose: Expert-cache simulator for H1: replays a trace at Pi byte budgets under LRU/LFU/static/Belady/prefetch policies, reports bytes/token and hit rates, projects tok/s per device profile with explicit assumptions.
files.spec: Access sequence: for token t (in trace order), for il in moe_layers, for e in ids[t,il] -> item (il,e) of size expert_unit_bytes (gate_up+down, both read on a miss; from map.json); per-item cost rounded up to `--read-granularity` (default 131072 B) to model readahead. Policies: `lru` (OrderedDict), `lfu` (counts with exponential decay `--lfu-decay 0.999`/token, ties by recency), `static` (pre-filled with top-N items by frequency on the first `--train-split` fraction of tokens, never replaced; misses are read but not inserted; evaluated on the remaining tokens and reported separately), `belady` (offline optimal: next-use index precomputed), `lru_prefetch` (LRU plus: after layer il of token t, predict the set for il+1 from the cross-layer table P(e' in S_{il+1} | e in S_il) built on the train split (top-K by summed probability), issue reads for predicted misses; prefetch bytes counted separately as `prefetch_bytes`, wasted prefetch = predicted but unused; in the projection the overlapped part is min(prefetch_bytes, storage_bw * t_layer) where t_layer = t_ram_per_token / n_layers), `lru_perlayer` (budget split equally per layer; control). Warm-up: first `--warmup-tokens` (default 256) excluded from steady-state metrics (overall also reported). Metrics per run: hit_rate, weighted_hit_rate (by routing weight), miss_bytes_per_token {mean,p50,p95,max}, n_miss_per_token mean, cold_bytes, per_layer_hit_rate[L], prefetch_bytes_per_token, wasted_prefetch_fraction, unique_items_touched, capacity_items. Budgets: `--budgets-gb 0.5,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,12.85` and/or `--profiles <names>` which derive expert_cache_bytes = ram_bytes - os_reserve_bytes - nonexpert_bytes - kv_bytes(n_ctx, q8_0 = f16/2 + 1/32) - compute_buffers_bytes (if <= 0 -> verdict INFEASIBLE, still simulated at 0). Projection per profile (kind=projected): resident_bytes_per_token = nonexpert_bytes_per_token + hit_bytes (expert bytes served from RAM); t_ram = resident_bytes_per_token / (mem_bw_gbps * eff) where eff = llama_efficiency measured on the desktop (= tg_measured * bytes_per_token / membw_read_gbps from results/e0 if present, else 0.65 assumed); t_io = miss_bytes_per_token / rand_read_3mb_mbps + n_miss * access_ms; tg_serial = 1/(t_ram + t_io); tg_overlap = 1/max(t_ram, t_io - overlapped/storage_bw); floor_all_in_ram = (mem_bw*eff)/(nonexpert_bytes_per_token + worst_expert_bytes_per_token); dense line for 31B: bytes/token = file data bytes -> tok/s at mem_bw and at storage_bw. Verdict per (profile,policy): FITS_RAM | STREAM_GOOD (tg_overlap>=2.0 and tg_serial>=1.0) | STREAM_WEAK (tg_serial 0.5-1.0) | NOT_VIABLE. CLI: `python -m pigemma.cache_sim <trace> --map map.json --catalog pigemma/data/catalog.json [--policies lru,lfu,static,belady,lru_prefetch] [--budgets-gb ...] [--profiles all] [--train-split 0.3] [--warmup-tokens 256] [--read-granularity 131072] [--token-range A:B] --out results/h1/sim.json [--csv results/h1/sim.csv] [--series results/h1/sim_series.npz]`. Output schema in data_formats 'sim.json'. API: `simulate(reader, map, policy, budget_bytes, **opts) -> SimResult`; `project(sim_result, profile, map, calibration) -> dict`. Performance: pure Python dict/OrderedDict over ~4-5M accesses per run finishes in < 1 min; Belady uses precomputed next-use arrays (numpy). Logs one line per (policy,budget) with hit rate and MB/token.
files.test: tests/test_cache_sim.py: infinite budget -> steady-state bytes 0 and cold_bytes == unique items * unit; zero budget -> bytes/token == L*K*unit; belady misses <= lru misses <= lru_perlayer misses on 30 random Zipf traces; cyclic pattern of budget+1 items -> LRU hit 0, Belady > 0; hit rate monotone in budget; lru_prefetch with a perfect predictor (table from the same trace, deterministic routing) -> stall bytes 0 and wasted 0; LRU hit rate equals trace.stats stack-distance curve within 1e-9; projection known-answer (hand-computed numbers); profile-derived budget formula; verdict thresholds.

files.language: Python 3.12+ stdlib only (runs on the Pi)
files.purpose: Pure decision logic for the Pi feasibility verdict: facts.json + catalog -> per model/quant verdict with reasons, recommended quant and llama.cpp flags, refusal on protected/busy hosts; exit codes drive every pi/*.sh.
files.spec: `load_catalog(path, io_mem=None)`; `verdict(facts, catalog, want=None, sim=None) -> Verdict(ok, exit_code, rows, recommended, reasons, host_refused)`. Constants at top (documented): OS_RESERVE = catalog device os_reserve or 0.7e9 (<=4 GB) / 0.8e9 (8 GB) / 0.9e9 (>=16 GB); KV_Q8_4K = 160e6 (26B at 4096 ctx, q8_0 K/V; from gguf_map kv_bytes) and 420e6 for 31B; COMPUTE_BUFFERS = 0.3e9; MIN_STREAM_CACHE = 2.0e9; MIN_FREE_RAM_TO_RUN = 1.0e9. Per model row: usable = ram_total - OS_RESERVE - kv - COMPUTE_BUFFERS; FITS_MAPPED if file_bytes <= usable (run with -nr: file-backed, no anon copy, graceful under pressure); FITS_REPACKED additionally if file_bytes + 0.3e9 <= usable - 1.0e9 (repack keeps an anonymous copy; on a 16 GB Pi with Q4_0 this is expected FALSE -> flags say -nr); else STREAM: expert_cache = usable - nonexpert_bytes; resident_fraction = expert_cache / expert_bytes; hit = interpolate catalog.selection.stream_hit_rate_curve_assumed (or sim.json LRU at that budget when --sim given, source then 'simulated'); miss_bytes = (1-hit) * 802897920; t_io = miss_bytes / storage.rand_read_3mb_mbps + n_miss*access_ms where n_miss = (1-hit)*240; t_ram = (nonexpert_bytes_per_token + hit*802897920) / (mem_bw*0.65); tok_s = 1/(t_ram+t_io); STREAM_OK if expert_cache >= MIN_STREAM_CACHE and storage.type in {nvme, usb-ssd} and tok_s >= 1.0; STREAM_SLOW if tok_s in [0.3,1.0) or storage microsd with tok_s>=0.3; NOT_VIABLE otherwise; dense (expert_bytes==0) streaming -> NEVER_GOOD_SPEED with the arithmetic string (file_bytes / storage_bw s per token). NO_DISK if free_disk < 1.05*file_bytes and the file is not already present. Host refusal (exit 4, ok=False, no rows evaluated for heavy work): hostname in catalog.protected_hosts, or any running service matches protected_service_globs, unless facts.override == 'PIGEMMA_I_KNOW'; busy refusal (exit 4): loadavg1 > 2.0 or ram_available < MIN_FREE_RAM_TO_RUN. Exit codes: 0 some row FITS_* or STREAM_OK; 2 best is STREAM_SLOW; 3 nothing viable / NO_DISK; 4 refused. `recommended` = best row by (FITS_MAPPED > STREAM_OK > STREAM_SLOW), tie-break higher-bit quant, with `flags`: FITS_MAPPED -> '-nr -lm mmap+mlock -t 4 -c 4096 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0'; FITS_REPACKED -> '-lm mmap -t 4 -c 4096 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0'; STREAM_* -> '-nr -lm mmap -t 4 -c 4096 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -b 256 -ub 64'. Always appends the recommendation line 'Pi 5 16 GB + NVMe Gen3: 26B-A4B fits in RAM (-nr); 8 GB + NVMe Gen3: stream experts (~40% cached); 8 GB + USB3: weak; 4 GB or microSD: not viable; 31B dense: never good speed on any Pi 5'. CLI: `python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts facts.json [--catalog pigemma/data/catalog.json] [--want 26b|31b] [--sim results/h1/sim.json] [--json out.json] [--emit env]` prints a table (model, quant, bytes, verdict, projected tok/s with source, reason) and, with --emit env, shell-safe `MODEL_ID= MODEL_REPO= MODEL_FILE= MODEL_BYTES= LLAMA_FLAGS='...' DRAFT_REPO= DRAFT_FILE= PIN_BUDGET_BYTES=` lines; exits with the verdict code.
files.test: tests/test_feasibility.py with the five facts fixtures: 4GB+microSD -> NOT_VIABLE for all, exit 3 (and exit 4 when the services list contains contextfriend-*); 8GB+USB3 -> 26b STREAM_SLOW/OK per curve, exit 2 or 0 as computed and asserted against hand arithmetic; 8GB+NVMe -> STREAM_OK exit 0 with flags containing '-nr'; 16GB+NVMe -> 26b-q4 FITS_MAPPED, FITS_REPACKED false, flags contain '-nr -lm mmap+mlock'; 31b always NEVER_GOOD_SPEED with the s/token string; busy facts -> exit 4; --emit env output is shell-safe (no unquoted spaces); --sim overrides the assumed curve.

files.purpose: Wrapper for llama-bench / llama-completion / llama-server on every platform: runs variant matrices, parses outputs, samples memory, measures bytes read, writes results-envelope JSON. Speculative decoding goes through llama-server timings.
files.spec: Binary resolution via paths.bin. Variants -> flags: default: []; norepack: llama-bench `--repack 0`, others `-nr`; hybrid_negctrl: `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` (negative control: expected to still repack); nommap: `-lm none`; mlock: `-lm mmap+mlock`; kvq8: `-fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`. Subcommands: (a) `matrix --model <id|path> --threads 4,6,12 --pp 128 --tg 32 -r 3 --variants default,norepack,hybrid_negctrl,nommap [--kvq8] --out <dir>` -> one llama-bench process per variant with `-m F -t <list> -p PP -n TG -r R -o json [flags]`; parse the JSON array rows (build_commit, build_number, cpu_info, model_size, n_threads, n_prompt, n_gen, avg_ts, stddev_ts, type_k/type_v, flash_attn); write one result per (variant, threads, pp|tg) with experiment E0, kind measured. (b) `completion --model F --prompt-file P -n 128 --threads 6 --variant V [--chat] --out <dir>` -> `llama-completion -m F -f P -n N --temp 0 -t T -c 4096 [flags]` (prompt chat-wrapped if --chat); memory sampler thread (0.25 s): Windows psutil memory_info().rss (working set) and memory_full_info().private peaks; Linux /proc/<pid>/status VmHWM, RssAnon, RssFile peaks and /proc/<pid>/io read_bytes delta; parse stderr: `load time = X ms`, `prompt eval time = ... (X tokens per second)`, `eval time = ... (X tokens per second)`, and buffer lines `load_tensors:\s+(\S+) model buffer size =\s+([\d.]+) MiB` into buffer_split; capture stdout text as output_sample; coherence via quality.is_coherent. (c) `server-spec --model F --variant plain|mtp|mtp-explicit|dflash|dflash-explicit|ngram --prompts data/prompts/gen_prompts.json -n 200 --threads 6 --port 18080 --out <dir>`: starts its OWN `llama-server -m F -t T -c 4096 -np 1 --host 127.0.0.1 --port P [-md DRAFT] [--spec-type draft-mtp|draft-dflash|ngram-simple] [--spec-draft-n-max 6]` (draft path from catalog drafts), polls /health until {"status":"ok"} (timeout 300 s, records load_time_s), one warm-up /completion of 16 tokens, then per prompt POST /completion {prompt: chat-wrapped, n_predict, temperature 0, cache_prompt false}; records timings (prompt_n, prompt_per_second, predicted_n, predicted_per_second, draft_n, draft_n_accepted), content; accept_rate = sum(draft_n_accepted)/sum(draft_n) or None; spec_active = draft_n > 0 on every request; spec_type_effective = 'inferred' | 'explicit:<type>' | 'none'; if variant mtp shows draft_n == 0/absent, the driver (not this function) also runs mtp-explicit; identical_to_plain computed by quality.visible_text equality vs the plain run's content per prompt; terminates only its own child (terminate, then kill after 10 s); never touches other llama-server processes. (d) `parse` helpers exported for tests: parse_bench_json, parse_completion_stderr, parse_buffer_split, parse_timings. All subcommands run under paths.bench_lock() and write results.write_result files named <experiment>_<model>_<variant>_<threads>_<ts>.json. Edge: llama-completion exit != 0 -> result with notes=['failed: <last stderr lines>'] and no tok/s; server never healthy -> same.
files.test: tests/test_bench_parse.py with checked-in fixtures: llama-bench JSON rows parsed (avg_ts/stddev_ts, n_threads); completion stderr lines parsed to load_s/pp/tg; buffer_split picks CPU_REPACK and CPU_Mapped MiB; server timings -> accept_rate and spec_active; a fake local HTTP server (threading.HTTPServer) exercises server-spec request/response shaping and the identical_to_plain logic without a model; variant->flags mapping exact strings.

files.language: Python (numpy; torch CPU for low-rank, imported lazily)
files.purpose: H2 step 1: load real Q4_0 matrices by byte range, dequantize, build cheap bases (2/3-bit group quant, low-rank), split the residual into input-column groups with per-group spectral-norm bounds and byte accounting.
files.spec: Quantization helpers: `dequant_q4_0(buf: bytes, n_rows, n_cols) -> np.float32[n_rows, n_cols]` (ggml layout: block of 32 = f16 scale d + 16 bytes; low nibbles are elements 0..15, high nibbles 16..31; value = d*(q-8); rows = ne[1], each row ne[0] contiguous) cross-checked bit-exactly against gguf.quants.dequantize; `load_matrix(map_or_gguf, tensor_name) -> np.float32[n_out, n_in]` reads only that tensor's byte range via np.memmap (y = W @ x; GGUF ne=[n_in, n_out]); `ffn_names(layer)` -> gate/up/down names; `group_quant(W, bits, block=32) -> (W_hat, bytes)` symmetric absmax per block with f16 scale (bytes/elem = bits/8 + 2/block; q2 = 0.3125, q3 = 0.4375, q4 = 0.5625); `lowrank(W, r) -> (U f16 [n_out,r], S, Vt f16 [r,n_in], bytes = 2*r*(n_in+n_out))` via torch.svd_lowrank(q=r+32, niter=3) (numpy fallback: randomized range finder). `decompose(W, base='q2'|'q3'|'lowrank256'|'lowrank512'|'q2+lowrank128', group_cols=128, res_bits=4|8|16) -> Decomp(W_base_hat f32, base_bytes, groups: list[Group(cols: slice, R_hat f32 [n_out, g] (residual quantized at res_bits per block 32, or exact for 16), bytes_g, norm2_g, normF_g)], total_residual_bytes, meta)`; norm2_g = largest singular value of R_g (np.linalg.svd(compute_uv=False) on [n_out, g], ~fast for g<=128), normF_g Frobenius. Memory discipline: one f32 matrix at a time (31B gate/up/down are 5376x21504 = 462 MB f32); residual groups stored as f16 to halve memory; explicit del + gc between matrices. CLI `python -m pigemma.h2.decompose --map traces/h2/map31.json --layers 5,20,35,50 --mats gate,up,down --bases q2,lowrank256 --group 128 --res-bits 4 --out traces/h2/decomp/` writes per (layer,mat,base) an .npz (W_base_hat f16, per-group R_hat f16 stacked [G, n_out, g], norm2[G], normF[G], bytes_g[G], base_bytes, cols) and prints bytes accounting vs Q4_0 (65,028,096 B per 31B matrix). Prints an ETA after the first matrix. Edge: n_in not divisible by group -> last group shorter (5376/128 = 42 exact; 21504/128 = 168 exact).
files.test: tests/test_h2_decompose.py: random f32 [64,256] -> gguf.quants.quantize(Q4_0) -> dequant_q4_0 equals gguf.quants.dequantize bit-exactly; group_quant(4) error <= Q4_0 reference error*1.05 on Gaussian data and bytes/elem formula; lowrank(r=min(dims)) reconstructs a rank-r matrix to 1e-4; decompose with res_bits=16: W_base_hat + sum_g R_g == W within 1e-5; bound soundness: for 1000 random x, ||R_g x_g|| <= norm2_g*||x_g|| always (and <= normF_g*||x_g||); bytes accounting = base + sum(bytes_g).

files.language: C++17 against llama-common + llama (built in Docker and on the Pi)
files.purpose: The one custom llama.cpp program (`pigemma-probe`): a cb_eval recorder with three modes (names, moe-trace, act-dump), teacher-forced replay of a fixed token stream, greedy generation, and per-token I/O accounting on Linux. Everything llama.cpp lacks for H1/H2 measurement, nothing else.
files.spec:
Pre-scan argv and pop probe flags before `common_params_parse(argc, argv, params, LLAMA_EXAMPLE_COMMON)`: `--mode names|moe-trace|act-dump` (required), `--trace-out F` (moe-trace), `--gen N` (greedy tokens after each chunk, default 0), `--probs-top K` (store top-K router probs from ffn_moe_probs, default 0), `--chunk-tokens N` (split the prompt into fresh-context chunks, default 1024), `--chat` (wrap each prompt in `<start_of_turn>user
…<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
`), `--gen-prompts FILE.json` (list of prompts, each a separate chunk with --gen), `--replay tokens.bin` (teacher-forced replay of an i32 stream; ignores -p/-f; split by --chunk-tokens and `--replay-chunks FILE` boundaries if given), `--replay-range A:B`, `--io-csv F` (Linux: per processed token/ubatch row 'token_index,phase,wall_ms,read_bytes_delta,majflt_delta,rss_anon_kb,rss_file_kb' from /proc/self/io, /proc/self/stat field 12, /proc/self/status), `--layers 5,20,35,50` and `--kinds ffn_norm,ffn_geglu,ffn_out` and `--tokens T` and `--act-out DIR` (act-dump), `--corpus-id S`. Standard args work: -m -f -p -t -c -b -ub -nr -lm -ctk -ctv -fa. Mandatory: params.cb_eval = probe_cb; params.cb_eval_user_data = &state; params.warmup = false (otherwise routing uses all experts, llama-graph.cpp:1473). Init: `auto init = common_init_from_params(params); model = init->model(); ctx = init->context();` vocab = llama_model_get_vocab; n_layer = llama_model_n_layer; arch = meta 'general.architecture'; n_expert/n_expert_used from meta `<arch>.expert_count` / `<arch>.expert_used_count` (0 => moe-trace refuses with a clear error). Callback `static bool probe_cb(ggml_tensor* t, bool ask, void* ud)`: parse name prefix (up to the last '-') and layer il = strtol after the last '-'; wanted set by mode: names -> on ask collect every name once into a std::set (return false), print sorted at exit; moe-trace -> {ffn_moe_topk, ffn_moe_weights_norm[, ffn_moe_probs]}; act-dump -> kinds x layers. On ask return true only for wanted names. On data: if !ggml_backend_buffer_is_host(t->buffer) use ggml_backend_tensor_get into a scratch buffer, else read t->data; ALWAYS honour nb[] strides: ffn_moe_topk is I32 ne=[K, T] with nb[1]=n_expert*4 (a view of the argsort); ffn_moe_weights_norm F32 ne=[1, K, T]; ffn_moe_probs F32 ne=[E, T]; activations F32 ne=[ne0, T] (each token vector contiguous when nb[0]==4). First sight of each name asserts type and ne[0]/ne[1] against expectations (K == n_expert_used, E == n_expert) else exit 4 with a message naming the tensor. Append the T columns to per-layer accumulators (std::vector per layer per kind). Processing loop per chunk: `llama_memory_clear(llama_get_memory(ctx), true)`; `common_batch batch = common_batch_get_one(ctx, tokens_chunk); if (llama_process(ctx, LLAMA_PROCESS_TYPE_DECODE, batch.get()) != 0) exit 3;` (n_batch >= chunk so one call; ubatches accumulate in order); after return assert every wanted layer accumulated exactly chunk_len columns (else exit 4 'layer %d got %d columns, expected %d'), flush one record per token (phase 0, pos = index in chunk, token_index = running counter, chunk_id = chunk number mod 256), append token ids to `<trace>.tokens.bin`, clear accumulators; then generation: `float* lg = llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1)`; argmax over llama_vocab_n_tokens; stop at llama_vocab_is_eog or N; `common_batch b = common_batch_get_one(ctx, &tok, 1)` (positions continue from memory) -> llama_process -> flush one record (phase 1, token_id = tok); accumulate the piece (common_token_to_piece) into `<trace>.gen.txt` with a '
--- chunk i ---
' separator. Trace file: header JSON written at start (format_version 1, model_name from meta general.name, gguf_path, gguf_size_bytes (stat), llama_build LLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER, llama_commit LLAMA_COMMIT, arch, n_layer, n_expert, n_expert_used, moe_layers (layers whose ffn_moe_topk was seen in the first chunk; record order), n_embd, probs_top, weights_tensor 'ffn_moe_weights_norm', corpus_id, created_at, n_ctx, n_batch, n_ubatch, n_threads, flags = argv, chunks: [{chunk_id, source, n_prompt, n_gen}] patched at close); n_records patched at close (also from a SIGINT handler). act-dump: for each (layer, kind) open DIR/L<il>.<kind>.npy with a fixed 128-byte npy v1.0 header '{"descr": "<f2", "fortran_order": False, "shape": (T_MAX, ne0), }' space-padded; append rows converted with ggml_fp32_to_fp16_row; at close rewrite shape with the real T and ftruncate; write DIR/meta.json {model, gguf_path, layers, kinds:{name: ne0}, n_tokens, phase_file 'phase.u8', tokens_file 'tokens.bin', chunks, llama_build, n_ubatch, flags}; stops after --tokens total tokens. Summary JSON on stderr at exit: n_prompt, n_gen, t_load_ms, t_p_eval_ms, t_eval_ms (llama_perf_context), tok/s, callback overhead (sum of time inside the callback). Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage, 3 load/compute failure, 4 tensor contract violation.
files.test: Integration (Docker, needs the 26B): `pc/trace_collect.sh --smoke` (64 prompt tokens + 8 generated) -> `python -m pigemma.trace validate` passes, n_records == 72, all layers 0..29 present, weights sum to 1; `--mode names` output contains ffn_moe_topk-0, ffn_moe_weights_norm-0, ffn_norm_2-0; act-dump smoke on the 31B with `--layers 0 --tokens 8` yields L0.ffn_geglu.npy shape (8, 21504) and L0.ffn_out.npy (8, 5376) loadable by numpy; the smoke trace is checked in as tests/fixtures/golden_26b_72tok.moetrace and validated by tests/test_trace.py. Unit: tests/test_pi_scripts.py checks the wrapper argv builders.

files.purpose: Hot-set pinning daemon: MAP_SHARED-maps the GGUF and mlocks the hot byte ranges so the kernel page cache keeps them resident for llama.cpp's own mapping of the same file while cold experts stream; verifies residency; reports and holds until SIGTERM.
files.spec: `pinner --gguf FILE --ranges hotset.ranges.txt [--verify] [--once] [--max-bytes N] [--pidfile P] [--json]`. Reads ranges file ('offset length' per line, '#' comments, decimal); page = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) (16384 on the Pi kernel); each range aligned down/up; total requested computed first and compared with --max-bytes and with MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo minus 512 MiB: refuse (exit 3) with the numbers if too large. open O_RDONLY, fstat, mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED) whole file; for each range: madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) then mlock(addr+off, len); on failure record errno (EPERM/ENOMEM -> RLIMIT_MEMLOCK: print getrlimit(RLIMIT_MEMLOCK) and the fix 'ulimit -l unlimited' / /etc/security/limits.d/90-pigemma.conf / CAP_IPC_LOCK; EAGAIN -> retry once after touching pages). --verify: mincore() per range -> resident bytes; print per-kind totals if the ranges file has '# kind=' comments, else total. Summary line (JSON with --json): {"requested_bytes","locked_bytes","resident_bytes","ranges","failed","page_size","memlock_limit","vm_lck_kb" (from /proc/self/status VmLck)}. Then: --once -> exit (locks released; warm-up only); else write pidfile, block in sigwait for SIGTERM/SIGINT, munlockall, munmap, remove pidfile, exit 0. Exit codes: 0 all locked, 2 partial (prints count), 3 refused/permission, 1 usage/IO error. No cross-process madvise claims (MADV_RANDOM from here does not affect llama.cpp's mapping); readahead is controlled by the device read_ahead_kb (pi/01). Builds with -Wall -Wextra -Werror; #error on non-Linux.
files.test: Integration in Docker (tests/test_pi_scripts.py @integration @linux): create a 64 MiB random file, ranges of 3 regions, run `pinner --verify --once --json` -> resident_bytes == requested (page-aligned) and VmLck > 0 during the run (checked via a --hold-seconds 2 debug flag); with `ulimit -l 64` -> exit 3 and the hint text; malformed ranges line -> exit 1.

files.language: bash (Git Bash on Windows -> Docker Desktop Linux)
files.purpose: The one Docker wrapper every pc/*.sh uses (fixes the MSYS path-mangling gotcha, memory/cpu caps, volumes) plus the tools build subcommand.
files.spec: `pc/docker_run.sh [--memory 6g] [--cpus 6] [--volume pigemma-models:/models:ro] [--name N] -- <command...>` => `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker run --rm -i $([ -t 0 ] && echo -t) -v "REPO_ROOT:/work" -w /work ${MEM:+--memory=$MEM --memory-swap=$MEM} ${CPUS:+--cpus=$CPUS} ${VOL:+-v $VOL} pi-gemma4-build:latest "$@"`. Repo path derived from the script location (`cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd -W`), image overridable via PIGEMMA_IMAGE. Refuses if `docker info` fails. Subcommand `build-tools [--clean]`: runs inside the container `cmake -S /work/tools -B /work/tools/build-linux-x86 -G Ninja -DLLAMA_DIR=/work/third_party/llama.cpp -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_AVX2=ON -DGGML_AVX512=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build /work/tools/build-linux-x86 -j12 --target pigemma-probe pinner membw`, then prints the three binary paths and `pigemma-probe --help | head -3`. Subcommand `vm-df`: prints `docker run --rm alpine df -B1 /` (VM root free bytes) and `docker system df`, used by pagecache_limit.sh to gate the volume copy. Exit code forwarded.
files.test: `pc/docker_run.sh -- ls /work/models` lists the model directories (bind mount non-empty); `pc/docker_run.sh build-tools` exits 0 and the binaries exist; `bash -n` in tests/test_pi_scripts.py.

files.purpose: Cheap quality metrics: KL-divergence vs the Q4_0 reference via llama-perplexity, the fixed Q&A set with Hebrew-aware grading, thinking-channel stripping, repetition/coherence check, and the lossless check for speculative variants.
files.spec: `strip_thinking(text) -> (visible, thinking_chars)`: removes `<|channel>thought ... <channel|>` blocks (DOTALL, also unterminated), a leading bare `<channel|>` or `<|channel>` token (observed in the server outputs), and `<end_of_turn>`; `is_coherent(text) -> (bool, reason)`: >= 60% of chars are letters/digits/space/punct, no 4-gram repeated >= 6 times, no 6-gram repeated > 3 times; `grade(item, visible) -> bool`: contains = any expected substring after normalisation (casefold, NFKC, Hebrew final forms ךםןףץ -> כמנפצ, strip niqqud U+0591-U+05C7, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation); regex = re.search; number = first number in the text within tolerance. `chat_wrap(user_text)` -> Gemma template. Subcommands: (a) `qa --model F --threads 6 [--server-variant plain|mtp|dflash] -n 160 --out results/quality/qa_<model>_<variant>.json`: uses bench.server-spec machinery (one server, 16 requests, temperature 0) or llama-completion per item when --no-server; records items [{id, lang, visible, thinking_chars, pass}], qa_score, qa_total, per-language scores, exact_match_vs_plain (fraction of items whose visible text equals the plain run's, None if plain not present); kind measured. (b) `kld-base --model F --text data/calibration/all.txt -c 512 --chunks 6 --out results/quality/ref_<model>.logits`: size_estimate = chunks*ctx*262144*2 bytes (6 chunks = 1.61 GB); refuses unless free disk >= 2*estimate (prints both numbers); runs `llama-perplexity -m F -f TEXT -c 512 --chunks N -t T --save-all-logits OUT`; verifies the file size afterwards. (c) `kld --model F --base results/quality/ref_<model>.logits --variant norepack|hybrid_negctrl|<quant-id> --out ...`: runs `llama-perplexity -m F -f TEXT -c 512 --chunks N -t T --kl-divergence --kl-divergence-base BASE [flags]`; parses `Mean    KLD: x ± y`, `Maximum KLD: x`, `99.9%   KLD: x`, `Mean PPL(Q)`, `Mean PPL(base)`, and the `Same top p` / `Mean Δp` lines (parser tolerant to spacing; missing -> None). (d) `ppl --model F ...` parses `Final estimate: PPL = x +/- y`. All model-loading paths under paths.bench_lock. Corpus: data/calibration/all.txt built by concatenating the existing calibration files (helper `build_corpus()`; sha256 recorded).
files.test: tests/test_quality.py: strip_thinking on fixtures incl. unterminated block and leading `<channel|>`; grader on Hebrew with final forms/niqqud and on numbers with tolerance; is_coherent flags a repetition loop; KLD/PPL line parsers on the checked-in fixture; disk gate arithmetic; exact_match_vs_plain computed on fixture outputs.

files.purpose: H2 step 2: with real FFN-input activations, measure per token how much residual an oracle needs, how much the norm bound certifies, soundness, the iso-byte competitor (plain lower-bit quant), and the implied Pi bytes/token; renders the H2 results markdown.
files.spec: Inputs: decomp .npz files, acts dir (meta.json, L<il>.ffn_norm.npy for gate/up, L<il>.ffn_geglu.npy for down, L<il>.ffn_out.npy for the sanity check, phase.u8). For each (layer, mat, base): X = rows of the matching kind (first --tokens tokens, both phases; stats reported separately for phase 0 (teacher-forced) and 1 (generated)); y_ref = W_q4 @ x (W_q4 = exact dequant of the Q4_0 matrix, the thing llama.cpp computes); SANITY (down only): rel_err(W_down_q4 @ geglu_t, ffn_out_t) median over tokens, expect < 0.03 (llama.cpp quantises activations to Q8 for the matmul); abort with a clear message if > 0.1 (orientation/scale bug). Per token (batched 32 tokens at a time to bound memory: contributions C[g] = R_g @ x_g for all groups = [G, n_out] per token): err_base = ||y_ref - W_base x|| / ||y_ref||; ORACLE: sort groups by ||C_g|| desc, add until rel error <= eps for eps in {0.01, 0.03, 0.10}; record k_oracle, residual byte fraction = sum(bytes_g selected)/total_residual_bytes, and the error-vs-bytes curve at byte fractions 0,0.05,...,1.0 (mean, p95 over tokens). BOUND: b_g = norm2_g * ||x_g||; certified-skip set = longest prefix of groups sorted by b_g ascending such that B = sum_prefix b_g <= eps * ||y_hat|| / (1+eps) where y_hat = y_ref - sum_prefix C_g (sound: ||y_ref - y_hat|| <= B and ||y_ref|| >= ||y_hat|| - B); record certified_skip_fraction (bytes), realised error after skipping (must be <= eps: soundness_violations counter must stay 0), certification_efficiency = certified bytes skipped / oracle bytes skipped at the same eps, tightness ratios ||C_g||/b_g (p10/p50/p90), Spearman rank correlation between b_g and ||C_g||. ISO-BYTE control: at byte budgets equal to uniform q2 and q3 full reads (and the oracle's bytes at eps=0.03), compare rel error of plain uniform group quant vs base+oracle vs base+certified. Aggregation: per (layer, mat, base, phase) means/p95; summary: median residual fraction at eps 0.03, median certification efficiency, implied bytes/token for 60 layers = 60*(sum over gate/up/down of base_bytes + mean selected residual bytes at eps 0.03) + attention 4,770,160,640 + head 1,156,076,544 (labelled PROJECTED/extrapolated from sampled layers) vs 17,635,166,448 (Q4_0) and 8.5e9 (IQ2_XXS); projected s/token on a Pi at 850 MB/s and at 10 GB/s in RAM; verdict PROMISING | WEAK | NOT_SUPPORTED | NO_ADVANTAGE by the E7 thresholds. CLI `python -m pigemma.h2.oracle --decomp traces/h2/decomp/ --acts traces/h2/acts/31b/ --tokens 512 --eps 0.01,0.03,0.10 --out results/h2/oracle.json --md docs/results/H2_RESULTS.md [--batch 32]`; prints ETA after the first matrix; writes JSON (schema data_formats 'h2.json', kind measured for errors/fractions, projected block with assumptions) and the markdown (tables: sanity, per layer/matrix/base fractions, bound tightness, iso-byte, extrapolation, verdict with the rule quoted).
files.test: tests/test_h2_oracle.py on synthetic [64,256] matrices and a synthetic acts dir: W with a planted residual concentrated in 10% of column groups -> oracle fraction <= 0.15 at eps 0.01 and certified set never contains a planted group; fraction non-increasing in eps; eps=inf -> 0 groups; W_base == W -> 0; soundness_violations == 0 over 200 random cases; Spearman in [-1,1]; sanity check passes on synthetic ffn_out = W_down @ geglu; markdown renders and contains the verdict string.

files.purpose: E3 driver: runs pigemma-probe --mode moe-trace in Docker on the calibration corpus plus generation prompts, in tiers sized for today, then validates, merges and computes stats.
files.spec: `pc/trace_collect.sh [--smoke|--quick|--full] [--gen N] [--threads 12] [--probs-top K] [--out traces/26b]`. Tiers: --smoke = first 64 tokens of en_tech + --gen 8 (validation only); --quick (default) = all data/calibration text/code files (concatenated per file, chunk 1024, --gen 128 per chunk; ~12-14k prefill + ~1.7k generated) + gen_prompts.json with --gen 256 (+2k generated); --full = quick with chunk 2048 and --gen 256 per chunk. One probe process per corpus file (fresh context per chunk inside): `pc/docker_run.sh -- python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold -- tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe --mode moe-trace -m /work/<26B> -f /work/data/calibration/<file> -nr -t 12 -c 4096 -b 2048 -ub 256 --chunk-tokens 1024 --gen N [--chat for gen prompts] [--probs-top K] --corpus-id <stem> --trace-out /work/traces/26b/<stem>.moetrace` (`-nr` so the 31 GB Docker VM holds the file in page cache instead of a 14 GB repack copy; warns that the first read through the bind mount takes minutes). After each run: `python -m pigemma.trace validate`; writes <stem>.meta.json (host, sha256_prefix of the GGUF, corpus sha256, argv, wall time, coherent flag of gen.txt via quality.is_coherent). Then `python -m pigemma.trace merge traces/26b/all.moetrace traces/26b/*.moetrace` and `python -m pigemma.trace stats traces/26b/all.moetrace --out traces/26b/all.stats.json --csv-dir results/h1/`. Prints the tok/s reported by the probe so the full tier can be sized. Refuses if the 26B file is missing or if results/.bench.lock is held.
files.test: --smoke passes validate with 72 records and all 30 layers; --quick asserts token_count >= 10000 prefill and >= 2000 generated and every chunk coherent; `bash -n`.

files.language: bash (host side + inner container script in the same file via --inner)
files.purpose: E5/E6: the desktop proxy for a RAM-limited Pi. Runs the probe in replay mode under a cgroup memory cap against the model in a Docker ext4 volume, measures real bytes read per token, and A/B tests hot-set pinning in the same cgroup; then compares with the simulator.
files.spec: `pc/pagecache_limit.sh [--mem 3,4,5,6,8] [--tokens traces/26b/all.moetrace] [--range 0:1500] [--pin] [--skip-copy] [--allow-bind-mount] [--out results/h1/validation.json]`. Step 0 gates: `pc/docker_run.sh vm-df` -> VM root free >= 16 GB AND Windows C: free >= 18 GB (the WSL2 vhdx grows on C:), else print 'docker builder prune would reclaim ~20 GB' and refuse unless --allow-bind-mount (bind-mount fallback: bytes/token = majflt*4096 lower bound only, results flagged notes=['bind-mount proxy: lower-bound bytes, timings not representative']). Step 1 (once): `docker volume create pigemma-models`; copy the 26B GGUF with `docker run --rm -v pigemma-models:/models -v <repo>:/work pi-gemma4-build cp /work/models/.../gemma-4-26B_q4_0-it.gguf /models/` showing progress; verify size. Step 2 per cap M: `pc/docker_run.sh --memory ${M}g --cpus 6 --volume pigemma-models:/models:ro -- bash /work/pc/pagecache_limit.sh --inner ...` where --inner (running in the container) does: record /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max, read_ahead_kb of the volume device if visible; `vmtouch -e /models/<gguf>` (cold start); fio tier characterisation once per cap: `fio --name=tier --filename=/models/<gguf> --rw=randread --bs=3345k --direct=1 --readonly --iodepth=1 --runtime=15 --time_based --output-format=json` -> tier_rand_read_3mb_mbps; optionally start `pinner --gguf /models/<gguf> --ranges /work/results/h1/hotset_<M>.ranges.txt --verify --json --pidfile /tmp/pinner.pid &` (hotset generated on the host beforehand with budget = M*1e9 - 0.6e9 anon - 0.3e9 slack, i.e. non-expert 1.577 GB + hottest experts) and wait for its summary; run `tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe --mode moe-trace -m /models/<gguf> --replay /work/traces/26b/all.moetrace.tokens.bin --replay-range A:B -ub 1 -nr -t 6 -c 2048 --io-csv /tmp/io.csv --trace-out /tmp/replay.moetrace` (ubatch 1 = decode-like access pattern identical to the simulator's sequence); after exit record /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.stat (anon, file, file_mapped), memory.events (oom_kill count -> run marked OOM), io.stat rbytes sum if present, exit code; also a plain `llama-completion -m /models/<gguf> -nr -t 6 -c 2048 -n 64 --temp 0 -f /work/data/calibration/en_tech_moe_streaming.txt` for a natural-generation tok/s under the cap; stop the pinner (SIGTERM to the pidfile only). Copies io.csv to results/h1/io_<M>[_pin].csv. Step 3 (host): `python -m pigemma.cache_sim traces/26b/all.moetrace --map results/map26.json --policies lru,belady --budgets-gb <M - anon_rss_measured - 1.577 - 0.1> --token-range A:B --warmup-tokens 200` and compare: measured bytes/token = mean read_bytes_delta over tokens after the warm-up window; ratio sim_lru/measured; time model: predicted tok/s with ram_bw calibrated from the uncapped (M=20 or native) run and storage_bw = tier measurement vs measured 1000/mean(wall_ms); writes results/h1/validation.json (points: [{mem_cap_bytes, pinned, anon_rss_bytes, file_cache_bytes, tier_mbps, measured_bytes_per_token, measured_majflt_per_token, sim_lru_bytes_per_token, sim_belady_bytes_per_token, ratio, measured_tok_s, predicted_tok_s, oom:bool}], kind measured + projected sub-blocks). Logs every gate decision.
files.test: Integration today (E5/E6 thresholds); `bash -n`; the comparison step is unit-tested in tests/test_cache_sim.py via a fixture io.csv.

files.language: bash (Debian 13 on the Pi; lint-tested under Git Bash)
files.purpose: Shared helpers and the single parameter file for all Pi scripts: fact collection into facts.json, production-host refusal, verdict gate, logging and exit-code conventions. Never kills or restarts anything; reads /proc and /sys only.
files.spec: pi_config.env (sourced first; every script prints the effective values): PIGEMMA_HOME (repo dir), MODEL_DIR (default $PIGEMMA_HOME/models; set to the NVMe mount), LLAMA_DIR (~/llama.cpp), LLAMA_COMMIT=a7b94df, THREADS=4, CTX=4096, QUANT_OVERRIDE=, OS_RESERVE_GIB=, MIN_FREE_DISK_FACTOR=1.1, DENY_HOSTS='context-friend-1', PROTECTED_SERVICE_GLOBS='contextfriend* context-friend*', TUNE_APPLY=0, TUNE_NVME_GEN3=0, TUNE_GOVERNOR=performance, TUNE_SWAPPINESS=10, TUNE_READAHEAD_KB=2048, TUNE_MEMLOCK=1, BUILD_JOBS=auto, HF_LIMIT_RATE=, PIN_BUDGET_BYTES=auto, PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=0. common.sh functions: `log`, `die <code> <msg>`, `need_cmd`, `collect_facts > pi/out/facts.json` (hostname, kernel, `getconf PAGESIZE`, cpu model + flags from /proc/cpuinfo (asimddp, i8mm, sve presence), nproc, MemTotal/MemAvailable/SwapTotal in kB, loadavg1, model_dir, storage: device via `findmnt -T $MODEL_DIR -o SOURCE`, type from the device name and sysfs: mmcblk* -> microsd, nvme* -> nvme with /sys/class/nvme/*/device/current_link_speed and current_link_width, sd* with transport usb (`lsblk -d -o TRAN`) -> usb-ssd else unknown, rotational flag, read_ahead_kb; free_disk via df -B1; running services from `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend`; hat from /proc/device-tree/hat/product if present; pciex1_gen from /boot/firmware/config.txt; governor; `ulimit -l`; tool versions cmake/gcc/git/python3; override='PIGEMMA_I_KNOW' when PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1), `assert_safe_host` (die 4 if hostname in DENY_HOSTS or a running service matches PROTECTED_SERVICE_GLOBS, unless PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1), `require_verdict_ok [--want X]` (runs `python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts pi/out/facts.json --json pi/out/feasibility.json`; die with its code if != 0 unless the caller allows 2), `pick_jobs` = min(nproc, floor(MemAvailable_GiB/1.2), 4), `fmt_gb`. Exit-code convention for every pi script: 0 ok, 2 only slow streaming possible, 3 not viable / precondition failed, 4 refused (protected or busy host). Testability: PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC=<dir> redirects /proc/meminfo, /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/loadavg, hostname and the systemctl/findmnt/lsblk/df outputs to fixture files so lib functions run under Git Bash.
files.test: tests/test_pi_scripts.py: `bash -n` on every pi/*.sh and pc/*.sh; with PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC=tests/fixtures/pi_proc_4gb collect_facts produces JSON with MemTotal 4039000, storage type microsd, page_size 16384 and assert_safe_host exits 4 (hostname context-friend-1); the 16 GB fixture passes.

files.purpose: Desktop driver for E0 (bench matrix + repack/mmap evidence), E1 (speculative via llama-server) and E2 (quality: KLD + Q&A) using the native Windows binaries, resumable and time-boxed.
files.spec: `.\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage bench,spec,quality [-Models 26b,31b] [-Threads 4,6,12] [-Quick] [-Force] [-AllowDownload] [-DryRun]`. Results dir results/<yyyy-mm-dd>/; a stage/model/variant is skipped if its result file exists unless -Force; -DryRun prints command lines. Stage bench (E0): `python -m pigemma.bench matrix --model <id> --threads 4,6,12 --pp 128 --tg 32 -r 3 --variants default,norepack,hybrid_negctrl,nommap` (31B: threads 6,12, -r 2, tg 16; -Quick: threads 6 only, r 1) then `bench completion` per variant (-n 64, 6 threads, EN prompt) to capture load_s, working-set/private peaks and the buffer_split lines; then asserts the E0 gate: norepack run shows CPU_Mapped MiB >= 0.95 * file MiB and no CPU_REPACK line, private peak < 1.5 GB; hybrid_negctrl shows a CPU_REPACK line (documents that -ot does not stream); prints PASS/FAIL per gate and writes results/<date>/E0_GATE.md. Stage spec (E1): `python -m pigemma.bench server-spec --model 26b-q4 --variant plain,mtp,dflash,ngram -n 200`; if mtp reports spec_active=false run mtp-explicit (`--spec-type draft-mtp`) and dflash-explicit; 31B: plain, mtp, mtp-explicit; records speedup vs plain, accept_rate, identical_to_plain (via quality.visible_text), spec_type_effective. Stage quality (E2): builds data/calibration/all.txt, `python -m pigemma.quality kld-base` per model (6 chunks, disk-gated), `kld --variant norepack` and `--variant hybrid_negctrl` per model (expect ~0), `qa` per model (plain; and mtp/dflash variants only if spec_active was true); with -AllowDownload and >= 1.3x free disk, downloads one lower quant per model via huggingface_hub (26b UD-Q3_K_M, 31b UD-IQ2_XXS) and runs kld + qa on it (default off: D: has 32 GB free). Each step runs under the bench lock (the python side enforces it); the script never runs two model jobs at once and prints free disk before each heavy step. Ends with `python -m pigemma.results summarize results/<date> --md docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>.md`.
files.test: -DryRun prints every command; parsing covered by tests/test_bench_parse.py and tests/test_quality.py; integration today.

files.purpose: Step 0 on any Pi: read-only fact collection + verdict table + recommendation; the only script allowed to run on an unknown or protected host; exit code gates everything heavier.
files.spec: `pi/00_feasibility.sh [--want 26b|31b] [--json pi/out/feasibility.json] [--sim results/h1/sim.json]`. Sources pi_config.env + lib/common.sh; collect_facts; runs `python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts pi/out/facts.json --catalog pigemma/data/catalog.json [--want] [--sim] --json ...` and prints: host facts (RAM total/available, storage type + link speed + read_ahead_kb, free disk, page size, CPU flags with 'asimddp: yes, i8mm: no' style, kernel, governor, HAT product if any, protected-host flag), the per-model verdict table with projected tok/s and its source (assumed curve or sim), the recommended model/quant/flags, and the fixed recommendation line (16 GB + NVMe Gen3 = fits; 8 GB + NVMe = stream; 4 GB/microSD = not viable; 31B dense never good speed). Never modifies anything; exit code = verdict code (0/2/3/4). Prints a loud banner when the host is protected (the probed context-friend-1) and that all other scripts will refuse.
files.test: Fixture-driven: PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC 4 GB fixture -> exit 3/4 table printed; 16 GB fixture -> exit 0; `bash -n`; also runs inside the Docker image (generic Linux: storage unknown tolerated).

files.purpose: Print-first OS tuning for the Pi: NVMe Gen3, governor, swappiness, read-ahead, memlock limits; refuses on protected hosts and when an AI HAT occupies the PCIe lane.
files.spec: `pi/01_tune_os.sh [--apply] [--no-pcie]` (TUNE_* flags from pi_config.env select items). Shows current vs proposed for: (a) /boot/firmware/config.txt `dtparam=pciex1_gen=3` under [all] — only if an NVMe is present AND /proc/device-tree/hat/product and lspci do not show Hailo/'AI HAT' (then prints 'PCIe lane used by the AI HAT: NVMe impossible without a dual-slot HAT' and skips); appended once (grep guard); prints REBOOT REQUIRED, never reboots; (b) governor performance via /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy*/scaling_governor + a systemd oneshot unit pigemma-governor.service to persist; (c) /etc/sysctl.d/90-pigemma.conf vm.swappiness=10, vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50 + sysctl --system; (d) read_ahead_kb on the model device (/sys/block/<dev>/queue/read_ahead_kb -> TUNE_READAHEAD_KB; expert slabs are 1.1-2.2 MB contiguous) + a udev rule for persistence; (e) /etc/security/limits.d/90-pigemma.conf '* soft memlock unlimited' / hard + /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/pigemma.conf DefaultLimitMEMLOCK=infinity (note: re-login needed); (f) advice only: zram/swap, Active Cooler (throttling at 80 C). Dry run prints the exact commands; --apply executes idempotently and prints before/after values. assert_safe_host first (exit 4).
files.test: `bash -n`; dry-run inside Docker prints the plan without touching files; a fixture test ensures the config.txt line is not duplicated on a second --apply (grep guard) using a temp copy via PIGEMMA_BOOT_CONFIG override.

files.purpose: Native llama.cpp + pigemma tools build on the Pi at the pinned commit, RAM-aware, refusing on protected hosts.
files.spec: `pi/02_build_llama.sh [--commit a7b94df] [--jobs N] [--with-tools] [--from-desktop user@host:REPO_ROOT/third_party/llama.cpp]`. Preconditions: assert_safe_host; free disk >= 3 GB; MemAvailable >= 1.5 GB; cmake/gcc/git present (apt hint otherwise). Source: `git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp $LLAMA_DIR && git -C $LLAMA_DIR fetch --depth 1 origin $COMMIT && git -C $LLAMA_DIR checkout $COMMIT` (or rsync --from-desktop). Configure: `cmake -S $LLAMA_DIR -B $LLAMA_DIR/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF`; if configure fails on arch detection retry with `-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16`. Build: `nice -n 10 cmake --build $LLAMA_DIR/build -j $(pick_jobs) --target llama-cli llama-completion llama-bench llama-perplexity llama-server` (jobs = min(nproc, floor(MemAvailable_GiB/1.2)); 2 on a 4 GB board). --with-tools: `cmake -S $PIGEMMA_HOME/tools -B $PIGEMMA_HOME/tools/build -DLLAMA_DIR=$LLAMA_DIR -DGGML_NATIVE=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build ... --target pigemma-probe pinner membw`. Prints binary paths and `llama-bench --help | head -1`; records versions into pi/out/build.json.
files.test: `bash -n`; the identical CMake invocations (minus the ARM arch string) are exercised in Docker by `pc/docker_run.sh build-tools`.

files.purpose: Measures the two constants the projections depend on, storage random-read at expert-slab granularity and memory bandwidth, and writes them where the catalog loader overrides the assumed values.
files.spec: `pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh [--file <path>] [--size-mb 2048] [--seconds 20] [--quick]`. assert_safe_host; free disk >= 1.2x size unless --file points at an existing GGUF (read-only use). fio jobs (--output-format=json, --direct=1, --readonly when using a GGUF): seq read bs=1M iodepth=1 and 8; randread bs=3345k iodepth=1 and 4 (expert-slab size); randread bs=16k iodepth=1 (16 KiB page faults, IOPS); each --runtime=$SECONDS --time_based. membw: `tools/build/bin/membw --size-mb 512 --threads 1,2,4 --json`. Writes results/pi/io_mem.json (schema data_formats) with host facts, device, and for each metric {value, unit, source:'measured', cmd}; prints a table and the derived numbers: in-RAM ceiling tok/s for the 26B = mem_bw_read*0.65/2.38 GB (eff flagged assumed until pi/05 calibrates it), streamed MB/token the storage can serve per second. Deletes the fio test file afterwards. fio missing -> prints the apt command and uses a dd fallback for seq read only (flagged).
files.test: `bash -n`; fio job strings validated with `fio --parse-only` in Docker; tests/test_catalog.py checks the merge of a fixture io_mem.json into the device profile.

files.purpose: Downloads the quant the verdict recommends (or an explicit one) with resume, size and sha256 verification, plus the draft sidecar, within the disk budget; or rsyncs from the desktop over LAN.
files.spec: `pi/04_fetch_model.sh [--model 26b|31b] [--quant auto|Q4_0|UD-Q3_K_M|...] [--draft] [--dest $MODEL_DIR] [--from-desktop user@host:REPO_ROOT/models] [--dry-run]`. assert_safe_host; `eval $(python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts pi/out/facts.json --emit env [--want])` unless --quant given (then catalog lookup); refuses placeholder filenames (catalog-refresh needed) and free disk < MIN_FREE_DISK_FACTOR x bytes; prints URL, size and ETA at a measured 10 MB/s probe (first 20 MB timed). Download: `curl -L -C - --retry 10 --retry-delay 5 ${HF_LIMIT_RATE:+--limit-rate $HF_LIMIT_RATE} -o $DEST/$FILE https://huggingface.co/$REPO/resolve/main/$FILE`; verify byte size == catalog bytes; sha256 verified when the catalog has one (from catalog-refresh) or the response's x-linked-etag carries it; --draft fetches the family's MTP sidecar the same way. --from-desktop uses `rsync -aP --partial`. Writes pi/out/fetch.json {model_id, file, bytes, sha256_verified, seconds}.
files.test: `bash -n`; --dry-run selection matrix through the feasibility fixtures (16 GB -> 26b Q4_0; 8 GB NVMe -> 26b Q4_0 streaming; 4 GB -> refuses); URL construction unit test in tests/test_pi_scripts.py.

files.purpose: Run / bench / stream-bench on the Pi with the verdict's flags: llama-bench variants (default vs -nr), a completion run that measures real bytes read per token, and the chat/server modes.
files.spec: `pi/05_run.sh bench|stream-bench|chat|server [--model <gguf>] [--draft <gguf>] [--variants default,norepack] [--pin] [-p 'text']`. assert_safe_host; require_verdict_ok (allows 2); flags from pi/out/feasibility.json (`-nr` whenever not FITS_REPACKED). bench: `llama-bench -m $MODEL -t 2,3,4 -p 64 -n 32 -r 3 -o json [--repack 0] [-lm ...]` per variant (refuses the default/repack variant when FITS_REPACKED is false — it would allocate a 14 GB anon copy) -> results/pi/bench_<variant>.json via `python3 -m pigemma.bench parse-bench` (same envelope as the desktop). stream-bench: `llama-completion -m $MODEL $LLAMA_FLAGS -n 64 --temp 0 -f data/calibration/en_tech_moe_streaming.txt` wrapped by `python3 -m pigemma.bench completion` which on Linux samples /proc/<pid>/io read_bytes, majflt, RssAnon/RssFile and `vmstat 1` during generation -> read_bytes_per_token, tok/s, and prints the EN+HE sample output; --pin starts pi/06 first. chat: `llama-cli -m $MODEL $LLAMA_FLAGS [-md $DRAFT]`; server: `llama-server -m $MODEL $LLAMA_FLAGS --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 [-md $DRAFT]`. Refuses (exit 3) if MemAvailable < nonexpert_bytes + 0.5 GB (streaming) or < file bytes + 0.5 GB (fits mode). Calibration: writes the measured in-RAM efficiency (tg * bytes/token / membw) into results/pi/calibration.json for cache_sim projections.
files.test: `bash -n`; argument parsing and refusal paths with the fake-proc fixtures; bench parse covered by tests/test_bench_parse.py.

files.language: PowerShell 5.1 (calls bash for the Docker step)
files.purpose: E7 driver: activation capture of the 31B in Docker, then decompose -> oracle -> markdown natively on Windows, with sampling knobs that keep it under one hour.
files.spec: `.\pc\h2_run.ps1 [-Layers 5,20,35,50] [-Tokens 512] [-Group 128] [-Bases q2,lowrank256] [-ResBits 4] [-Force] [-SkipActs] [-Quick]`. Refuses > 8 layers or > 1024 tokens without -Force (prints the ETA formula: ~60 s per (layer,matrix,base) on the 8400F). Step 1 (unless -SkipActs or acts exist): `bash pc/docker_run.sh -- python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold -- tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe --mode act-dump -m /work/<31B> -f /work/data/calibration/all.txt --chunk-tokens 384 --gen 128 -nr -t 12 -c 1024 -b 512 -ub 128 --layers <L> --kinds ffn_norm,ffn_geglu,ffn_out --tokens <T> --act-out /work/traces/h2/acts/31b` (prefill 384 + 128 generated per chunk until T tokens; both phases recorded). Step 2: `python -m pigemma.gguf_map build <31B> --out traces/h2/map31.json` (cached), `python -m pigemma.h2.decompose --map ... --layers <L> --mats gate,up,down --bases <B> --group <G> --res-bits <R> --out traces/h2/decomp/`. Step 3: `python -m pigemma.h2.oracle --decomp traces/h2/decomp/ --acts traces/h2/acts/31b/ --tokens <T> --eps 0.01,0.03,0.10 --out results/h2/oracle.json --md docs/results/H2_RESULTS.md`. -Quick: layers 20,45; tokens 128; bases q2; group 128. Prints wall time per step and the verdict line at the end.
files.test: Pipeline unit-tested with synthetic acts (tests/test_h2_oracle.py); -Quick integration today once the probe is built.

files.purpose: A/B of hot-set pinning on the Pi: generates the ranges from the desktop trace statistics, runs the pinner, benchmarks hybrid streaming with and without it, reports read_bytes/token and tok/s for both.
files.spec: `pi/06_pin_hotset.sh start|stop|status|ab [--model <gguf>] [--map results/map26.json] [--stats traces/26b/all.stats.json] [--budget-bytes N]`. assert_safe_host; requires `ulimit -l` unlimited (points at pi/01). Budget auto = MemAvailable - KV(ctx) - 0.3e9 compute - 0.5e9 headroom (the non-expert 1.577 GB is part of the pinned set). start: `python3 -m pigemma.gguf_map hotset --map $MAP --stats $STATS --budget-bytes $B --page-size $(getconf PAGESIZE) --out pi/out/hotset.json` (map built on the Pi from the local GGUF if absent; falls back to non-expert-only pinning when no stats are shipped), then `nohup tools/build/bin/pinner --gguf $MODEL --ranges pi/out/hotset.ranges.txt --verify --json --pidfile pi/out/pinner.pid > pi/out/pinner.log &`, waits for the summary line, prints locked/resident bytes and expert coverage. stop: SIGTERM to pi/out/pinner.pid only. status: VmLck of that pid + mincore summary via `pinner --verify --once`. ab: runs `pi/05_run.sh stream-bench` unpinned, then start, stream-bench again, stop; writes results/pi/pin_ab.json with both tok/s and read_bytes_per_token and the ratio.
files.test: `bash -n`; hotset unit tests; the same code path exercised in Docker by pc/pagecache_limit.sh --pin.

files.purpose: Honest front page: goal, non-goals, what is measured vs projected, quick start for desktop (today) and Pi (later), repository map, and the recommendation.
files.spec: Sections: What this is (download a full Gemma 4 and run it on a Pi 5 'with good speed and quality' is the question, not the claim); The two models and their byte budgets (table from gguf_map: 26B-A4B 1.577 GB non-expert incl. the 0.606 GB tied head + 803 MB/token worst-case experts; 31B 17.64 GB/token); The one llama.cpp fact everything depends on (default repack copies weights out of the mmap; `-nr` is the only streaming mode at a7b94df; `-ot ...=CPU` still repacks — with line references); Honest status table with MEASURED / PROJECTED / ASSUMED columns (desktop numbers from results/desktop-baseline-2026-10-04.md and docs/results/*, Pi projections from E4, assumptions from the catalog); Hypotheses H1/H2 in one paragraph each with a link to docs/HYPOTHESES.md and the pre-registered thresholds; Quick start desktop: `pip install -e . && pytest`, `bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools`, `.\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage bench,spec,quality`, `bash pc/trace_collect.sh --quick`, `python -m pigemma.cache_sim ...`, `bash pc/pagecache_limit.sh --mem 4,5,6,8 --pin`, `.\pc\h2_run.ps1`; Quick start Pi: pi/00 -> 06 in order with the refusal rules; The plain statements: the dense 31B cannot reach good speed on any Pi 5 with known post-training techniques (17.6 GB/token: ~22 s/token from NVMe Gen3, ~1.3 tok/s even if it were all in a 16 GB board's RAM — which it is not), H2 is a measurement; the MoE is the realistic tier and Pi 5 16 GB + NVMe Gen3 is the configuration where it fits in RAM; Repository map; Safety: never run heavy scripts on context-friend-1 (deny-listed). Links to every doc.
files.test: tests/test_docs.py: all relative links resolve; the numbers quoted for the byte budgets match pigemma/data/catalog.json.

files.purpose: H1 and H2 stated as falsifiable hypotheses with the arithmetic, the Pi 5 hardware budget tables, what each configuration implies in tok/s, and what would change our minds.
files.spec: H1 (MoE small active set): per-token traffic model t = resident/mem_bw + miss_bytes/storage_bw + n_miss*latency; what a cache must achieve at each Pi budget (expert cache bytes per profile from the catalog formula; 8 GB NVMe ~5.2 GB = 40% of experts); literature priors (LRU 15%->60%, 25%->74%, 35%->84%, 45%->88%; Qwen3-30B-A3B reuse 0.444) flagged as priors to be replaced by E3/E4; pre-registered thresholds (E3 coverage@32 >= 0.70 strong skew; E4 STREAM_GOOD if tg_overlap >= 2.0 and tg_serial >= 1.0 with LRU; E5 sim within +-30%; E6 pinning >= 15%). H2 (dense staged residuals): W = W_base + sum_g R_g, bound ||R_g x_g|| <= ||R_g||_2 ||x_g||_2, why groups are input-column groups stored group-major, expected looseness ~1/sqrt(g) for random directions, the oracle definition, the sound certification rule used in oracle.py, the iso-byte competitor, thresholds (PROMISING only if residual fraction <= 25% at eps 3% AND certification efficiency >= 50% AND implied bytes/token < 8.5 GB), and the non-promise: even a perfect H2 leaves attention + head = 5.9 GB/token. Hardware budget section: Pi 5 physics with sources (LPDDR4X ~10 GB/s effective, microSD 85-90 MB/s, USB3 SSD 360-416 MB/s, NVMe Gen2 x1 ~450, Gen3 x1 784-894 MB/s; Cortex-A76 dotprod yes, i8mm/SVE no; 16 KiB pages; one PCIe lane: Hailo HAT excludes NVMe), RAM worksheets per configuration (OS reserve, non-expert resident, KV at 4096 ctx q8_0 ~160 MB, compute buffers, expert cache), the desktop calibration (MoE 15.18 tok/s x 2.38 GB = 36 GB/s effective; 31B 2.44 x 17.64 = 43 GB/s), the in-RAM ceiling on a Pi (~10 GB/s x eff / 2.38 GB = 2.7-4 tok/s) and the dense line (17.64 GB/token). Every constant here is the same as in pigemma/data/catalog.json.

data_formats.name: .moetrace (expert routing trace, binary, little-endian)
data_formats.spec: HEADER: bytes 0-7 magic ASCII 'MOETRC01'; 8-11 u32 header_json_len (UTF-8 JSON, space-padded to a multiple of 8); 12-15 u32 record_size; 16-23 u64 n_records (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF while open, patched at close; readers infer from file size and flag truncated=True if unpatched); 24-31 u64 reserved=0; then the JSON header; records begin at 32 + header_json_len. JSON header keys (all required): format_version:1, model_name, gguf_path, gguf_size_bytes, llama_build:11398, llama_commit:'a7b94df', arch:'gemma4', n_layer:30, n_expert:128, n_expert_used:8, moe_layers:[0..29] (record order), n_embd:2816, probs_top:P (0 = none), weights_tensor:'ffn_moe_weights_norm', corpus_id, created_at (ISO UTC), n_ctx, n_batch, n_ubatch, n_threads, flags:[argv], chunks:[{chunk_id, source, n_prompt, n_gen}] (patched at close). RECORD (fixed size = 16 + L*K*3 + L*P*3 bytes; 26B with P=0: 736 B): u32 token_index (0-based position in this trace's token stream = index into tokens.bin) | u32 pos (position inside its chunk/context) | i32 token_id (the INPUT token at that position) | u8 phase (0 = prefill/teacher-forced, 1 = generated) | u8 chunk_id | u16 reserved=0 | for each il in moe_layers: K x u8 expert_id in ffn_moe_topk order (descending prob) then K x f16 normalised routing weight (ffn_moe_weights_norm; sum ~ 1) | if P>0, for each il: P x (u8 id, f16 prob) descending from softmax(ffn_moe_probs). Invariants enforced by validate(): ids < n_expert, K distinct ids per (token, layer), weights finite and sum within 0.02 of 1, token_index contiguous from 0, n_expert <= 256. Sidecars next to the trace: `<stem>.tokens.bin` (raw i32 LE token ids in stream order, one per record), `<stem>.gen.txt` (generated text per chunk), `<stem>.meta.json` (host fingerprint, gguf sha256_prefix, corpus files + sha256, argv, wall_ms, tok/s, callback_overhead_ms, coherent:bool), `<stem>.stats.json` (see stats.json).
