experiments.hypothesis: Both Q4_0 models run end-to-end on the 8400F; the MoE is bandwidth-bound and peaks at 4 threads (~15 tok/s), the dense 31B at ~2.4 tok/s; `-nr` keeps the whole file CPU_Mapped with anon RSS < 1.5 GB at a measurable kernel penalty, while `-ot "ffn_(gate_up|down)_exps=CPU"` still repacks (negative control). Variants differ in speed, not output.
experiments.procedure: .\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage bench: llama-bench.exe -t 4,6,12 -p 128 -n 32 -r 3 -o json for variants default / --repack 0 / -ot hybrid_negctrl / -lm none on both GGUFs (31B: -t 6,12, -n 16, -r 2); then llama-completion.exe -n 64 --temp 0 per variant capturing load time, working-set and private-bytes peaks and the 'load_tensors: <buft> model buffer size' lines.
metrics: pp128 and tg tok/s per thread count and variant (mean, sd)
buffer_split: CPU_REPACK vs CPU_Mapped MiB per variant
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~35 min (31B dominates)
experiments.thresholds: PASS if 26B tg@4t within +-20% of 15.18 and tg@6t within +-20% of 13.5 (idle-machine reference), 31B tg@6t within +-20% of 2.44; REPACK GATE PASS if the norepack variant logs CPU_Mapped >= 95% of the file size with no CPU_REPACK line and private peak < 1.5 GB, AND hybrid_negctrl logs a CPU_REPACK line (confirms -ot does not stream). If the gate fails, stop all streaming work (E5/E6/Pi) until the flags are fixed. The norepack penalty is reported as the cost of streaming mode (expected 10-40%).

experiments.hypothesis: At b11398 the Gemma 4 MTP sidecars load but do not draft in the server slot (ad-hoc evidence), DFlash drafts at ~28% acceptance and is slower on the CPU-bound MoE; an explicit `--spec-type` may activate MTP; any active drafter must be greedy-lossless.
experiments.procedure: .\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage spec: pigemma.bench server-spec on the 26B for plain, mtp, mtp-explicit (--spec-type draft-mtp), dflash, dflash-explicit, ngram (--spec-type ngram-simple) and on the 31B for plain, mtp, mtp-explicit; 8 prompts, -n 200, temperature 0, -t 6, -c 4096; record timings.draft_n / draft_n_accepted per request and compare visible text with the plain run.
metrics: tg tok/s per variant and speedup vs plain
spec_active (draft_n > 0 on every request) and spec_type_effective
load_time_s and peak private bytes with the draft loaded
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~30 min
experiments.thresholds: A variant counts as ACTIVE only if spec_active; report 'useful' if speedup >= 1.2x with identical_to_plain >= 0.95 on >= 6 of 8 prompts; 'inactive' (MTP never drafting) and 'slower' (DFlash) are recorded as findings, not failures; any non-identical greedy output with an active drafter is a bug noted in results and that draft is excluded from the Pi recommendation.

experiments.hypothesis: -nr and the -ot negative control are numerically identical to the default run (KLD ~ 0); both Q4_0 models answer the fixed EN/HE/arithmetic set; lower quants (optional) degrade measurably.
experiments.procedure: .\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage quality: llama-perplexity.exe --save-all-logits on data/calibration/all.txt (-c 512 --chunks 6 = 1.61 GB per model, disk-gated) for each Q4_0 model; --kl-divergence --kl-divergence-base for variants norepack and hybrid_negctrl (and a lower quant only with -AllowDownload and >= 1.3x free disk); pigemma.quality qa (16 items) per model via llama-server, plus mtp/dflash variants only when E1 found them active.
metrics: KLD mean / max / p99.9 and same-top-p per variant
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~40 min for both models (+30 min per optional quant)
experiments.thresholds: PASS: norepack and hybrid_negctrl KLD mean < 0.001 and same-top-p > 99.5% (proves the streaming mode is numerically neutral); qa_score >= 13/16 for both models and Hebrew subset >= 4/6 (else document a Hebrew caveat). Quant tiers for the Pi recommendation: KLD mean < 0.05 'acceptable', < 0.15 'degraded', else 'not recommended'.

experiments.hypothesis: Expert routing on real mixed EN/HE/code text is skewed and temporally sticky: per layer, the 32 hottest of 128 experts cover >= 70% of selections and >= 40% of a token's experts were used by the previous token in the same layer; Hebrew and code use partly different experts than English.
experiments.procedure: bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools; bash pc/trace_collect.sh --smoke (validate 72 records, commit as golden fixture); bash pc/trace_collect.sh --quick (all calibration files, chunk 1024, --gen 128 per chunk, plus 8 gen prompts x 256, -nr -t 12 -ub 256, warmup off); merge; python -m pigemma.trace stats.
metrics: n_prefill, n_gen, all 30 layers present, validate() clean
per-layer coverage@8/16/32/48/64 (count and weight mass), entropy, Gini
adjacent reuse and Jaccard, working sets
cross-layer predictor precision@16 vs static and same-ids baselines
per-corpus top-32 overlap (EN vs HE vs code)
experiments.runtime_estimate: build 5-8 min; smoke 3 min (first bind-mount read of the GGUF dominates); quick ~20-25 min
experiments.thresholds: Trace VALID if validate() passes, >= 10k prefill + >= 2k generated tokens, generated text coherent. H1 precondition MET ('strong skew') if mean coverage@32 >= 0.70 or adjacent reuse >= 0.40; 'moderate' 0.5-0.7; 'near-uniform' < 0.5 (then LRU alone is the plan and static hot sets are dropped). Prefetch worth modelling only if predictor precision@16 beats the static baseline by >= 0.1.

experiments.hypothesis: At the 8 GB + NVMe Gen3 budget (~5.2 GB expert cache, ~40% of experts) LRU reaches >= 60% hit rate on real text (miss bytes <= ~320 MB/token) giving a projected 1.5-2.5 tok/s streaming; 4 GB / microSD is < 0.3 tok/s under every policy; 16 GB holds everything and is RAM-bandwidth-bound at ~3-4 tok/s.
experiments.procedure: python -m pigemma.cache_sim traces/26b/all.moetrace --map results/map26.json --policies lru,lfu,static,belady,lru_prefetch,lru_perlayer --budgets-gb 0.5,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,12.85 --profiles all --train-split 0.3 --warmup-tokens 256 --out results/h1/sim.json; projections use the catalog device profiles (assumed) and the desktop-calibrated llama_efficiency; python -m pigemma.results summarize -> docs/results/H1_RESULTS.md.
metrics: hit_rate, weighted_hit_rate, miss MB/token (mean, p95) per policy x budget
Belady gap = LRU miss bytes / Belady miss bytes
projected tg_serial and tg_overlap per Pi profile with assumptions listed (kind=projected)
stack-distance curve vs simulator LRU agreement
experiments.runtime_estimate: < 10 min
experiments.thresholds: Decision rule for the Pi recommendation: a configuration is 'viable for streaming' if LRU (no oracle) gives tg_overlap >= 2.0 and tg_serial >= 1.0 tok/s; 'weak' if tg_serial 0.5-1.0; else not viable. Belady reported as the upper bound only. If LRU bytes/token > 1.5x Belady, prefetch/static policies are worth implementing on the Pi; if static is within 10% of LRU, hot-set pinning is the simpler deployment. Any projection whose inputs are still 'assumed' is printed with that word.

experiments.hypothesis: With `-nr`, the simulator's LRU bytes/token predicts real page-cache behaviour within +-30% when the cache budget equals the cgroup limit minus anon RSS minus the resident non-expert bytes, and the time model predicts tok/s within +-35% using the measured proxy tier bandwidth.
experiments.procedure: bash pc/pagecache_limit.sh --mem 3,4,5,6,8 --range 0:1500: 26B GGUF copied once into the ext4 Docker volume (VM/C: disk gated), per cap: vmtouch -e, fio randread bs=3345k on the volume (tier bandwidth), pigemma-probe --replay all.moetrace.tokens.bin -ub 1 -nr -t 6 --io-csv under --memory=<N>g --memory-swap=<N>g --cpus 6, record /proc/self/io read_bytes and majflt per token, cgroup memory.stat and memory.events (OOM detection), plus a plain llama-completion -nr -n 64 tok/s; compare with cache_sim lru/belady at budget = cap - anon_rss - 1.577 GB - 0.1 GB on the same token range after a 200-token warm-up.
metrics: measured read bytes per token and majflt per token per cap
measured tok/s (replay -ub 1 and natural generation) per cap
sim LRU and Belady bytes/token at the matching budget and the ratio
experiments.runtime_estimate: volume copy ~10-15 min once; ~5 min per cap (load storm under the cap + 1500 tokens at -ub 1) -> ~45 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS if |sim_lru/measured - 1| <= 0.30 for caps 4-8 GB and measured lies within [0.8 x Belady, 1.3 x LRU]; time model PASS if |predicted/measured - 1| <= 0.35 on >= 3 caps. If measured >> sim: readahead inflation (record the VM device read_ahead_kb, feed the inflation factor into --read-granularity and document). If measured << sim: the kernel keeps more than the limit charged (compare memory.stat file vs anon) -> adjust the budget formula and document. Any OOM means repack leaked (check buffer_split) -> fix before continuing.

experiments.hypothesis: mlock-pinning the non-expert weights plus the hottest experts beats plain page-cache LRU at the same memory cap by >= 15% tok/s or >= 20% fewer bytes/token, because LRU otherwise evicts always-needed attention/head/dense pages under pressure.
experiments.procedure: Same as E5 at caps 5 and 6 GB with --pin: hotset from results/map26.json + all.stats.json at budget = cap - 0.6 GB anon - 0.3 GB slack (non-expert 1.577 GB first, then hottest experts), pinner --verify in the same container/cgroup before the run, compared against the unpinned run of E5.
metrics: pinner resident fraction (mincore) before and after the run
experiments.runtime_estimate: ~20 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS if pinned tg >= 1.15x unpinned at 5 GB OR bytes/token reduced >= 20%. If no gain, document that the kernel LRU already keeps the hot pages and make pinning optional (not default) in pi/05; if the pinner cannot lock the full budget (exit 2), report the achieved fraction.

experiments.hypothesis: For the dense 31B, W = W_base + sum R_g with a cheap base (2-bit group quant or rank-256) needs only a minority of residual bytes per token to keep FFN output error <= 3%, the norm bound certifies a useful share of the skippable groups, and this beats plain lower-bit quantisation at equal bytes. Expected honest outcome: the bound is loose (~1/sqrt(g)) and the bytes saved do not approach what a Pi needs.
experiments.procedure: .\pc\h2_run.ps1 -Layers 5,20,35,50 -Tokens 512 -Group 128 -Bases q2,lowrank256: act-dump of ffn_norm / ffn_geglu / ffn_out in Docker (-nr, 384 prefill + 128 generated per chunk); decompose (q2 block-32, randomized SVD rank 256, groups of 128 input columns, spectral norms, residual at 4 bits); oracle at eps 1/3/10% with the sound certification rule, iso-byte control, teacher-forced vs generated split, extrapolation to 60 layers.
metrics: sanity rel_err of W_down_q4 @ ffn_geglu vs captured ffn_out (median)
oracle residual byte fraction at eps 1/3/10% (mean, p90) per layer x matrix x base x phase
certified-skip fraction, certification efficiency, soundness violations, tightness p10/p50/p90, Spearman
iso-byte: uniform q2/q3 error vs base+oracle vs base+certified
implied bytes/token (attention 4.77 GB + head 1.16 GB + FFN) vs 17.64 GB (Q4_0) and 8.5 GB (IQ2_XXS), s/token at 850 MB/s, tok/s at 10 GB/s
experiments.runtime_estimate: act-dump ~20 min (17.65 GB first read through the bind mount + 512 tokens at ~10 tok/s prefill); decompose + oracle ~25-35 min for 4 layers x 3 matrices x 2 bases
experiments.thresholds: Pipeline VALID only if sanity median rel_err < 0.03 and soundness_violations == 0. PROMISING only if at eps 3% the oracle residual fraction <= 25% AND certification efficiency >= 50% AND implied bytes/token < 8.5 GB AND base+oracle error < uniform-quant error at equal bytes; WEAK if fraction <= 50% or efficiency 0.2-0.5; NO_ADVANTAGE if uniform q3 error <= 1.2x the oracle error at equal bytes; NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise. Regardless: report s/token on a Pi (any number > 2 GB/token is < 0.5 tok/s from NVMe) and that attention + head alone (5.9 GB/token) cap the dense model at ~1.7 tok/s even if it were entirely in RAM.

experiments.hypothesis: The Pi scripts are correct before a Pi exists: verdict logic, flag selection, safety refusals, and the native build tree configure on generic Linux.
experiments.procedure: pytest tests/test_feasibility.py tests/test_pi_scripts.py tests/test_catalog.py (fixtures: 4GB+microSD/context-friend-1, 8GB+USB3, 8GB+NVMe, 16GB+NVMe, busy host); bash -n and shellcheck on pi/*.sh and pc/*.sh; `pc/docker_run.sh -- bash pi/00_feasibility.sh` and `-- bash pi/01_tune_os.sh` (dry run) inside the image; pinner integration on a 64 MiB synthetic file in Docker; no command is ever run on context-friend-1.
metrics: verdict table renders for every fixture with the expected codes
pinner locks and verifies the synthetic file
experiments.runtime_estimate: 10 min
experiments.thresholds: PASS: 4 GB + microSD -> NOT_VIABLE (exit 3; exit 4 with the protected services present); 8 GB + USB3 -> STREAM_SLOW or STREAM_OK as computed (asserted against hand arithmetic); 8 GB + NVMe -> STREAM_OK with flags containing -nr; 16 GB -> FITS_MAPPED with -nr -lm mmap+mlock and FITS_REPACKED false; busy -> exit 4; all scripts lint clean. On the real Pi later: pi/03 and pi/05 replace 'assumed' inputs and E4 projections are recomputed.

run_order_today: 0. Orchestrator (10 min): freeze docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md, pigemma/data/catalog.json and the results envelope from this manifest; commit the existing results/ and data/calibration; create results/<date>/.

1. Group 0 in parallel (5 agents, ~45 min): pyproject + paths + results | trace.py | gguf_map.py (run `build` on both real GGUFs immediately: expect 802,897,920 B/token and the verified constants) | catalog.json + prompts + TRACE_FORMAT.md | tests/conftest + synth + tools/CMakeLists + membw.c.

2. Group 1 in parallel (5 agents, ~60 min): LANE A probe.cpp + pc/docker_run.sh build-tools (run `--mode names` on the 26B first, then --smoke trace, commit the golden fixture) | LANE B bench.py and start E0 on the 26B natively right away (E0 gate decides everything downstream) | LANE C cache_sim.py validated on synthetic traces | LANE D h2/decompose.py + a dequant sanity run on one real 31B tensor | LANE E feasibility.py + pi/lib/common.sh + fixtures (E8 tests).

3. Group 2 (~45 min): quality.py (then E2 KLD base for both models runs in the background under the bench lock, serialized after E0) | h2/oracle.py on synthetic acts | pc/trace_collect.sh --quick on the 26B in Docker (E3, ~25 min, bench lock) | pc/pagecache_limit.sh (volume copy can start as soon as E0's repack gate passed and the Docker VM disk check passes) | pi/* scripts.

4. Group 3 (~60 min): desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage spec,quality (E1, E2) natively while E3 finishes in Docker only if free RAM >= 20 GB (bench lock enforces) | pi/00-05 + h2_run.ps1 (E7 act-dump on the 31B in Docker runs after E3 releases the lock; decompose/oracle run natively afterwards, ~35 min).

5. Integration (~60 min): E4 cache_sim + stats -> docs/results/H1_RESULTS.md; E5 pagecache_limit --mem 3,4,5,6,8 then E6 --pin at 5,6 GB (Docker, bench lock); E7 oracle -> docs/results/H2_RESULTS.md; pi/06 + E8 checks.

6. Write-up (~30 min): python -m pigemma.results summarize results/<date> -> docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>.md; README + HYPOTHESES + EXPERIMENT_PLAN + PI_RUNBOOK finalized with MEASURED / PROJECTED / ASSUMED tables, the repack finding with line references, the Pi recommendation (16 GB + NVMe Gen3) and the plain dense-31B statement; commit results JSON + md (traces/npy/logits stay untracked).

Rules: never two model-loading jobs at once (results/.bench.lock + 20 GB free-RAM check, Docker runs included); the 31B-dependent steps (E0-31B, E7 act-dump) are scheduled last in their lanes; every heavy script prints free disk first (D: 32 GB, C: 26 GB); nothing is ever run on context-friend-1.

risks.risk: Repack leakage: any run without `-nr` copies all Q4_0 tensors into CPU_REPACK anonymous memory (verified llama-model.cpp:1849-1870 + llama-model-loader.cpp:1240-1242), so 'streaming' silently becomes a 14 GB anon allocation that OOMs under a cgroup cap or on an 8 GB Pi, and pinned file pages are never read by the inference process.
risks.mitigation: `-nr` (llama-bench `--repack 0`) is the only streaming mode; the hybrid `-ot ...=CPU` is kept purely as a negative control. E0 asserts the 'CPU_Mapped model buffer size' line covers >= 95% of the file with no CPU_REPACK line and private bytes < 1.5 GB before any streaming experiment; pagecache_limit.sh reads memory.events oom_kill and marks runs; feasibility refuses the repack/default mode whenever the anon copy would not fit (FITS_REPACKED false on a 16 GB Pi with Q4_0). Follow-up (not today): a ~30-line llama.cpp patch adding a tensor-name pattern that skips extra bufts would give the true hybrid (repacked attention/head, mapped experts); its hook is create_tensor in llama-model-loader.cpp.

risks.risk: The non-repacked Q4_0 kernels are slower (x86 AVX-512 and especially ARM NEON dotprod vs Q4_0_4x4), so the measured streaming tok/s and the Pi in-RAM ceiling are lower than the repacked desktop numbers suggest.
risks.mitigation: E0 measures the norepack penalty on both models; pi/05 measures default vs norepack on the Pi when it exists; projections use the norepack efficiency (calibration.json) and label the repacked number as the ceiling of a future hybrid patch.

risks.risk: Trace pollution or misread tensors: warmup routes to all experts (llama-graph.cpp:1473); ffn_moe_topk is a strided I32 view; the pre-normalisation `ffn_moe_weights` does not sum to 1 while `ffn_moe_weights_norm` does; ubatch splitting could misalign records.
risks.mitigation: probe sets params.warmup=false, reads with nb[] strides, hooks ffn_moe_weights_norm, asserts tensor type/shape on first sight (exit 4), flushes only after llama_process returns with an equal-column assertion per layer, and the validator rejects != 8 distinct ids, ids >= 128 or weight sums off by > 0.02; `--mode names` runs first and the 72-token golden trace is checked in.

risks.risk: Speculative decoding plumbing: `-md` is rejected by llama-completion/llama-bench; the MoE MTP sidecar loads but never drafts in the server at b11398; DFlash drafts at 28% acceptance and is slower.
risks.mitigation: All speculative measurement goes through llama-server timings (draft_n / draft_n_accepted) with an explicit --spec-type retry and spec_type_effective recorded; inactive drafters are reported as 'inactive' rather than a 1.0x speed-up; the dense +24% seen with llama-cli stays 'unconfirmed' unless the server shows draft_n > 0 with identical greedy output.

risks.risk: Docker Desktop constraints: first reads of 14-18 GB GGUFs through the 9p bind mount take minutes; the VM has 31 GB RAM (both GGUFs cannot be cached at once); the ext4 volume copy for E5 needs ~15 GB on the VM disk whose vhdx grows on C: (26 GB free); cgroup io.stat may be empty and /proc/pid/io read_bytes is not accounted for bind-mount reads; load under a cap triggers a MAP_POPULATE/MADV_WILLNEED storm (llama-mmap.cpp:493-515) through the whole file.
risks.mitigation: -nr in all Docker runs (no 14 GB anon copy); one model job at a time (bench lock); pagecache_limit.sh gates the volume copy on `docker run alpine df` and C: free space and offers `docker builder prune` (20 GB reclaimable) as a human decision, with a bind-mount fallback that records majflt-based lower bounds flagged 'not representative'; bytes/token measured via /proc/self/io read_bytes AND majflt, warm-up tokens excluded so the load storm does not pollute steady-state numbers; the real validation is repeated on the Pi via pi/05 stream-bench and pi/06.

risks.risk: Honesty of projections: Pi memory/storage bandwidth, access latency, OS reserve and the llama.cpp efficiency factor are assumptions until a Pi is measured; the desktop proxy's slow tier is a virtual disk, not NVMe over a Pi's PCIe lane.
risks.mitigation: results envelope forces kind in {measured, projected, assumed} with a non-empty assumptions block for projections; every catalog number carries source:'assumed'/'measured'; projections are recomputed automatically once pi/03 (io_mem.json) and pi/05 (calibration.json) exist; docs carry three-column tables and E5 is described as validating the cache model, not Pi NVMe speed.

risks.risk: The wrong Pi: context-friend-1 (4 GB, microSD, Hailo on the single PCIe lane, production ContextFriend services) must not be touched; the right Pi's RAM/storage are unknown.
risks.mitigation: Every pi/*.sh sources assert_safe_host (hostname deny-list + running-service globs, exit 4 unless PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1), collects facts and requires a passing verdict before download/build/run; 01_tune_os refuses pciex1_gen=3 when a HAT occupies the lane; E8 is fixture-driven and nothing is executed on context-friend-1; the verdict names the recommended configuration (16 GB + NVMe Gen3) with the arithmetic for 8 GB + NVMe streaming.

risks.risk: 16 KiB pages on the Pi kernel and unaligned expert slabs (2,230,272 / 1,115,136 B) mean adjacent experts share pages; RLIMIT_MEMLOCK defaults are tiny; mlock of file pages from a separate process cannot change llama.cpp's own madvise/readahead behaviour.
risks.mitigation: All alignment uses the runtime page size (getconf PAGESIZE / sysconf), hotset merges adjacent ranges and reports page overhead, pinner reports partial locks (exit 2) and the exact ulimit/limits.d fix, 01_tune_os installs memlock unlimited and sets device read_ahead_kb (the lever that actually controls readahead for every mapping); the cross-process MADV_RANDOM idea was dropped.

risks.risk: Disk space: D: 32 GB and C: 26 GB free must hold KLD reference logits (1.61 GB per model at 6 chunks; 20 chunks would be 5.4 GB), optional extra quants (9-13 GB each), traces, acts and the Docker volume growth on C:.
risks.mitigation: KLD chunks default 6 with a 2x free-space gate; extra-quant downloads only with -AllowDownload and a 1.3x gate; traces (~15 MB) and acts (~130 MB) are small; every heavy script prints free disk before writing; large outputs are gitignored.

risks.risk: H2 compute/memory on the desktop: 5376x21504 f32 matrices (462 MB each), randomized SVD and 512-token group products for 4 layers x 3 matrices x 2 bases could exceed the one-hour budget or RAM while benchmarks run.
risks.mitigation: One matrix at a time with explicit frees, f16 residual groups, token batches of 32, torch.svd_lowrank with niter=3, group 128, an ETA printed after the first matrix, refusal above 8 layers/1024 tokens without -Force, -Quick (2 layers, 128 tokens, q2 only), the ffn_out sanity check aborts early on an orientation bug, and the run is serialized behind the bench lock so it never overlaps a model benchmark.

risks.risk: Even a perfect H1 outcome gives only ~3-4 tok/s in RAM on a Pi 5 (2.38 GB RAM traffic per token at ~10 GB/s), and streaming on 8 GB + NVMe is bandwidth-limited to roughly 1.5-2.5 tok/s; the dense 31B is 17.6 GB/token (~22 s/token from NVMe). 'Good speed' on a Pi may not be reachable with this model family.
risks.mitigation: State the arithmetic up front in README/HYPOTHESES with the measured desktop calibration, keep all Pi numbers labelled projected until measured, and list what would change the number (a working high-acceptance drafter, the hybrid repack patch, a lower-bit expert quant with KLD evidence, 16 GB + NVMe Gen3 hardware) so the conclusion is actionable rather than only negative.

risks.risk: Several agents implementing the same formats (C++ probe, Python reader, bash wrappers) drift, or gguf-py offset semantics are misread and shift every byte range.
risks.mitigation: docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md is frozen first; constants are asserted on both sides (magic, header offsets, record_size formula); the C++-produced golden trace is validated by the Python reader in CI; tests/test_gguf_map.py round-trips a GGUFWriter file and the integration test asserts the verified 26B constants (data_offset 15,823,936; unit 3,345,408; experts 12,846,366,720).

grafted_from_other_designs: From design #0: all speculative measurement through llama-server with timings.draft_n / draft_n_accepted, the explicit --spec-type retry and spec_type_effective, and 'speculation active only if draft_n > 0 on every request' (bench.py server-spec, E1).

From design #0: thinking-channel stripping (incl. the leading bare <channel|> seen in real outputs), thinking_chars share, exact_match_vs_plain as the losslessness gate, Hebrew-aware grading (quality.py).

From design #0: the dequant-pipeline sanity check W_down_q4 @ ffn_geglu vs the captured ffn_out before trusting any H2 number (oracle.py); tensor name corrected to ffn_geglu after verifying gemma4's GELU+PAR branch.

From design #0: results/.bench.lock + psutil free-RAM check so parallel agents never co-load two GGUFs; --quick/-Quick and skip-if-result-exists on every driver; WorkingSet vs PrivateBytes split in memory reporting; disk-gated KLD base files with the computed size.
From design #0: stdlib-only Pi Python with fixture facts for the four reference configurations AND the probed context-friend-1; AI-HAT-on-PCIe detection refusing pciex1_gen=3; RAM-scaled build jobs.
From design #2: ffn_moe_weights_norm as the recorded routing weight (gemma4 passes norm_w=true) and the weights-sum invariant in the validator.

From design #2: fixed token-stream replay (tokens.bin, probe --replay with -ub 1) so the Docker proxy processes exactly the simulator's access sequence, and per-token io.csv (read_bytes, majflt, wall_ms, RssAnon/RssFile) as the primary bytes/token measurement.

From design #2: LRU stack-distance histogram -> exact hit-rate curve cross-checked against the simulator to 1e-9; cross-layer predictability (precision@8/16 vs static-top-16 and same-ids baselines, mutual information) to decide whether prefetch is worth building; weighted hit rate; teacher-forced vs generated routing split; probs-based margin stats.

From design #2: H2 controls — iso-byte uniform-quant competitor, bound tightness p10/p50/p90 + Spearman, teacher-forced vs free-running activations, explicit NO_ADVANTAGE / bound-useless outcomes; a sound certification rule (B <= eps*||y_hat||/(1+eps)) replaces the winner's loose tau.

From design #2: pi_config.env single parameter surface, DENY_HOSTS + PROTECTED_SERVICE_GLOBS with the 0/2/3/4 exit-code convention, PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC fixture harness for lib.sh under Git Bash, HF ETag/catalog sha256 verification, udev-persisted read_ahead_kb.

Fixes to the winner from verification: the 'hybrid -ot' streaming mode replaced by -nr (an override to the CPU buft still selects CPU_REPACK; -ot cannot name extra bufts); act-dump now captures ffn_norm + ffn_geglu + ffn_out; compute_tg_in_ram replaced by a desktop-calibrated efficiency times measured/assumed memory bandwidth; --random-rest dropped (cross-process madvise is ineffective); KLD chunks 6 not 20; extra-quant downloads optional; a --quick trace tier (~14k prefill + ~4k generated tokens from the existing calibration corpus) replaces the 55k-token Docker job on the critical path; probe flushes after llama_process returns with per-layer column assertions.
